children.text: Spandakārikā, prathamo niḥṣyandaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Spandakārikā</s>, First Outflow (<s>Prathamo Niḥṣyandaḥ</s>)

children.text: yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyāṃ jagataḥ pralayodayau /
children.translated_text: By whose opening and closing of the eyes, the dissolution and arising of the world [occur] —

children.text: taṃ śakticakravibhavaprabhavaṃ śaṃkaraṃ stumaḥ // VSpk_1.1 //
children.translated_text: We praise that <s>Śaṃkara</s> (the beneficent one), who is the source of the splendor of the wheel of powers. (1.1)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* śam upaśāntāśeṣopatāpaparamānandādvayamayasvacaitanyasphārapratyabhijñāpanasvarūpam anugrahaṃ karoti yas tam imaṃ svasvabhāvaṃ śaṃkaraṃ stumas taṃ viśvotkarṣitvena parāmṛśantas tatkḷptakalpitapramātṛpadanimajjanena samāviśāmaḥ tatsamāveśa eva hi jīvanmuktiphala iha prakaraṇa upadeśyaḥ || VSpkC_1.1:1
children.translated_text: '<s>Śam</s>' means grace (<s>anugraha</s>) whose nature is the recognition of the expansion of one's own consciousness — which is non-dual, of supreme bliss, in which all afflictions have been pacified. He who performs that [grace] — him, this <s>Śaṃkara</s> who is one's own essential nature — we praise; apprehending him as the one who elevates the entire universe, we enter into him by immersing [ourselves] in the station of the knower constituted by him. For it is precisely this absorption into him (<s>tatsamāveśa</s>) that is taught in this treatise as the fruit of liberation while living (<s>jīvanmukti</s>).

children.text: * bahuvacanam anugrahadṛṣṭikaṭākṣitāśeṣānugrāhyābhedaprathanāya || VSpkC_1.1:2
children.translated_text: The plural [in 'we praise'] is for the purpose of manifesting the non-difference [of the teacher] from all those worthy of grace who have been favored by the gracious glance of his grace-bestowing vision.

children.text: * tam ity anena yad asya asāmānyatvam api dhvanitaṃ tat prathayati yasyety ardhena || VSpkC_1.1:3
children.translated_text: By the word 'him' (<s>tam</s>), even the uncommonness of this [<s>Śaṃkara</s>] is suggested — that he makes manifest through the half-verse 'whose' (<s>yasya</s>).

children.text: * iha parameśvaraḥ prakāśātmā mahādevaḥ śabdarāśiparamārthapūrṇāhantāparāmarśasāratvāt sadaivānandaghanasphurattātmakobhayavisargāraṇiparāśaktyātmakapūrṇasvātantryasvarūpas tata eva citsvābhāvyād acalasyāpi śrībhagavataḥ svātantryaśaktir avibhaktāpy aśeṣasargasaṃhārādiparamparāṃ darpaṇanagaravatsvabhittāv eva bhāviyuktyānadhikām apy adhikām iva darśayantī kiṃcic calattātmakadhātvarthānugamāt spanda ity abhihitā tena bhagavān sadāspandatattvasatattvo na tv aspandaḥ yad āhuḥ kecit aspandaṃ paraṃ tattvam iti || VSpkC_1.1:4
children.translated_text: Here, the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), the Great God (<s>Mahādeva</s>), whose nature is luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>) — because his essence is the supreme reflective awareness of full 'I'-consciousness, which is the ultimate meaning of the totality of words (<s>śabdarāśi</s>) — is ever of the nature of a dense mass of bliss (<s>ānandaghana</s>), his essential nature being complete autonomy (<s>pūrṇasvātantrya</s>), consisting of the supreme <s>Śakti</s> (power), which is the fire-churning-stick (<s>araṇi</s>) of the twofold emission (<s>visarga</s>), having the nature of vibrant luminosity (<s>sphurattā</s>). Therefore, even though the Blessed Lord is immovable by the very nature of consciousness, his power of autonomy (<s>svātantrya-śakti</s>), though undivided, displaying on the screen of his own being — like a city in a mirror — the succession of the entire creation and dissolution and the rest, [which is] not additional yet appears as if additional, through the logic of the future [manifestation] — this [power] is designated '<s>spanda</s>' (vibration) because it follows the meaning of the verbal root which has a slightly dynamic character. Therefore the Blessed Lord is ever of the reality of the <s>spanda</s> principle — but he is not without vibration (<s>aspanda</s>), as some say: 'the supreme reality is without vibration.'

children.text: * evaṃ hi śāntasvarūpatvād anīśvaram evaitad bhavet || VSpkC_1.1:5
children.translated_text: For if [it were] thus — of a quiescent nature — it would be nothing other than something devoid of lordship (<s>anīśvara</s>).

children.text: * sphurattāsāraspandaśaktimayaśaṃkarātmakasvasvabhāvapratipādanāyaiva cedaṃ śāstraṃ samucitaspandābhidhānaṃ mahāgurubhir nibaddham || VSpkC_1.1:6
children.translated_text: Indeed, this treatise, fittingly named '<s>Spanda</s>' (Vibration), was composed by the great <s>Guru</s> [<s>Vasugupta</s>] precisely to establish one's own essential nature as consisting of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, who is made of the <s>spanda</s>-power whose essence is vibrant luminosity (<s>sphurattā</s>).

children.text: * etac ca vyaktībhaviṣyati || VSpkC_1.1:7
children.translated_text: And this will become evident [as we proceed].

children.text: * sā caiṣā spandaśaktir garbhīkṛtānantasargasaṃhāraikaghanāhantācamatkārānandarūpā niḥśeṣaśuddhāśuddharūpāmātṛmeyasaṃkocavikāsābhāsanasatattvā sarvopaniṣadupāsyā yugapad evonmeṣanimeṣamayī || VSpkC_1.1:8
children.translated_text: And this <s>spanda</s>-power — whose nature is the delight of the wonder of a dense mass of 'I'-consciousness that has absorbed within itself the infinite [cycles of] creation and dissolution; whose essential reality is the constant manifestation of the contraction and expansion of all pure and impure forms, subjects, and objects — [this power,] worshipped by all the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, simultaneously consists of both opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>) and closing (<s>nimeṣa</s>).

children.text: * tathā hi śivādeḥ kṣityantasyāśeṣasya tattvagrāmasya prāksṛṣṭasya saṃhartṛrūpā yā nimeṣabhūr asāv evodbhaviṣyaddaśāpekṣayā sraṣṭurūponmeṣabhūmis tathā viśvanimeṣabhūś cidghanatonmeṣasārā cidghanatānimajjanabhūmir api viśvonmeṣarūpā || VSpkC_1.1:9
children.translated_text: Thus: that which is the closing-ground (<s>nimeṣa-bhūmi</s>), having the nature of withdrawal, of the entire group of principles from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth that were previously created — that very same [power], from the perspective of its about-to-manifest state, is the opening-ground (<s>unmeṣa-bhūmi</s>), having the nature of creation. Similarly, the closing-ground of the universe, whose essence is the opening of the dense mass of consciousness, is also the ground of immersion in the dense mass of consciousness, [and yet] is of the nature of the opening of the universe.

children.text: * yad āgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: As scripture says:

children.text: * lelihānā sadā devī sadā pūrṇā ca bhāsate || VSpkC_1.1:10
children.translated_text: "The Goddess, ever licking [all things], ever full, shines forth."

children.text: * ūrmir eṣā vibodhābdheḥ śaktir icchātmikā prabhoḥ || VSpkC_1.1:11
children.translated_text: "She is the wave of the ocean of awakening, the power of the Lord whose nature is will (<s>icchā</s>)."

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.1:12
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * śrīmān maheśvaro hi svātantryaśaktyā śivamantramaheśvaramantreśvaramantravijñānākalapralayākalasakalāntāṃ pramātṛbhūmikāṃ tadvedyabhūmikāṃ ca gṛhṇānaḥ pūrvapūrvarūpatāṃ bhittibhūtatayā sthitām apy antaḥsvarūpāvacchādanakrīḍayā nimeṣayann evonmeṣayati uttararūpatām avarohakrameṇa ārohakrameṇa tūttarottararūpatāṃ nimeṣayann eva jñānayoginām unmeṣayati pūrvapūrvarūpatām ata evottaram uttaraṃ pūrvatra pūrvatra saṃkocātmatāṃ jahadvikasitatvenāsāv ābhāsayati pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ tu rūpaṃ yathottaraṃ vikasitatāṃ nimajjayan saṅkucitatvena darśayati || VSpkC_1.1:13
children.translated_text: The glorious Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>), through his power of autonomy (<s>svātantrya-śakti</s>), assuming the ground of knowers ending with <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Mantra-Maheśvara</s>, <s>Mantreśvara</s>, <s>Mantra</s>, <s>Vijñānākala</s>, <s>Pralayākala</s>, and <s>Sakala</s>, and the corresponding grounds of the knowable — even while closing (<s>nimeṣa</s>) the progressively prior forms that exist as the background screen, through the play of concealing his inner essential nature, he simultaneously opens (<s>unmeṣa</s>) the subsequent forms in the order of descent. And in the order of ascent, even while closing the progressively subsequent forms, he opens for the <s>jñāna-yogins</s> (yogins of knowledge) the progressively prior forms. Therefore, each subsequent [form], in relation to each prior [level], shedding its contracted nature, he manifests as expanded. But each prior form, as each subsequent [form] submerges its expanded nature, he displays as contracted.

children.text: * evaṃ ca sarvaṃ sarvamayam eva prathayati kevalaṃ tadavabhāsitasaṃkocamātrata iyaṃ bhedapratipattir iva yad uddalanāyehatya upadeśa ity āstāṃ tāvad etat || VSpkC_1.1:14
children.translated_text: And thus he manifests everything as being made of everything — it is merely by the contraction manifested by that [Lord] that there is this appearance of differentiation. The teaching is intended for the uprooting of that [illusion of differentiation] — but enough of this for now.

children.text: * nīlasukhādyābhāsonmeṣamayy api ca saṃvit pramātrekātmakatatsvarūpanimeṣarūpāvabhātacarapītādyābhāsopasaṃhārarūpā ceti svasaṃvedanasiddhām imāṃ yugapad evonmeṣanimeṣobhayarūpāṃ pratibhāṃ bhagavatīṃ vicinvan tu mahādhiyaḥ saṃsāravicchedāya || VSpkC_1.1:15
children.translated_text: And awareness (<s>saṃvit</s>), though consisting of the opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>) that is the manifestation of blue, pleasure, and the like — is also of the form of closing (<s>nimeṣa</s>), which is its essential nature as one with the subject, [and] of the form of the withdrawal of the appearances of the moving, stationary, and the like that shine forth [as objects]. The person of great intellect who contemplates this awareness — the venerable <s>Pratibhā</s> (creative intuition) that is simultaneously of both forms, opening and closing, and established by self-awareness — [does so] for the purpose of cutting through <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence).

children.text: * ata evonmeṣanimeṣābhyām ityetatpadaṃ nijavṛttau bhaṭṭaśrīkallaṭena saṃkalpamātreṇā ity avibhaktam evecchaśaktirūpatayā vyākhyāyi || VSpkC_1.1:16
children.translated_text: Therefore, the expression 'by the opening and closing' (<s>unmeṣa-nimeṣābhyām</s>) was explained by the revered <s>Bhaṭṭa Śrī Kallaṭa</s> in his own commentary as 'by mere intention' (<s>saṃkalpamātreṇa</s>), interpreting it as undivided, in the form of the power of will (<s>icchā-śakti</s>).

children.text: * saṃgrahakṛtāpi ekacintāprasaktasya yataḥ syād aparodayaḥ || VSpkC_1.1:17
children.translated_text: The author of the <s>Saṃgraha</s> also [says]: 'From one to whom a single thought has attached, the arising of another [thought occurs].'

children.text: * unmeṣaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ svayaṃ tam upalakṣayet || VSpkC_1.1:18
children.translated_text: 'That should be known as <s>unmeṣa</s> (opening); one should observe it oneself.'

children.text: * ity atra prārabdhacintāsaṃharaṇam eva parasvarūpodayahetur unmeṣa ity abhidhāsyate pravṛttacintāsaṃhāraṃ vinā parasvarūpodayābhāvāt || VSpkC_1.1:19
children.translated_text: In that [verse], it will be stated that the withdrawal of the thought that has commenced is the <s>unmeṣa</s> that is the cause of the arising of the supreme nature — since without the withdrawal of the current thought, the arising of the supreme nature does not occur.

children.text: * etac ca tatraiva vitaniṣyāmaḥ || VSpkC_1.1:20
children.translated_text: And we shall elaborate on this in that very context.

children.text: * parāmṛtarasāpāyas tasya yaḥ pratyayodbhavaḥ || VSpkC_1.1:21
children.translated_text: "The arising of a cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>) in one who has lost the relish of the supreme nectar —"

children.text: * tenāsvatantratām eti sa ca tanmātragocaraḥ || VSpkC_1.1:22
children.translated_text: "By that, he comes under the power of non-autonomy; and that [cognition] has only that [limited domain] as its scope."

children.text: * ity atrāpy udayaḥ pralayaparamārtha iti spaṣṭam eva vakṣyate || VSpkC_1.1:23
children.translated_text: In that [verse] too, it will be clearly stated that 'arising' (<s>udaya</s>) has dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) as its ultimate meaning.

children.text: * yadā kṣobhaḥ pralīyeta tadā syāt paramaṃ padam || VSpkC_1.1:24
children.translated_text: "When the agitation subsides, then the supreme state arises."

children.text: * ity atrāpi kṣobhapralayātmā nimeṣaḥ parapadonmeṣarūpa ity api nirūpayiṣyate || VSpkC_1.1:25
children.translated_text: In that [verse] too, it will be demonstrated that the closing (<s>nimeṣa</s>), which has the nature of the dissolution of agitation, is of the form of the opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>) into the supreme state.

children.text: * tad evam ekaivobhayarūpāpi śaktiḥ kadācid unmeṣapradhānatayā vyavahriyate kadācin nimeṣapradhānatayā || VSpkC_1.1:26
children.translated_text: Thus, this one and the same power, though of both forms, is sometimes designated with predominance of opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>), and sometimes with predominance of closing (<s>nimeṣa</s>).

children.text: * tataś ca yasya saṃbandhinyāḥ svarūpanimeṣātmanaḥ kāryonmeṣapradhānāyāḥ śakter hetor jagato viśvasya śivāder dharaṇyantasyodayo 'bhedasāratānimajjanasattvo nānāvaicitryaśālī bhedarūpaḥ sargaḥ svarūponmeṣātmanaś ca bāhyatānimeṣapradhānāyāḥ śakter jagataḥ pralayo 'bhedamayatodayātmā vicitrabhedarūpatāsaṃhāra ita pralayo 'py udayarūpa udayo 'pi ca pralayarūpa iti vyākhyeyam vastutas tu na kiṃcid udeti vyayate vā kevalaṃ spandaśaktir eva bhagavaty akramāpi tathātathābhāsarūpatayā sphuranty udetīva vyayata iva ceti darśayiṣyāmaḥ || VSpkC_1.1:27
children.translated_text: And therefore: of him [<s>Śaṃkara</s>] whose [power] is related [to the world] — from the power that has the nature of the closing of its own form (<s>svarūpa-nimeṣa</s>), predominantly [manifesting as] the opening of effects (<s>kāryonmeṣa</s>) — the arising of the world, i.e. the entirety of [principles] from <s>Śiva</s> to earth, is the creation (<s>sarga</s>), which is of the form of differentiation, rich in varied diversity, whose reality is immersion in non-duality. And from the power that has the nature of the opening of its own form (<s>svarūponmeṣa</s>), predominantly [manifesting as] the closing of externality (<s>bāhyatā-nimeṣa</s>) — the dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) of the world is the withdrawal of the varied forms of differentiation, whose reality is the arising of non-duality. Hence dissolution too is of the nature of arising, and arising too is of the nature of dissolution — this is how it should be interpreted. But in reality, nothing arises or perishes — only the <s>spanda</s>-power of the Blessed [Lord], though beyond sequence, appearing as 'such and such' forms while vibrating, seems to arise and seems to perish — this we shall demonstrate.

children.text: * sthitivilayānu grahāṇāṃ viśiṣṭapralayodayarūpatvān nādhikyam iti pralayodayābhyām eva pañcavidhaṃ pārameśvaryaṃ kṛtyaṃ saṃgṛhītam || VSpkC_1.1:28
children.translated_text: Since maintenance, dissolution, and grace are of the nature of specific forms of dissolution and arising, they are not additional [to those two]. Thus by 'dissolution and arising' alone, the fivefold divine activity (<s>pārameśvarya-kṛtya</s>) is comprehended.

children.text: * nirṇītaṃ caivaṃprāyaṃ mayaiva prathamasūtramātravivaraṇe spandasaṃdohe || VSpkC_1.1:29
children.translated_text: And a treatment of this kind has already been given by me in the <s>Spandasaṃdoha</s>, the exposition of the very first <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: * nanu śrīmanmahārthadṛṣṭyā sṛṣṭyādidevatābhir eva vicitrā jagataḥ pralayodayāḥ saṃpādyante tat katham etad uktaṃ yasyetyādi ityāśaṅkyāha taṃ śakticakravibhavaprabhavām iti || VSpkC_1.1:30
children.translated_text: Now, from the perspective of the revered <s>Mahārtha</s> (Great Meaning) doctrine, the varied dissolutions and arisings of the world are accomplished by the very deities of creation and the rest — then how is it said 'whose' etc.? Anticipating this doubt, he says: 'him, who is the source of the splendor of the wheel of powers.'

children.text: * śaktīnāṃ sṛṣṭiraktādimarīcīdevīnāṃ cakraṃ dvādaśātmā samūhas tasya yo vibhava udyogāvabhāsanacarvaṇavilāpanātmā krīḍāḍambaras tasya prabhavaṃ hetum || VSpkC_1.1:31
children.translated_text: The 'wheel' of powers — of the <s>Marīcī</s> goddesses, including <s>Sṛṣṭi</s> (Creation), <s>Raktā</s> (Passionate), and the rest — is the twelvefold assembly. Its 'splendor' (<s>vibhava</s>), whose nature is impulse, manifestation, relishing, and dissolution — the play and pageantry of that — its 'source' (<s>prabhava</s>) means cause.

children.text: * etā hi devyaḥ śrīmanmanthānabhairavaṃ cakreśvaram āliṅgya sarvadaivajagatsargādikrīḍāṃsaṃpādayantīty āmnāyaḥ || VSpkC_1.1:32
children.translated_text: For these goddesses, embracing the glorious <s>Manthāna-Bhairava</s>, the Lord of the Wheel (<s>Cakreśvara</s>), accomplish at all times the play of the creation of the world and the rest — such is the scriptural tradition.

children.text: * atha ca kasmāt parameśvarasya jagatsargasaṃhārādihetutvam ity āśaṅkāyām etad evottaraṃ śakticakreti || VSpkC_1.1:33
children.translated_text: Now, if the doubt arises: why is the Supreme Lord the cause of the creation and dissolution of the world? — the answer to this is precisely 'the wheel of powers' (<s>śakticakra</s>).

children.text: * yāvaddhi kiṃcid viśvaṃ saṃbhavati tatprakāśamānatvena prakāśamayatvāt svāminaś cātmasaṃsthasya bhāvajātasya bhāsanam || VSpkC_1.1:34
children.translated_text: For whatever universe comes into being, because it shines as the light [of consciousness], it is of the nature of light; and the illumination of the totality of existents that abides within the Self of the Lord —

children.text: * asty eva na vinā tasmād icchāmarśaḥ pravartate || VSpkC_1.1:35
children.translated_text: '[This universe] exists indeed; without him, the reflective awareness of will (<s>icchāmarśa</s>) does not operate.'

children.text: * iti vipaścinniścitanītyā parameśvarasyāntaḥprakāśaikātmyena prakāśamānaṃ sthitaṃ sacchakticakram ity ucyate yataḥ parameśvarasyāgameṣv anantaśaktitvam uddhoṣyate || VSpkC_1.1:36
children.translated_text: Thus, according to the settled doctrine of the wise, the wheel of powers that abides within the Supreme Lord, shining in identity with his inner luminosity, is called 'real' (<s>sat</s>) — because in the scriptures the Supreme Lord's infinite power is proclaimed.

children.text: * tasya śakticakrasyābhāsaparamārthasya viśvasya yo vibhavaḥ parasparasaṃyojanāviyojanāvaicitryam anantaprakāraṃ tasya prabhavaṃ kāraṇam || VSpkC_1.1:37
children.translated_text: Of that wheel of powers — whose ultimate reality is manifestation — of the universe, the 'splendor' (<s>vibhava</s>) is the infinite variety of mutual conjunction and disjunction; its 'source' (<s>prabhava</s>) means cause.

children.text: * sa eva hi bhagavān vijñānadehātmakān svātmaikātmyena sthitān viśvān ābhāsān anyonyaṃ nānāvaicitryeṇa saṃyojayan viyojayaṃś ca viśvodayapralayahetuḥ || VSpkC_1.1:38
children.translated_text: For that <s>Bhagavān</s> (the Lord), having the universe of manifestations established in identity with His own self, whose nature is the body of consciousness (<s>vijñānadeha</s>), by conjoining and disjoining [them] with each other in various modes of diversity, is the cause of the arising and dissolution of the universe. (1.1:38)

children.text: * tad uktaṃ śrībhaṭṭakallaṭena vijñānadehātmakasya śakticakraiśvaryasyotpattihetutvam || VSpkC_1.1:39
children.translated_text: Thus it has been stated by the venerable <s>Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa</s>: that which has the nature of a body of consciousness is the cause of the arising of the sovereignty of the circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>). (1.1:39)

children.text: * ity etad vṛttyakṣarāṇām atra vyākhyādvaye 'py ānurūpyam || VSpkC_1.1:40
children.translated_text: And thus the letters of the <s>vṛtti</s> (gloss) are fitting in both interpretations here. (1.1:40)

children.text: * api ca śaktayo 'sya jagat kṛtsnam || VSpkC_1.1:41
children.translated_text: Moreover: 'His powers are the entire universe.' (1.1:41)

children.text: * ity āgamadṛṣṭyā tasmāc chabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ || VSpkC_1.1:42
children.translated_text: Thus, from the perspective of scripture (<s>āgama</s>): 'Therefore, in the deliberation upon word and meaning, there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>.' (1.1:42)

children.text: * itīhatyasthityā ca jagadātmanaḥ tatkhecaryūrdhvamārgasthaṃ vyoma vāmeśigocaram || VSpkC_1.1:43
children.translated_text: And thus, by the method of established tradition: 'The sky situated on the upper path of <s>Khecarī</s> is the domain of <s>Vāmeśī</s>, belonging to the self of the universe.' (1.1:43)

children.text: * iti rahasyanītyā ca vāmeśvarīkhecarīgocarīdikcarībhūcarī rūpasya mayaiva spandasandohe samyaṅ nirṇītasya aprabuddhadhiyas tv ete svasthitisthaganodyatāḥ || VSpkC_1.1:44
children.translated_text: And by the method of esoteric doctrine: [He whose form is] <s>Vāmeśvarī</s>, <s>Khecarī</s>, <s>Gocarī</s>, <s>Dikcarī</s>, and <s>Bhūcarī</s> — which has been properly determined by me in the <s>Spandasandoha</s> — 'But those of unawakened intellect, intent on concealing their own [true] state...' (1.1:44)

children.text: * ity atrāpi nirṇeṣyamāṇasyaitadvyākhyādvayavyākhyātaśakticakraprapañcabhūtasya ca yataḥ karaṇavargo 'yaṃ || VSpkC_1.1:45
children.translated_text: And here too, of that which is to be determined [later], and which is the expansion of the circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>) explained in both commentaries: 'since this group of instruments (<s>karaṇavarga</s>)...' (1.1:45)

children.text: * iti sthityendriyagrāmātmanaḥ tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ || VSpkC_1.1:46
children.translated_text: Thus, [He whose nature] is the group of faculties and the body, and by that [nature]: '<s>mantras</s> (sacred formulas), having appropriated that power...' (1.1:46)

children.text: * iti nityamantrātmanaḥ śabdarāśisamutthasya śaktivargasya || VSpkC_1.1:47
children.translated_text: Thus, [He whose nature] is the eternal <s>mantra</s>: 'of the group of powers arisen from the aggregate of words (<s>śabdarāśi</s>)...' (1.1:47)

children.text: * iti nītyā brāhmyādidevatāsvabhāvasyaivam āder anantaprakārasyāpi mayaiva spandasandohe vitatya nirṇītasya śakticakrasya yo vibhavo māhātmyaṃ tatra prabhavatīti prabhavaṃ svatantraṃ na tu paśuvat paratantram || VSpkC_1.1:48
children.translated_text: Thus, by the method [showing that He whose] essential nature is the deities <s>Brāhmī</s> and the rest — of the circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>) determined extensively by me in the <s>Spandasandoha</s>, though of infinite varieties — the sovereignty, the greatness, is such that [He] is the source (<s>prabhava</s>), [meaning He is] autonomous and not dependent like a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>). (1.1:48)

children.text: * śakticakrasya raśmipuñjasya yo vibhavo 'ntarmukho vikāsas tataḥ prabhava udayo 'bhivyaktir yasyeti bahuvrīhiṇāntarmukhatatsvarūpanibhālanād ayatnena parameśvarasvarūpapratyabhijñānaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ || VSpkC_1.1:49
children.translated_text: Of the circle of powers — the cluster of rays — the sovereignty is the inward expansion; from that, the source (<s>prabhava</s>) means arising, manifestation — by which [reading it as a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound]: through the inward contemplation of that essential nature, the recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) of the supreme Lord's own nature occurs effortlessly — this is the meaning. (1.1:49)

children.text: * kiṃ ca yasya cidānandaghanasyātmana unmeṣanimeṣābhyāṃ svarūponmīlananimīlanābhyāṃ yad antas tad bahiḥ iti yuktyā jagataḥ śarīrarūpasya tadanuṣaṅgeṇa bāhyasyāpi viśvasya pralayodayau yathāsaṃkhyaṃ majjanonmajjane bhavatas taṃ śakticakravibhavasya parasaṃviddevatāsphārasya prabhavaṃ bhaktibhājām etatsvarūpaprakāśakaṃ śaṃkaraṃ stumaḥ || VSpkC_1.1:50
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of that Self whose nature is a mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānandaghana</s>), through the opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>) and closing (<s>nimeṣa</s>), which are the unfolding and folding of His own nature — by the logic that 'what is within is [also] without' — of the universe in the form of the body, and by extension of the external world as well, dissolution and arising are respectively submersion and emergence. We praise that <s>Śaṃkara</s> — the source of the sovereignty of the circle of powers, the expansion of the supreme consciousness-deity — who manifests this essential nature for those devoted [to Him]. (1.1:50)

children.text: * tathā yasya svātmanaḥ saṃbandhino bahirmukhatāprasararūpād unmeṣāj jagata udayo 'ntarmukhatārūpāc ca nimeṣāt pralayas taṃ viśvasargādikāryunmeṣādisvarūpasaṃviddevīmāhātmyasya hetuṃ śaṃkaraṃ stuma iti yathāsaṃbhavam api yojyam || VSpkC_1.1:51
children.translated_text: Likewise, from the opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>) — which is the outward-directed expansion of His own self — the universe arises; and from the closing (<s>nimeṣa</s>) — which is the inward-directed [contraction] — dissolution [occurs]. We praise that <s>Śaṃkara</s>, who is the cause of the greatness of the consciousness-goddess (<s>saṃviddevī</s>) whose nature is the opening and the rest, manifesting as the creation of the universe and the rest — this should be construed as appropriate. (1.1:51)

children.text: * dehādyāviṣṭo 'pi parameśvaraḥ karaṇonmīlananimīlanābhyāṃ rūpādipañcakamayasya jagataḥ sargarsaṃhārau karoti || VSpkC_1.1:52
children.translated_text: Even though entering (<s>āviṣṭa</s>) bodies and the rest, the supreme Lord, through the opening and closing of the instruments [of perception], brings about the creation and dissolution of the universe consisting of the five [sense-objects] such as form and the rest. (1.1:52)

children.text: * yad uktaṃ rahasyatattvavidā tad evaṃ vyavahāre 'pi prabhur dehādim āviśan || VSpkC_1.1:53
children.translated_text: As stated by the knower of esoteric truth: 'Thus, even in ordinary experience (<s>vyavahāra</s>), the Lord, entering the body and the rest,' (1.1:53)

children.text: * bhāntam evāntararthaugham icchayā bhāsayed bahiḥ || VSpkC_1.1:54
children.translated_text: 'causes the mass of objects shining within to shine outwardly, by [His] will (<s>icchā</s>).' (1.1:54)

children.text: * evaṃvidhārthaparigrahāyāpi yasya svātantryaśaktyā iti tyaktvā yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyām iti nyarūpi guruṇā || VSpkC_1.1:55
children.translated_text: For grasping the meaning of this kind as well, the teacher formulated [the verse] using 'by whose opening and closing' (<s>yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyām</s>), setting aside 'by the power of autonomy' (<s>svātantryaśaktyā</s>). (1.1:55)

children.text: * atra ca śaṃkarastutiḥ samāveśarūpā prāpyatvenābhidheyā śakticakravibhavāt prabhavo yasyeti bahuvrīhiṇā śakticakravikāsas tatprāptāv upāya uktaḥ śakticakravibhavasya parasaṃviddevatāsphārasya bhaktibhājāṃ prabhavaṃ prakāśakam iti tatpuruṣeṇa phalam uktam || VSpkC_1.1:56
children.translated_text: And here the praise of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, which is of the nature of absorption (<s>samāveśa</s>), is to be designated as the goal to be attained. By the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [compound] 'whose source is from the sovereignty of the circle of powers,' the expansion of the circle of powers is stated as the means for attaining that. By the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> [compound] 'the manifestor, for the devotees, of the sovereignty of the circle of powers — the expansion of the supreme consciousness-deity,' the fruit is stated. (1.1:56)

children.text: * yad vakṣyati tataś cakreśvaro bhavet || VSpkC_1.1:57
children.translated_text: As will be stated [later]: 'Then he becomes the lord of the circle [of powers].' (1.1:57)

children.text: * ity abhidheyopāyayor upāyopeyabhāvaḥ saṃbandha ity abhidheyopāya saṃbandhaprayojanāny anenaiva sūtreṇa sūtritāni || VSpkC_1.1:58
children.translated_text: Thus the relation between the subject-matter and the means is that of means and goal; and by this very <s>sūtra</s>, the subject-matter, the means, the relation, and the purpose have all been indicated. (1.1:58)

children.text: * nanv evaṃbhūtaśaṃkarasvarūpasattāyāṃ kiṃ pramāṇaṃ kutaś copādānādihetuṃ vinā jagad asau janayati tasyaivopādānatve mṛtpiṇḍasyeva ghaṭena jagatā tirodhānaṃ kriyeta tirohitātirohitatāyāṃ ca bhagavataḥ svabhāvabhedaḥ syāt punar unmajjane ca hetuścintyo jagadudayeca dveetaprasaṅga ityetāḥ śaṅkā eka prahāreṇāpahartumāha || VSpkC_1.1:59]
children.translated_text: Now, what is the proof for the existence of such a nature of <s>Śaṃkara</s>? And how does He generate the universe without a material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) and the rest? If He Himself is the material cause, then like a clay-lump becoming a pot, He would be concealed by the universe, and in being both concealed and unconcealed, there would be a difference in the Lord's essential nature; and for His re-emergence, a cause would need to be sought, and in the arising of the universe there would be the fallacy of infinite regress — to remove all these doubts with a single stroke, he says: (1.1:59)
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s> commentary:]

children.text: yatra sthitamidaṃ sarvaṃ kāryaṃ yasmāc ca nirgatam /
children.translated_text: That in which all this, [which is] an effect, abides, and from which it has emerged —

children.text: tasyānāvṛtarūpatvān na nirodho'sti kutracit // VSpk_1.2 //
children.translated_text: because Its form is unobstructed, there is no obstruction [of It] anywhere. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.2)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* tasyāsya śaṃkarātmanaḥ prakāśānandaghanasya svasvabhāvasya na kutraciddeśe kāla ākāre vā nirodhaḥ prasaravyāghāto 'sti anāvṛtarūpatvād asthagitasvabhāvatvāt || VSpkC_1.2:1
children.translated_text: Of this [reality] whose nature is <s>Śaṃkara</s>, a mass of luminosity and bliss (<s>prakāśānandaghana</s>), [which is] its own essential nature — there is no obstruction, no impediment to [its] expression, anywhere — neither in [any] place, nor in time, nor in [any] form — because its form is unobstructed, because its essential nature is unconcealed. (1.2:1)

children.text: * ayaṃ bhāvaḥ iha yatkiṃcitprāṇapuryaṣṭakasukhanīlādikaṃ citprakāśasyāvarakaṃ saṃbhāvyate tadyadi na prakāśate na kiṃcit prakāśamānaṃ tu prakāśātmakaśaṃkarasvarūpameveti kiṃ kasya nirodhakaṃ ko vā nirodhārthaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:2
children.translated_text: The purport is this: whatever — vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), pleasure, blue, and so forth — might be supposed to be an obscurer of the light of consciousness (<s>citprakāśa</s>): if it does not appear, it is nothing; but if it does appear, it is itself of the nature of the light that is <s>Śaṃkara</s> — so what could obstruct what, and what is the purpose of obstruction? (1.2:2)

children.text: * etadeva tasyetyetadviśeṣaṇena yatretyādinopapādayati || VSpkC_1.2:3
children.translated_text: He establishes this very point through the qualifier 'of that' (<s>tasya</s>) and through [the words] 'in which' (<s>yatra</s>) and the rest. (1.2:3)

children.text: * yatra yasmiṃścid rūpe svātmani idaṃ mātṛmānameyātmakaṃ sarvaṃ jagatkāryaṃ sthitaṃ yatprakāśena prakāśamānaṃ satsthitiṃ labhate tasya kathaṃ tena nirodhaḥ śakyas tannirodhe hi nirodhakābhimatameva na cakāsyādity āśayaśeṣaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:4
children.translated_text: 'In which' — in a certain form, in His own self — 'all this,' the entire universe-effect, consisting of the knower (<s>mātṛ</s>), the means of knowledge (<s>māna</s>), and the knowable (<s>meya</s>), is 'established' — which, being illuminated by His light, attains actual existence. How could that [which establishes] be obstructed by that [which is established]? For if it were obstructed, that which is supposed to be the obstructer itself would not shine — this is the implied conclusion. (1.2:4)

children.text: * yathoktam /
children.translated_text: As it has been stated:

children.text: * tadātmanaiva tasya syātkathaṃ prāṇena yantraṇā || VSpkC_1.2:5
children.translated_text: 'Since it is of that very nature, how could there be restraint by <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath)?' (1.2:5)

children.text: * ityajaḍapramātṛsiddhau || VSpkC_1.2:6
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi</s> (Establishment of the Non-inert Knower). (1.2:6)

children.text: * nanūtpannasya sthityātmā prakāśe bhavati utpattireva tv asya kuta ityāha yasmāc ca nirgatamiti || VSpkC_1.2:7
children.translated_text: But the light [becomes apparent] for [the universe] that has arisen, in [its] state of abiding — but whence its arising itself? To this he says: 'and from which it has emerged.' (1.2:7)

children.text: * smṛtisvapnasaṃkalpayoginirmāṇadṛṣṭayā citaḥ svānubhavasiddhaṃ jagatkāraṇatvam ujjhitvā apramāṇakam anupapannaṃ ca pradhānaparamāṇvādīnāṃ na tatkalpayituṃ yujyate || VSpkC_1.2:8
children.translated_text: From the perspective of memory, dream, imagination (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), and yogic creation (<s>yoginirmāṇa</s>), the causality of consciousness (<s>cit</s>) for the universe is established through one's own experience. Abandoning that, it is not proper to construct [theories of] <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), and the rest, which are without valid evidence and logically untenable. (1.2:8)

children.text: * kāryapadena cedameva dhvanitaṃ kartuḥ kriyayā niṣpādyaṃ hi kāryamucyate na tu jaḍakāraṇānantarabhāvi jaḍasya kāraṇatvānupapatteḥ īśvarapratyabhijñoktanītyā || VSpkC_1.2:9
children.translated_text: And by the word 'effect' (<s>kārya</s>), this is implied: for what is called an 'effect' is that which is accomplished by an agent through action — not something that merely follows after an insentient cause, since the causality of the insentient is logically untenable, as established in the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s>. (1.2:9)

children.text: * bhaviṣyati caitat || VSpkC_1.2:10
children.translated_text: And this will [also] be [stated later]: (1.2:10)

children.text: * avasthāyugalaṃ cātra kāryakartṛtvaśabditam || VSpkC_1.2:11
children.translated_text: 'And here there is a pair of states designated as effect-hood and agent-hood.' (1.2:11)

children.text: * ityatra /
children.translated_text: In this [verse]: (1.2:12 preamble)

children.text: * sarvaśabdenopādānādinairapekṣyaṃ karturdhvanitam || VSpkC_1.2:12
children.translated_text: By the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>), the agent's independence from material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) and the rest is implied. (1.2:12)

children.text: * na ca kāryaṃ ghaṭādi kartuḥ kumbhakārādeḥ kadācitsvarūpaṃ tirodadhad dṛṣṭam || VSpkC_1.2:13
children.translated_text: And an effect such as a pot is never seen to conceal the essential nature of the agent such as a potter. (1.2:13)

children.text: * nanu nirgatir avasthitasya bhavati tatkimetat kvacid ādāv eva sthitaṃ nānyatra sthitamapitu tatraiva cidātmanītyāha yatra sthitamiti || VSpkC_1.2:14
children.translated_text: Now, emergence belongs to that which [already] abides [somewhere]; so what is this [about]? Originally it was established somewhere, [and then] it was not established elsewhere, but rather [it was established] in that very [reality] whose nature is consciousness (<s>cidātman</s>) — thus he says 'in which it is established.' (1.2:14)

children.text: * āvṛttyā caitadyojyam || VSpkC_1.2:15
children.translated_text: And this should be construed in a circular manner [i.e., the 'yatra' clause should be read twice]. (1.2:15)

children.text: * ayamarthaḥ yadi cidātmani jagadahaṃprakāśābhedena na bhavet tat katham upādānādinirapekṣaṃ tata udiyāt || VSpkC_1.2:16
children.translated_text: The meaning is this: if the universe were not [established] in the consciousness-self in non-difference from the I-luminosity, then how could it arise from that [consciousness] independently of material cause and the rest? (1.2:16)

children.text: * yatastu yathā nyagrodhabījasthaḥ śaktirūpo mahādrumaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since, just as the great tree, in the form of a potency (<s>śakti</s>), abides in the seed of the banyan,

children.text: * tathā hṛdayabījasthaṃ jagad etac carācaram || VSpkC_1.2:17
children.translated_text: so too this universe of the moving and the unmoving abides in the seed of the heart. (1.2:17)

children.text: * ityāmnāyasthityā || VSpkC_1.2:18
children.translated_text: Thus, according to the scriptural tradition (<s>āmnāya</s>). (1.2:18)

children.text: * svāminaścātmasaṃsthasya || VSpkC_1.2:19
children.translated_text: 'And of the lord, [it is] established in [His] own self.' (1.2:19)

children.text: * iti pūrvoktayuktyā ca tatraitad abhedena sphuratsthitaṃ tato 'yaṃ cidātmā bhagavānnijarasāśyānatārūpaṃ jagad unmajjayatīti yujyate || VSpkC_1.2:20
children.translated_text: And by the reasoning previously stated, since this [universe] is established there in non-difference, vibrating [within consciousness], therefore this Lord whose nature is consciousness (<s>cidātmā bhagavān</s>) causes the universe — which is of the form of the relishing delight of His own essence (<s>nijarasāśyānatā</s>) — to emerge. This is logically justified. (1.2:20)

children.text: * evaṃ ca yatra sthitameva sad yasmān nirgatamityatra yojanā jātā || VSpkC_1.2:21
children.translated_text: And thus the construction is achieved: 'that in which it abides, being [already] existent, from which it has emerged.' (1.2:21)

children.text: * ca evārthe bhinnakramaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:22
children.translated_text: The word 'ca' (and) is used in the sense of 'eva' (indeed/certainly), and is displaced in sequence. (1.2:22)

children.text: * nanu yadi tasmāt prakāśavapuṣa idaṃ jagan niryātaṃ tan na pratheta na hi prathābāhyaṃ ca prathate ceti yuktam ityāśaṅkya yasmān nirgatamapi sadyatra sthitam ity āvṛttyā saṃgamanīyam || VSpkC_1.2:23
children.translated_text: Now, if this universe has issued forth from that [reality] whose body is luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>), then it would not manifest [as something separate] — for what is outside of manifestation does not manifest, yet it does manifest — this is correct. Anticipating this [objection], [the verse] is to be construed circularly: 'that from which it has emerged yet in which it [still] abides.' (1.2:23)

children.text: * co 'pyarthe bhinnakramaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:24
children.translated_text: The word 'ca' is used in the sense of 'api' (also/even), and is displaced in sequence. (1.2:24)

children.text: * etaduktaṃ bhavati na prasevakādivākṣoṭādi tat tasmān nirgatamapi tu sa eva bhagavān svasvātantryād anatiriktām apyatiriktāmiva jagadrūpatāṃ svabhittau darpaṇanagaravat prakāśayan sthitaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:25
children.translated_text: What is being said is this: it is not the case that [the world] is like a walnut [produced] from a fig tree, having actually gone out from it; rather, the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>) himself, by his own autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>), remains manifesting upon his own screen (<s>bhitti</s>), like a city in a mirror, the form of the world which, though not different [from him], appears as if different.

children.text: * nanu ca bhavatvevaṃ sargasthityavasthayor jagatāsyāniruddhatvaṃ saṃhārāvasthayā tv abhāvātmanā suṣuptadeśīyayā jagataḥ sambandhinyā kathaṃ naitat tirodhīyate nahi grāhyaṃ jagadvinā grāhakaścidātmā kaścidity āvṛttyaitad evottaraṃ yasmān nirgatamapi sadyatraiva sthitamutpannam api jagatsaṃhārāvasthāyāṃ tadaikātmyenaivāste na tv asyānyaḥ kaściducchedaḥ śūnyarūpastasya vakṣyamāṇayuktyā prakāśaṃ bhittibhūtaṃ vinānupapatterityarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:26
children.translated_text: Now, let it be that in the states of creation (<s>sarga</s>) and maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>), the world is unobstructed; but in the state of dissolution (<s>saṃhāra</s>), which is of the nature of absence and resembles deep sleep — how is the world, connected with that [state], not concealed? For without the world as the apprehensible (<s>grāhya</s>), there is no self (<s>ātman</s>) as an apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>) of any sort — to dispel this [objection], he gives this very answer by repetition: since [the world], even though it has emerged from that [consciousness], remains right there where it arose; even in the state of dissolution, the world exists with identity in that very [consciousness]. There is no other destruction of it in the form of a void (<s>śūnya</s>), since without the light (<s>prakāśa</s>) that serves as the screen (<s>bhitti</s>), [the world] cannot exist, as will be shown by reasoning — this is the meaning.

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrīsvacchandaśāstre /
children.translated_text: As stated in the sacred <s>Svacchandaśāstra</s>:

children.text: * aśūnyaṃ śūnyamityuktaṃ śūnyaṃ cābhāva ucyate /
children.translated_text: 'What is called void (<s>śūnya</s>) is [actually] non-void (<s>aśūnya</s>); and void is said to be absence (<s>abhāva</s>).

children.text: * devyabhāvaḥ sa vijñeyo yatra bhāvāḥ kṣayaṃ gatāḥ || VSpkC_1.2:27
children.translated_text: O Goddess, that [state] is to be known as absence (<s>abhāva</s>) wherein [all] things have perished.'

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.2:28
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * evaṃ sarvaṃ yasya kāryaṃ yatprakāśenaiva prakāśate saṃhṛtamapi ca sadyatprakāśaikātmyena tiṣṭhati na tasya deśakālākārādi kiṃcin nirodhakaṃ yujyate iti vyāpakaṃ nityaṃ viśvaśaktikhacitaṃ svaprakāśamādisiddhaṃ caitattattvamiti nāsya siddhāv ajñātārthaprakāśarūpaṃ pramāṇavarākamupapadyata upayujyate sambhavati vā pratyutaitattattvasiddhyadhīnā pramāṇādiviśvavastusiddhiḥ || VSpkC_1.2:29
children.translated_text: Thus, [this reality] whose entire effect (<s>kārya</s>) shines only by its light (<s>prakāśa</s>), and which, even when dissolved, remains with identity in that light — for such a [reality], no place, time, form, etc. can be an obstruction. Therefore, this reality is all-pervading, eternal, studded with the powers of the universe (<s>viśvaśakti</s>), self-luminous (<s>svaprakāśa</s>), and primordially established (<s>ādisiddha</s>). Therefore, for its establishment, the wretched means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), whose nature is the illumination of previously unknown objects, is neither appropriate, useful, nor possible. On the contrary, the establishment of all things in the universe, including <s>pramāṇas</s>, depends on the establishment of this reality.

children.text: * taduktamasmadgurubhis tantrāloke /
children.translated_text: As stated by our teacher (<s>guru</s>) in the <s>Tantrāloka</s>:

children.text: * pramāṇānyapi vastūnāṃ jīvitaṃ yāni tanvate /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) that extend the life of things —

children.text: * teṣāmapi paro jīvaḥ sa eva parameśvaraḥ || VSpkC_1.2:30
children.translated_text: even for them, the supreme life is He alone, the <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord).'

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.2:31
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * yasmān nirgatamapīdaṃ jagadyatra sthitaṃ yatprakāśena prakāśamānaṃ tathābhūtamapi yatra sthitaṃ yatprakāśaikarūpaṃ yatprakāśa eva yasya siddhyai nyakṣeṇekṣyamāṇaṃ bhavati na tv anyaj jagan nāma kiṃcit || VSpkC_1.2:32
children.translated_text: Since [the world], though having emerged from that [consciousness], remains in that [consciousness], manifesting by that light; being of such nature, it also remains in that [consciousness], being of the form of that light alone; for the establishment of that light, [the world] being directly perceived — there is nothing else whatsoever called 'world.'

children.text: * atra yatra sthitamityāvartya dvir yojyam || VSpkC_1.2:33
children.translated_text: Here, the phrase 'remains in which' (<s>yatra sthitam</s>) is to be supplied a second time by repetition.

children.text: * evaṃ ca svānubhavasiddhamevāsya tattvasya sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāramelanāvabhāsino 'tidurghaṭakāriṇaḥ sarvadā sarvatrāniruddhatvam || VSpkC_1.2:34
children.translated_text: And thus, the unrestricted nature (<s>aniruddhatva</s>) — always and everywhere — of this reality, which is established by one's own experience (<s>svānubhava</s>), which manifests creation, maintenance, dissolution, and absorption (<s>melana</s>), and which accomplishes the extremely difficult (<s>atidurghaṭakārin</s>).

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrīmadutpaladevācāryaiḥ /
children.translated_text: As stated by the revered master <s>Utpaladeva</s>:

children.text: * parameśvaratā jayatyapūrvā tava sarveśa yadīśitavyaśūnyā /
children.translated_text: 'Victorious is your unprecedented Supreme Lordship (<s>parameśvaratā</s>), O Lord of all, for it is devoid of anything to be ruled over;

children.text: * aparāpi tathaiva te yayedaṃ jagadābhāti yathā tathā na bhāti || VSpkC_1.2:35
children.translated_text: and yet another [power] of yours, by which this world appears just as [it does], and [yet] does not [truly] appear.'

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.2:36
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * atrahibhāsamānameva jagad bhāsanaikaśeṣībhūtatvād bhāsanātiriktaṃ na kiṃcidbhātītyarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:37
children.translated_text: Here, the world being manifest itself — since manifestation (<s>bhāsana</s>) alone remains as the residue — nothing other than manifestation shines: this is the meaning.

children.text: * kiṃca yatra sthitam ityuktyopaśamapade yasmāc ca nirgatamiti prasarapade yato'sya na nirodhas tato nimīlanonmīlanasamādhidvaye'pi yoginā svasvabhāvasamāveśapareṇaiva bhavitavyam || VSpkC_1.2:38
children.translated_text: Moreover, by the statement 'in which it remains' — in the mode of repose (<s>upaśama</s>) — and 'from which it has emerged' — in the mode of expansion (<s>prasara</s>) — since there is no obstruction of this [reality], therefore, in both types of <s>samādhi</s> — <s>nimīlana</s> (inward-closing) and <s>unmīlana</s> (outward-opening) — the <s>yogin</s> must be absorbed in the entry into his own essential nature (<s>svasvabhāva-samāveśa</s>).

children.text: * yadvakṣyate /
children.translated_text: As will be stated:

children.text: * yadā kṣobhaḥ pralīyeta tadā syātparamaṃ padam || VSpkC_1.2:39
children.translated_text: 'When the agitation (<s>kṣobha</s>) dissolves, then the supreme state (<s>paramaṃ padam</s>) arises.'

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.2:40
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * tathā /
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: * tasmāc chabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:41
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, in the contemplation of word and meaning, there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>.'

children.text: * ityapi ca || VSpkC_1.2:42
children.translated_text: And so on.

children.text: * kutracidanātmavādini saugatādau pramātari kutracic ca bādhakābhimate pramāṇe sati na tasya nirodhaḥ pratiṣedho'sti yato yastasya pratiṣedhako yac ca tasya pratiṣedhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ tadyadi na siddham abhittikam etac citraṃ siddhiścāsya prakāśate iti tatsiddhyaiva bhagavānādisiddhasvaprakāśamūrtir astīty etat pratiṣedhāyoditenāpy anakṣaramuktam || VSpkC_1.2:43
children.translated_text: Even when some denier of the self (<s>anātmavādin</s>), such as a Buddhist, serves as the knowing subject (<s>pramātṛ</s>), and when there is some <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) considered as invalidating [this reality] — even then, there is no negation or refutation of it. Because, whatever would refute it, and whatever <s>pramāṇa</s> would refute it — if that [<s>pramāṇa</s>] is not established, then this picture [of negation] is without a wall; and its very establishment shines as light (<s>prakāśa</s>). Therefore, by the very establishment [of the <s>pramāṇa</s>], the Lord, whose form is primordially established self-luminous light, exists — this is said wordlessly (<s>anakṣaram</s>) even by what is raised for the sake of refutation.

children.text: * bhaviṣyati caitat /
children.translated_text: And this will be [discussed in the verse]:

children.text: * na tu yo 'ntarmukho bhāvaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:44
children.translated_text: 'But that which is the inward-turned state (<s>antarmukha bhāva</s>)...'

children.text: * ityatrāntare || VSpkC_1.2:45
children.translated_text: — in that context.

children.text: * evaṃ cānena viśvottīrṇaṃ viśvamayaṃ viśvasargasaṃhārādikāri śāṃkaraṃ svasvabhāvātmakaṃ tattvam ityabhidadhatā sarveṣu pārameśvareṣu yadupāsyaṃ taditaḥ spandatattvān nādhikaṃ kevalametatsvātantryavaśenaiva tadupāsāvaicitryam ābhāsyate || VSpkC_1.2:46
children.translated_text: And thus, by this [verse] which declares a reality (<s>tattva</s>) that transcends the universe (<s>viśvottīrṇa</s>), constitutes the universe (<s>viśvamaya</s>), performs the creation, dissolution, etc. of the universe, is of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> (<s>śāṃkara</s>), and is one's own essential nature (<s>svasvabhāvātmaka</s>) — [it is established that] among all the <s>Pārameśvara</s> [doctrines], what is to be worshipped is not greater than this <s>Spanda</s> reality; only by the autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>) of this [reality] is the variety of worship manifested.

children.text: * vastutastu etadvīryasāram evāśeṣam || VSpkC_1.2:47
children.translated_text: In reality, however, everything is nothing but the essence of the power (<s>vīryasāra</s>) of this [<s>Spanda</s> reality].

children.text: * yadvakṣyati /
children.translated_text: As will be stated:

children.text: * tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ sarvajñabalaśālinaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:48
children.translated_text: 'Taking resort to that power, <s>mantras</s> become endowed with the power of omniscience (<s>sarvajñabala</s>).'

children.text: * ityetadapi bhaṅgyā pratipāditam || VSpkC_1.2:49
children.translated_text: This too has been indicated in an indirect manner.

children.text: * evaṃ ca na kaścid uktacodyāvakāśaḥ || VSpkC_1.2:50
children.translated_text: And thus, there is no room for any of the stated objections.

children.text: * evametādṛśeṣu cintāratnaprāyeṣu śrīspandasūtreṣu yadanyaiḥ sarvair vivṛtikṛdbhir vyākhyāyi yac cāsmābhiḥ kiṃcid vyākriyate tatrāntaramamatsarā anavaliptāś ca svayameva vicinvantu sacetaso na tu tad asmābhir udghāṭya pratipadaṃ pradarśyate granthagauravāpatteḥ || VSpkC_1.2:51
children.translated_text: In these jewel-like <s>Spanda Sūtras</s>, whatever has been commented upon by all other commentators, and whatever little we comment on — let the discerning, free from jealousy and without conceit, examine the difference for themselves. We do not lay it bare and show it word by word, lest the work become unduly voluminous.

children.text: * nanu jāgarādidaśasv īdṛśaḥ svabhāvo nānubhūyate yadi cāyamuktayuktibhirna kenacit nirudhyate tat jāgarādyavasthā svayameva nirotsyate iti śaṅkāta uktamapyartham apratipadyamānaṃ pratibodhayann upadiśati || VSpkC_1.2:52]
children.translated_text: [Objection:] In the states of waking, etc., such an essential nature is not experienced. And if this [reality] cannot be obstructed by anything, as stated by the reasoning given, then the states of waking, etc. would themselves cease. To one who does not understand the already stated meaning due to this apprehension, he instructs, making [the point] clear:
[<s>Spandakārikā-nirṇaya</s>]

children.text: jāgradādivibhede'pi tadabhinne prasarpati /
children.translated_text: In the differentiation of waking and the other [states], though that [<s>Spanda</s> principle] extends [through them] as undifferentiated,

children.text: nivartate nijān naiva svabhāvādupalabdhṛtaḥ // VSpk_1.3 //
children.translated_text: it never turns away from its own nature as the perceiving subject (<s>upalabdhṛ</s>). (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.3)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* jāgarāparaparyāyo jāgracchabdaḥ śiṣṭaprayuktatvāt || VSpkC_1.3:1
children.translated_text: The word '<s>jāgrat</s>' (waking) is a synonym for '<s>jāgarā</s>' — since it is established in learned usage.

children.text: * lokaprasiddhe jāgratsvapnasuṣuptānāṃ bhede yogiprasiddhe 'pi vā dhāraṇādhyānasamādhirūpe prasarpati anyānyarūpe pravahati sati arthāt tattattvaṃ nijādanapāyinaḥ sarvasyātmabhūtāc cānubhavitṛrūpāt svabhāvān naiva nivartate || VSpkC_1.3:2
children.translated_text: When in the commonly known differentiation of waking, dream, and deep sleep, or in the differentiation known to <s>yogins</s> — in the form of <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) — [the <s>Spanda</s> principle] extends, i.e., flows in various forms, its reality (<s>tattva</s>) does not turn away from its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), which is inseparable from it and which is the form of the perceiver (<s>upalabdhṛ</s>) — the very self of all.

children.text: * yadihisvayaṃnivarteta taj jāgradādy api tatprakāśavinākṛtaṃ na kiṃcitprakāśeta || VSpkC_1.3:3
children.translated_text: For if it were to turn away of its own accord, then even waking, etc., deprived of its light (<s>prakāśa</s>), would not appear at all.

children.text: * upalabdhṛtā caitadīyā jāgarāsvapnayoḥ sarvasya svasaṃvedanasiddhā sauṣupte yadyapi sā tathā na cetyate tathāpy auttarakālikasmṛtyanyathānupapattyā siddhā upalabdhṛta eva ca svabhāvān na nivartate upalabhyaṃ tv avasthādi tanmāhātmyān nivartatāṃ kāmaṃ kātra kṣatiḥ || VSpkC_1.3:4
children.translated_text: And the nature of being a perceiver (<s>upalabdhṛtā</s>) of this [<s>Spanda</s> principle] is established through self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) in the states of waking and dream. Even though in deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>) it is not cognized as such, it is established through subsequent memory (<s>smṛti</s>), which would otherwise be inexplicable. It is from the nature of being a perceiver that [the principle] does not turn away. But let that which is perceived — states and so forth — turn away by its greatness, as it will. What harm is there in that?

children.text: * evakāro'pyarthe bhinnakramas tadabhāve'pi na nivartata ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.3:5
children.translated_text: The particle '<s>eva</s>' has the sense of '<s>api</s>' (even), with a different sequence; [the meaning is]: even in the absence of that [differentiation], [the <s>Spanda</s> principle] does not turn away — this is the meaning.

children.text: * jāgarādivibhedasya viśeṣaṇadvāreṇa hetustadabhinne iti tasmāc chivasvabhāvādabhedena prakāśamānatvāt prakāśarūpe ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.3:6
children.translated_text: The differentiation of waking, etc., serves as the reason through the qualifying expression 'in that which is undifferentiated' (<s>tadabhinna</s>) — therefore, because of manifesting without difference from the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, 'of the nature of light (<s>prakāśa</s>)' — this is the meaning.

children.text: * yac ca yadekātmakaṃ tatkathaṃ tannivṛttāv avatiṣṭhate || VSpkC_1.3:7
children.translated_text: And that which is of the nature of one thing — how does it persist when that [thing] ceases?

children.text: * yadvā taditi kartṛpadam || VSpkC_1.3:8
children.translated_text: Alternatively, '<s>tat</s>' (that) is the subject (<s>kartṛpada</s>).

children.text: * abhinna iti tu kevalamabhinnatvaṃ jāgarādeḥ śivāpekṣameva || VSpkC_1.3:9
children.translated_text: 'Undifferentiated' (<s>abhinna</s>) — the non-difference of waking, etc. is only with reference to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: * arthāttattattvaṃ jāgarādibhede'pi sati prasarpati prasarati vaicitryaṃ gṛhṇāti tan naiva svabhāvān nivartata iti yojyam || VSpkC_1.3:10
children.translated_text: Implicitly, that reality (<s>tattva</s>), even when the differentiation of waking, etc. exists, extends, expands, takes on variety, yet does not turn away from its own nature — thus it should be construed.

children.text: * kiṃcāyaṃ jāgradādibhedaḥ pariṇāmo vivarto veti yat sāṃkhyapāñcarātraśābdikādayo manyante tadvyudāsāyāpyuktaṃ tadabhinna iti || VSpkC_1.3:11
children.translated_text: Moreover, this differentiation of waking, etc. — whether it is a [real] transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) or an [apparent] manifestation (<s>vivarta</s>) — in order to refute what the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, <s>Pāñcarātras</s>, Grammarians, and others maintain, it is also said 'in that which is undifferentiated.'

children.text: * avasthāprapañco'pi yadi cinmātrāt manāgapy atiricyeta cidrūpaṃ vā tatpariṇatau manāg atiricyeta tan na kiṃcic ca kā syād iti tāvan na pariṇāmo'sti || VSpkC_1.3:12
children.translated_text: If the elaboration of states were to differ even slightly from pure consciousness (<s>cinmātra</s>), or if the nature of consciousness (<s>cidrūpa</s>) were to differ even slightly in its transformation — then [both] would be nothing. What would remain? Therefore, there is no [real] transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>).

children.text: * yathoktam /
children.translated_text: As stated:

children.text: * pariṇāmo'cetanasya cetanasya na yujyate || VSpkC_1.3:13
children.translated_text: 'Transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) does not befit the conscious; [nor] of the unconscious [is it possible].'

children.text: * iti śrīkiraṇe || VSpkC_1.3:14
children.translated_text: — in the sacred <s>Kiraṇa</s> [<s>Āgama</s>].

children.text: * na ca bhāsamāno 'sāv asatyo brahmatattvasyāpi tathātvāpatteḥ ity asatyavibhaktānyarūpopagrāhitā vivarta ityapi na saṃgatam || VSpkC_1.3:15
children.translated_text: Nor is that [world], while being manifest, unreal — since the absurd consequence of the same [unreality] applying to the <s>Brahman</s> reality would follow. Therefore, <s>vivarta</s> (apparent transformation) — which is grasped as a form different from the unreal yet not distinct [from <s>Brahman</s>] — is also not tenable.

children.text: * anena cātidurghaṭakiratvam eva bhagavato dhvanitam || VSpkC_1.3:16
children.translated_text: And by this, the extremely-difficult-to-accomplish nature (<s>atidurghaṭakāritva</s>) of the Lord is intimated.

children.text: * yasmāj jāgarādivibhedaṃ ca prakāśayati tatraiva ca svābhedamiti bhedātmanā tadabhedātmanobhayātmanā ca rūpeṇāparāparāparāparāśaktitrayasvarūpeṇa sphuratīty anuttaraṣaḍardhatattvātmatayā bhagavān eva sphurati || VSpkC_1.3:17
children.translated_text: Because [the Lord] illuminates the distinctions of waking and other [states], and also [reveals] His own non-difference therein — He pulsates in the form of difference, non-difference, and both, through the essential nature of the triad of <s>parā</s>, <s>parāparā</s>, and <s>aparā</s> powers — thus the Blessed Lord alone pulsates as identical with the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> of the <s>Anuttara</s> system.

children.text: * ataścajāgarādidaśāvasthito 'pi evamimaṃ svasvabhāvaṃ pariśīlayan yaścinute sa śaṃkara evetyupadiṣṭaṃ bhavati || VSpkC_1.3:18
children.translated_text: Therefore, even one situated in the states of waking and so forth, who thus cultivates this own essential nature — it is taught that he is <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) Himself.

children.text: * atha ye ekamevedaṃ saṃvidrūpaṃ harṣaviṣādādyanekākāravivartaṃ paśyāma ityuktyā jñānasaṃtāna eva tattvamiti saugatā manyante ye cāhaṃpratītipratyeyaḥ sadaiva sukhādyupadhitiraskṛta ātmeti mīmāṃsakāḥ pratipannās tānekenaiva ślokenāpavadati || VSpkC_1.3:19]
children.translated_text: Now, those who say 'we see this single consciousness-nature as transforming into many forms such as joy, sorrow, and so forth' — i.e., the Buddhists (<s>Saugatās</s>) who hold that the continuum of cognition alone is reality — and those <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> who have accepted that 'the self, which is the object of I-consciousness, is always obscured by conditions such as pleasure' — he refutes both of them with a single verse:
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>]

children.text: ahaṃ sukhī ca duḥkhī ca raktaścetyādisaṃvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I am happy,' 'I am miserable,' 'I am attached' — such cognitions,

children.text: sukhādyavasthānusyūte vartante 'nyatra tāḥ sphuṭam // VSpk_1.4 //
children.translated_text: pervaded by states of pleasure and the like, these clearly exist elsewhere. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.4)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* ya evāhaṃ sukhī sa eva duḥkhī sukhānuśāyinā rāgeṇa yuktatvād rakto duḥkhānuśāyinā dveṣeṇa sambandhād dviṣṭetyādayaḥ saṃvido jñānāni tā anyatreti avasthātary ātmatattve vartante tatraivāntarmukhe viśrāmyanti sphuṭaṃ svasākṣikaṃ kṛtvā || VSpkC_1.4:1
children.translated_text: The very same 'I' that is happy is also miserable; being endowed with desire (<s>rāga</s>), which follows upon pleasure, he is attached; being connected with aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), which follows upon pain, he hates — and so forth. These <s>saṃvids</s> (cognitions), these experiences, 'elsewhere' means in the self-principle, the experiential subject — they rest there, reposing inwardly, making their own witness manifest.

children.text: * anyathā kṣaṇikajñānānāṃ svātmamātrakṣīṇatvāt tatsaṃskārajanmanām api vikalpānāmanubhavāgocare pravṛttyabhāvādanusaṃdhānam idaṃ na ghaṭeta || VSpkC_1.4:2
children.translated_text: Otherwise, since momentary cognitions perish within their own moment, and since even the conceptual constructs (<s>vikalpas</s>) born from their impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) have no operation in the domain of experience, this recognition and retrospection would not be possible.

children.text: * cakārās tulyayogitāparā anusaṃdhānaṃ dyotayanti || VSpkC_1.4:3
children.translated_text: The particles 'ca' (and) signify equal applicability and indicate [the act of] recognition.

children.text: * kīdṛśe'nyatra sukhādyavasthā udayapralayinyo 'nusyūtā dṛbdhā yasmiṃs tasmin sukhādyavasthānusyūte 'ntaḥsraksūtrakalpatayā sthite || VSpkC_1.4:4
children.translated_text: In what kind of 'elsewhere'? That which is pervaded by the states of pleasure and the like — in which the states of pleasure and the like, which arise and dissolve, are strung through like an inner thread of a garland, remaining steadily — in that [self] which is pervaded by the states of pleasure and the like.

children.text: * tā ity anenānusaṃdhīyamānāvasthānāṃ smaryamāṇatām abhidadhatkṣaṇikajñānavādimate 'nubhavasaṃskārotpannatvād arthākārārūṣitatve 'pi smṛteḥ kāmam anubhavasadṛśatvaṃ bhavatu na tv anubhavānubhūtātītakālārthavyavasthāpakatvaṃ ghaṭate sarvasaṃvidantarmukhe tu pramātari sati sarvaṃ yujyata iti sūcitavān ity alaṃ sukumārahṛdayopadeśyajanavairasyadāyinībhir ābhiḥ kathābhiḥ || VSpkC_1.4:5
children.translated_text: By the word 'tāḥ' (those), indicating that the states being recognized are being remembered, he points out to those holding the doctrine of momentary cognition: even though memory, being tinted with the form of the object, may have similarity to direct experience due to arising from the <s>saṃskāra</s> of experience, it does not succeed in establishing the pastness of the object experienced in direct experience. But when there is a cognizer turned inward who is the inner [ground] of all cognitions, everything is consistent — thus he has indicated. Enough of these discussions that breed hostility in those gentle-hearted persons who are [proper] recipients of instruction.

children.text: * etadarthibhiḥ pratyabhijñā parīkṣyā || VSpkC_1.4:6
children.translated_text: Those who desire this [understanding] should examine the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> [texts].

children.text: * granthakṛtaiva tu yata iha yuktir āsūtritā tato'smābhiḥ kiṃcid udghāṭitam iti sacetobhir nāsmabhyam asūyayitavyam || VSpkC_1.4:7
children.translated_text: But since the reasoning hinted at here was composed by the author of the text himself, we have merely elucidated it somewhat — therefore the discerning should not bear ill-will toward us.

children.text: * mīmāṃsakaparihārāya tu etad itthaṃ vyākhyātavyam || VSpkC_1.4:8
children.translated_text: But for refuting the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> position, this should be explained thus:

children.text: * ahaṃ sukhītyādisaṃvido yās tā anyatreti puryaṣṭakasvarūpe pramātari sukhādyavasthābhir anusyūte otaprotarūpe sphuṭaṃ lokapratītisākṣikaṃ vartante tiṣṭhanti na tv asmadabhyupagate 'smiṃś cidānandaghane śaṃkarātmani svasvabhāve iti na sarvadā sukhādyupādhitiraskṛto 'yamātmāpi tu cinmayaḥ || VSpkC_1.4:9
children.translated_text: The cognitions 'I am happy' and so forth — those — 'elsewhere,' i.e., they exist and rest in the knowing subject whose nature is the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), which is in the form of being woven through by states of pleasure and the like. [They do] not [rest] in what we accept — in the <s>Śaṅkara-ātman</s>, one's own essential nature, which is a solid mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānandaghana</s>). Thus the self is not always obscured by conditions such as pleasure; rather, it is of the nature of consciousness.

children.text: * yadā tu nijāśuddhayā vakṣyamāṇayāyaṃ svasvarūpaṃ gūhayitvā tiṣṭhati tadā puryaṣṭakādyavasthāyāṃ sukhitvādirūpatāsya tatrāpi na nirodhas taiḥ sukhādibhir asyety uktam eveti na tattiraskṛto 'yaṃ kadācidapi || VSpkC_1.4:10
children.translated_text: But when, through his own impurity that will be described [later], he conceals his own essential nature and remains [thus], then in the state of the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>) and the like, he has the nature of being happy and so forth. But even there, there is no suppression of him by those pleasures and the like — as has been stated. Thus he is never obscured by those [states].

children.text: * ahaṃ kṛśo 'haṃ sthūla ityādipratītiparihāreṇa ahaṃ sukhī duḥkhītyādi vadato 'yamāśayaḥ sukhitvādipratītisaṃbhinnāṃ puryaṣṭakabhūmim antarmukhe pade nimajjayaṃs tadanuṣaṅgeṇa bāhyasyāpi dehaghaṭāder galanāt pratyabhijānāty eva svaṃ śivasvabhāvatvam iti sarvathā puryaṣṭakaśamanāyaiva yatna āstheya iti || VSpkC_1.4:11
children.translated_text: By setting aside cognitions like 'I am thin, I am stout,' and speaking of 'I am happy, I am miserable' and so forth, the intention is this: submerging the plane of the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), which is mixed with cognitions of being happy and so forth, into the inward-turned ground, and through that connection, even the external body, pot, and the like dissolve — and [thus] one recognizes one's own <s>Śiva</s>-nature. Therefore, effort should be directed solely toward the pacification of the subtle body.

children.text: * uktopapattisiddhāṃ samastavādānām anupapannatām anuvadann upapattisiddhaṃ spandatattvam evāstīti pratijānāti yuktyanubhavāgamajño rahasyagurupravaraḥ || VSpkC_1.4:12]
children.translated_text: Reiterating the inconsistency of all doctrines established by the reasoning stated [above], and asserting that the <s>spanda</s>-principle alone, established by reasoning, exists — [speaks] the supreme secret teacher who knows reasoning, experience, and scripture.
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>]

children.text: na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ yatra na grāhyaṃ grāhakaṃ na ca /
children.translated_text: Where there is neither pain nor pleasure, neither graspable nor grasper,

children.text: na cāsti mūḍhabhāvo'pi tadasti paramārthataḥ // VSpk_1.5 //
children.translated_text: nor even the state of delusion — that exists in the highest sense. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.5)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* iha yatkiṃcidduḥkhasukhādyāntaraṃ nīlapītādikaṃ bāhyaṃ grāhyaṃ yac caitad grāhakaṃ puryaṣṭakaśarīrendriyādi tattāvatsauṣuptavad asaṃcetyamānaṃ sphuṭameva nāstīti vaktuṃ śakyam || VSpkC_1.5:1
children.translated_text: Here, whatever internal [phenomena] like pain, pleasure, and so forth, and whatever external [phenomena] like blue, yellow, and so forth constitute the graspable (<s>grāhya</s>), and whatever grasps these — the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), the gross body, the sense organs, and so forth — when [all of] that is not apprehended, as in deep sleep, one can clearly say that it does not exist.

children.text: * yadāpi tu saṃcetyate tadā saṃcetyamānasyāpy asya caitanyamayatvāc caitanyam evāstīty āyātam || VSpkC_1.5:2
children.translated_text: But when it is apprehended, then even of this which is being apprehended, since it is of the nature of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>), [the conclusion] comes that consciousness alone exists.

children.text: * yadāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: As they say:

children.text: * prakāśātmā prakāśyo 'rthe nāprakāśaś ca sidhyati || VSpkC_1.5:3
children.translated_text: What illuminates is of the nature of light; and the illuminated object cannot exist as non-illumination.

children.text: * iti rahasyatattvavido'smatparameṣṭhinaḥ śrīmadutpaladevapādāḥ śrīmadīśvarapratyabhijñāyām || VSpkC_1.5:4
children.translated_text: Thus [say] the revered <s>Utpaladeva</s>, our supreme teacher who knows the secret reality, in the revered <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s>.

children.text: * ihāpi vakṣyate /
children.translated_text: Here too it will be said:

children.text: * tatsaṃvedanarūpeṇa tādātmyapratipattitaḥ || VSpkC_1.5:5
children.translated_text: Through the recognition of identity in the form of its being experienced...

children.text: * ityato duḥkhasukhādi nīlādi tadgrāhakaṃ ca yatra nāsti tatprakāśaikaghanaṃ tattvamasti || VSpkC_1.5:6
children.translated_text: Therefore, that reality which is a solid mass of pure illumination — where neither pain, pleasure, and the like, nor blue and the like, nor their grasper exists — that exists.

children.text: * nanvevaṃ sarvagrāhyagrāhakocchede śūnyātmaiva tattvamityāyātaṃ netyāha na cāsti mūḍhabhāvo 'pi iti || VSpkC_1.5:7
children.translated_text: Objection: Thus, with the elimination of all graspable and grasper, the reality turns out to be of the nature of void! No, he says — 'nor even the state of delusion.'

children.text: * mūḍhabhāvo mūḍhatvaṃ śūnyarūpatāpi yatra nāsti so 'pi hi na prathate kathamasti prathate cet tarhi prathātmakatvān nāsau kaścit prathaivāsti na ca prathāyāḥ kadācidbhāvo bhavati tadabhāve prathābhāvasyāpyasiddheḥ || VSpkC_1.5:8
children.translated_text: The state of delusion, i.e., the nature of void — where even that does not exist. For that [void] too, if it does not manifest, how can it exist? And if it does manifest, then since it is of the nature of manifestation, it is not some [separate thing] — manifestation alone exists. And manifestation can never be non-existent, because in its absence, the non-existence of manifestation itself would be unestablished.

children.text: * bhaviṣyati caitat /
children.translated_text: And this will be [stated]:

children.text: * na tu yo 'ntarmukho bhāvaḥ || VSpkC_1.5:9
children.translated_text: 'But that which is the inward-turned state...'

children.text: * ityatra || VSpkC_1.5:10
children.translated_text: in that [passage].

children.text: * api ca mūḍhabhāva aiśvaryātmakavimarśaśūnyaprakāśamātratattvo brahmarūpo 'pi yatra nāsti yac chrutyantavidaḥ pratipannāḥ vijñānaṃ brahma iti tasyāpi svātantryātmakaspandaśaktiṃ vinā jaḍatvāt || VSpkC_1.5:11
children.translated_text: Moreover, the state of delusion — even the <s>Brahman</s>-nature, consisting of mere illumination devoid of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), which is of the nature of sovereignty — where even that does not exist; which those who know the end of the <s>Vedas</s> (Vedāntins) have accepted as 'consciousness is <s>Brahman</s>' — even that, without the <s>spanda</s>-power which is of the nature of autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>), would be inert.

children.text: * yathoktaṃ pratyabhijñāyām /
children.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>:

children.text: * svabhāvamavabhāsasya vimarśaṃ vidur anyathā /
children.translated_text: They know reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) to be the essential nature of illumination; otherwise,

children.text: * prakāśo 'rthoparakto'pi sphaṭikādijaḍopamaḥ || VSpkC_1.5:12
children.translated_text: illumination, even though tinged with objects, would be inert like a crystal.

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.5:13
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * bhaṭṭanāyakastotre 'pi /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka-stotra</s> also:

children.text: * napuṃsakamidaṃ nātha paraṃ brahma phalet kiyat /
children.translated_text: O Lord, how much fruit could this neuter Supreme <s>Brahman</s> yield,

children.text: * tvatpauruṣī niyoktrī cen na syāttvadbhaktisundarī || VSpkC_1.5:14
children.translated_text: if Your masculine directing power, beautiful with devotion to You, were not [there]?

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.5:15
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * evaṃ ca yatra sthitam ityataḥ prabhṛti yattattvaṃ vicāritaṃ tadevāsti tac cāstyeva paramārthato yuktyanubhavāgamasiddhena rūpeṇa paramārthata eva cākalpitena pūrṇena rūpeṇāsti na tu nīlādivat kalpitena /
children.translated_text: And thus, the reality that has been investigated beginning from 'where it is established' — that alone exists, and indeed exists in the highest sense (<s>paramārthataḥ</s>), in a form established by reasoning, experience, and scripture. And it exists in the highest sense, in an uncreated, complete form — not in a constructed [form] like blue and the like.

children.text: * yathoktaṃ mahāgurubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: As stated by the great teacher:

children.text: * evamātmanyasatkalpāḥ prakāśasyaiva santy amī /
children.translated_text: Thus in the self, these unreal constructions belong to illumination alone;

children.text: * jaḍāḥ prakāśa evāsti svātmanaḥ svaparātmabhiḥ || VSpkC_1.5:16
children.translated_text: the inert [things] — illumination alone exists — [known] by its own self and by other selves.

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.5:17
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * tatrabhavadbhartṛhariṇāpi /
children.translated_text: By the revered <s>Bhartṛhari</s> also:

children.text: * yadādau ca yadante ca yanmadhye tasya satyatā /
children.translated_text: What [exists] in the beginning, in the end, and in the middle — that has reality.

children.text: * na yad ābhāsate tasya satyatvaṃ tāvadeva hi || VSpkC_1.5:18
children.translated_text: What does not appear — its reality is only to that extent.

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.5:19
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * sāvadhāraṇatvāt sarvavākyānām evakāro 'tra trir yojyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Due to the emphatic and restrictive nature of all these sentences, the particle 'eva' (alone/indeed) should be applied three times here.

children.text: * evamanena sūtreṇa sukhādyākārasaṃvitsaṃtānavādināṃ sukhādikaluṣitapramātṛtattvavādināṃ grāhyagrāhakanānātvavādināṃ sarveṣām abhāvavādināṃ niṣparāmarśaprakāśabrahmavādināṃ ca matam anupapannatvād asattvenānūdya pāramārthikaṃ spandaśaktirūpameva tattvam astīti pratijñātam || VSpkC_1.5:20
children.translated_text: Thus, by this <s>sūtra</s>, having rejected as non-existent — because of their logical inconsistency — the positions of those who hold the doctrine of a continuum of cognitions with forms of pleasure and the like (Buddhists), of those who hold the doctrine of a knowing subject tainted by pleasure and the like (<s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>), of those who hold the doctrine of the multiplicity of graspable and grasper, of all those who hold the doctrine of non-existence (<s>śūnyavādins</s>), and of those who hold the doctrine of <s>Brahman</s> as mere illumination without reflective awareness (Vedāntins) — it has been asserted that the reality is solely the <s>spanda</s>-power in its ultimate form.

children.text: * atha ca yasminn asmin sopadeśasāvadhānamahānubhāvapariśīlye sphurattāsāre spandatattve sphurati duḥkhasukhagrāhyagrāhakatadabhāvādikam idaṃ sad api na kiṃcid eva sarvasyaitac camatkāraikasāratvāt tad evaitad astīty upadiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: And furthermore, in this <s>spanda</s>-principle, whose essence is pulsation, which is to be cultivated by the greatly powerful ones through attentive instruction — when it pulsates, this [entire range of] pain, pleasure, graspable, grasper, and their absence and the like, though existing, is nothing at all, because everything has as its sole essence wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) — it is taught that precisely this exists.

children.text: * yanmahāguravaḥ /
children.translated_text: As the great teacher [says]:

children.text: * duḥkhānyapi sukhāyante viṣam apy amṛtāyate /
children.translated_text: Even pains turn into pleasures, even poison turns to nectar,

children.text: * mokṣāyate ca saṃsāro yatra mārgaḥ sa śāṃkaraḥ || VSpkC_1.5:21
children.translated_text: and even <s>saṃsāra</s> becomes liberation — where that path is, that is the <s>Śāṅkara</s> [path].

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.5:22
children.translated_text: Thus. || VSpkC_1.5:22

children.text: * śāṃkaro mārgaḥ śaṃkarātmasvabhāvaprāptihetuḥ parāśaktirūpaḥ prasaraḥ || VSpkC_1.5:23
children.translated_text: The path of <s>Śaṃkara</s> (Śiva) — that which is the cause of attaining one's own essential nature as <s>Śaṃkara</s> — is the expansion (<s>prasara</s>) in the form of the supreme power (<s>parāśakti</s>). || VSpkC_1.5:23

children.text: * evam upapattiparighaṭitatattvapratyabhijñānāya sābhijñānam upāyaṃ nirūpayati || VSpkC_1.5:24]
children.translated_text: Thus, for the recognition of the reality established through reasoning, he sets forth the means accompanied by direct knowledge. || VSpkC_1.5:24
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>]

children.text: yataḥ karaṇavargo 'yaṃ vimūḍho 'mūḍhavat svayam /
children.translated_text: Since this group of organs (<s>karaṇavarga</s>), though deluded, by itself, as if undeluded,

children.text: sahāntareṇa cakreṇa pravṛttisthitisaṃhṛtīḥ // VSpk_1.6 //
children.translated_text: together with the inner circle [of governing powers], [engages in] creation, maintenance, and dissolution — // VSpk_1.6 //

children.text: labhate tatprayatnena parīkṣyaṃ tattvamādarāt /
children.translated_text: [that] reality is to be examined with effort and with reverence;

children.text: yataḥ svatantratā tasya sarvatreyam akṛtrimā // VSpk_1.7 //
children.translated_text: since this unfabricated autonomy (<s>svatantratā</s>) of that [reality] is everywhere. // VSpk_1.7 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
children.translated_text: [From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: * tannirṇītaṃ tattvam ādarāt śraddhayā prayatnena ca /
children.translated_text: That ascertained reality, with reverence — that is, with faith — and with effort;

children.text: * udyamo bhairavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The exertion is <s>Bhairava</s>;

children.text: * iti śivasūtrapratipāditena sarvabhedopasaṃhārātmanā nijaujovṛttisphāraṇarūpeṇa paripūrṇāntarmukhasvarūpasevanātmanā bhairavarūpeṇodyamena parīkṣyam || VSpkC_1.6-7:1
children.translated_text: that is, it is to be examined through exertion in the form of <s>Bhairava</s> — whose nature is the cultivation of one's own complete, inward-turned essential nature, whose form is the expansion of one's own power and vitality, whose nature is the withdrawal of all differentiation — as taught in the <s>Śivasūtras</s>. || VSpkC_1.6-7:1

children.text: * yata iyamiti sarvasya svasaṃviditā tasya śaṃkarātmanaḥ svasvabhāvasyākṛtrimā sahajā spandatattvarūpā svatantratā sarvatra jaḍājaḍaviṣaye sphurantī sthiteti śeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Since this' — known to all through one's own awareness — the unfabricated, innate autonomy (<s>svatantratā</s>), whose nature is the reality of <s>spanda</s> (vibration), of that one whose essential nature (<s>svasvabhāva</s>) is <s>Śaṃkara</s>, shining everywhere — in the domain of both the inert and the conscious — remains. This is the completion [of the verse]. 'What is that reality?' — to this he says, from 'since' up to 'obtains.' || VSpkC_1.6-7:2

children.text: * kiṃ tat tattvam ityāha yata ityādi labhata ityantam || VSpkC_1.6-7:2
children.translated_text: 'What is that reality?' — he says, from 'since' to 'obtains.' || VSpkC_1.6-7:2

children.text: * ayamiti lokaprasiddho golakādirūpo na tu śāstritastasya nityaparokṣatvenāyamiti nirdeśābhāvāt karaṇavargas trayodaśendriyāṇi viśeṣeṇa mūḍho māyāvaśāj jaḍābhāsībhūto 'ṇor mūḍhād apyadhikaṃ mūḍhatvaṃ prāpto 'mūḍhavac cetanavat svayaṃ pravṛttisthitisaṃhṛtīr labhate viṣayonmukhībhavati tatra rajyate tataśca nivartata ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.6-7:3
