children.translated_text: 'This' [refers to what is] well-known in the world, having the form of eyeballs and the like, not [to what is known] according to scripture, because of the absence of the demonstrative pronoun 'this' for what is always beyond direct perception. 'Group of organs' [means] the thirteen <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties). 'Specially deluded' — having become inert in appearance due to the power of <s>Māyā</s>, having attained a degree of delusion even greater than that of the deluded <s>aṇu</s> (limited self). 'As if undeluded' — as if conscious — 'by itself obtains creation, maintenance, and dissolution' — meaning: it becomes oriented toward objects, becomes attached therein, and then withdraws from them. || VSpkC_1.6-7:3

children.text: * kathaṃ sahāntareṇa cakreṇa ihāntaraṃ cakraṃ karaṇeśvaryo nāntaḥkaraṇāni teṣāṃ vargaśabdena svīkārāt na vakṣyamāṇaṃ puryaṣṭakaṃ tatsthasyāntaḥkaraṇatrayasya vargaśabdenaiva gṛhītatvāt tanmātrāṇāṃ ca vāsanāmātrarūpāṇām upadeśyam ayoginaṃ prati sākṣāt pravṛttyādikartṛtvenāsiddheḥ yoginastu sākṣāt kṛtatanmātrasya svayameva paratattvapariśīlanāvahitasyopadeśyatvābhāvāt tasmād etadekīyamatam asat || VSpkC_1.6-7:4
children.translated_text: How? 'Together with the inner circle.' Here, the 'inner circle' [refers to] the <s>karaṇeśvarīs</s> (governing powers of the organs), not the inner organs (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), since those have already been included by the word 'group.' Nor [does it mean] the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body) to be discussed later, since the triad of inner organs residing within it has already been grasped by the word 'group.' Nor [does it refer to] the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), which are merely of the nature of latent impressions, because their direct agency in activity and the like is not established with respect to a person being instructed who is not a <s>yogin</s>. But for a <s>yogin</s> who has directly realized the <s>tanmātras</s> and who is naturally absorbed in the cultivation of the supreme reality, there is no need for instruction. Therefore, this opinion of certain [teachers] is incorrect. || VSpkC_1.6-7:4

children.text: * vimūḍho 'mūḍhavad ityanena karaṇavarga eva saṃbandhyo natvantaramapi karaṇeśvarīcakraṃ tasya ciccamatkārarūpatvāt || VSpkC_1.6-7:5
children.translated_text: 'Deluded as if undeluded' — this should be connected with the group of organs alone, not with the inner circle of <s>karaṇeśvarīs</s>, because the latter has the nature of the wonder of consciousness (<s>ciccamatkāra</s>). || VSpkC_1.6-7:5

children.text: * evam abhidadhānasyāyam āśayaḥ yadayaṃ śaṃkarātmā svasvabhāvo 'tidurghaṭakariṇaḥ svātantryād yugapadeva saṃvittisāraṃ ca karaṇeśvarīcakraṃ jaḍābhāsarūpaṃ ca karaṇavargam ekatayaiva nirbhāsayan pravṛttisthitisaṃhṛtīḥ kārayati yena bhagavatyaḥ karaṇeśvaryo yathā tattadbhāvasṛṣṭyādi vidadhati tathā karaṇavargo jaḍo 'pi tatkārīva lakṣyate || VSpkC_1.6-7:6
children.translated_text: The intention of one who states thus is this: this essential nature, which is <s>Śaṃkara</s>, by its autonomy which accomplishes the most impossible things, simultaneously manifesting both the circle of <s>karaṇeśvarīs</s> — whose essence is consciousness — and the group of organs — whose form is the appearance of inertness — as a single [reality], causes creation, maintenance, and dissolution. By virtue of which, just as the blessed <s>karaṇeśvarīs</s> (governing goddesses of the organs) perform the creation of various states and the like, so too the group of organs, though inert, appears as if performing those [actions]. || VSpkC_1.6-7:6

children.text: * yadyapi rahasyadṛṣṭau na kaścij jaḍaḥ karaṇavargo 'sti apitu vijñānadehāḥ karaṇeśvarya eva vijṛmbhante tathāpīha suprasiddhapratītyanusāreṇopadeśyaḥ krameṇa rahasyārthopadeśe 'nupraveśya ityevam uktam || VSpkC_1.6-7:7
children.translated_text: Although from the esoteric perspective no inert group of organs exists whatsoever — rather, the <s>karaṇeśvarīs</s> themselves, as bodies of consciousness, expand — nevertheless, here the teaching follows the well-known ordinary understanding, so as to gradually lead [the student] into the instruction on the esoteric meaning. This is why it has been stated thus. || VSpkC_1.6-7:7

children.text: * evaṃ ca golakādirūpakaraṇavargāpravṛttyādikrameṇa tadadhiṣṭhātṛrūpaṃ nijamarīcicakraṃ cinvānenaiva tadubhayapracodakaṃ śrīmacchaṃkarātmakaṃ svasvarūpaṃ parīkṣaṇīyaṃ yatas tatprāptau tadīyākṛtrimā svatantratāsya yoginaḥ syād ity apy anenaivoktaṃ bhavati || VSpkC_1.6-7:8
children.translated_text: And thus, by tracing through the sequence of activity and the like of the group of organs in the form of eyeballs and so forth, one discovers the circle of one's own rays (<s>nijamarīcicakra</s>) — which is the governing principle of those [organs] — and thereby one's own essential nature, which is the glorious <s>Śaṃkara</s> and which impels both [the organs and their governing powers], is to be examined. Because upon its attainment, its unfabricated autonomy would become [manifest] for this <s>yogin</s> — this too is stated by this very [verse]. || VSpkC_1.6-7:8

children.text: * tadetadeva parīkṣaṇārhaṃ paramopādeyatvād etadeva ca parīkṣituṃ śakyamuktayuktyā sukhopāyatvāt ata evādareṇābhilaṣitaviṣayopabhogānirodhātmanā bahumānena || VSpkC_1.6-7:9
children.translated_text: This alone is worthy of examination, because it is supremely worth attaining; and this alone can be examined, by the reasoning already stated, because the means [to do so] are easy. Therefore, 'with reverence' means with great esteem, whose nature is the non-suppression of the enjoyment of desired objects. || VSpkC_1.6-7:9

children.text: * atra parīkṣaṇasyehatyopadeśānusāreṇa prāptakālatā || VSpkC_1.6-7:10
children.translated_text: Here, the timeliness of the examination follows the instruction [given] in this [verse]. || VSpkC_1.6-7:10

children.text: * yathoktaṃ rahasyagurubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: As stated by the esoteric teachers:

children.text: * nijanijeṣu padeṣu patantv imāḥ karaṇavṛttaya ullasitā mama /
children.translated_text: Let these radiant activities of the organs fall upon their respective objects;

children.text: * kṣaṇam apīśa manāgapi maiva bhūt tvadvibhedarasakṣatisāhasam || VSpkC_1.6-7:11
children.translated_text: O Lord, may there never be, even for a moment, even slightly, the violence of the taste of separation from You. || VSpkC_1.6-7:11

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.6-7:12
children.translated_text: Thus. || VSpkC_1.6-7:12

children.text: * parīkṣyam ity arhe śakye prāptakālatāyāṃ praiṣādau ca kṛtyaḥ || VSpkC_1.6-7:13
children.translated_text: 'To be examined' (<s>parīkṣyam</s>) — the <s>kṛtya</s> suffix [is used] in the sense of worthiness, capability, timeliness, and command. || VSpkC_1.6-7:13

children.text: * atha ca jaḍaḥ karaṇavargo yad balād amūḍhavat pravṛttyādi labhate iti sarvasyānubhavasākṣikam abhidadhadindriyādicaitanyavādicārvākamatam apyanena vyudastavān || VSpkC_1.6-7:14
children.translated_text: Moreover, by stating that the inert group of organs forcibly obtains activity and the like 'as if undeluded' — which is witnessed by everyone's experience — he has also by this [verse] refuted the <s>Cārvāka</s> (materialist) doctrine that holds that consciousness belongs to the sense organs and the like. || VSpkC_1.6-7:14

children.text: * atha kathamuktaṃ tatas tattvāc cetanatām ivāsādyendriyāṇi svayaṃ pravṛttyādi labhanta iti yāvatāyam eva grāhaka icchayā dātrādīnīva karaṇāni prerayati || VSpkC_1.6-7:15
children.translated_text: Now, how is it said that 'therefore, having attained consciousness as it were from that reality, the sense organs by themselves obtain activity and the like'? To the extent that this very [reality], the perceiver, impels the organs like gifts given by will. || VSpkC_1.6-7:15

children.text: * yad apyuktaṃ tat tattvaṃ prayatnena parīkṣyam iti tadapi kathaṃ yato 'smākam icchā bahir evānudhāvati na tu tattvaparīkṣāyāṃ pravartitum utsahata ity āśaṅkyāha || VSpkC_1.6-7:16]
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'that reality is to be examined with effort' — how [is this possible]? Because our desire (<s>icchā</s>) runs only outward and does not venture to engage in the examination of reality — anticipating this [objection], he says: || VSpkC_1.6-7:16

children.text: na hīcchānodanasyāyaṃ prerakatvena vartate /
children.translated_text: For this [person] does not function by way of desire-impulsion as the impeller;

children.text: api tv ātmabalasparśāt puruṣas tatsamo bhavet // VSpk_1.8 //
children.translated_text: rather, from contact with the power of the Self, the person becomes equal to That. // VSpk_1.8 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* ayaṃ laukikaḥ puruṣa icchaiva nodanaṃ pratodastasya prerakatvena karaṇapravartanārthavyāpāraṇāya yasmān na pravartate api tu ātmanaś cidrūpasya yad balaṃ spandatattvātmakaṃ tatsparśāt tatkṛtāt kiyanmātrād āveśāt tatsamo bhavet ahaṃtārasavipruḍabhiṣekādacetano 'pi cetanatām āsādayatyeva || VSpkC_1.8:1
children.translated_text: 'This' ordinary person — desire itself is the impulsion, the goad, for him — does not function as an impeller, for the purpose of engaging the organs in purposeful activity. Rather, from the contact with — that is, from the slight absorption produced by — the power of the Self, which is consciousness, whose nature is the reality of <s>spanda</s> (vibration), he becomes equal to That. Through the consecration of the sprinkle of the essence of 'I'-consciousness, even what is non-conscious attains the state of consciousness. || VSpkC_1.8:1

children.text: * tatas tat tattvaṃ na kevalaṃ karaṇāni yāvat tatprerakatvena śaṅkitaṃ kalpitamapi pramātāraṃ cetanīkṛtya svayaṃ pravṛttyādipātraṃ karoti yenāsyāyam abhimāno 'haṃ karaṇāni prerayāmīti || VSpkC_1.8:2
children.translated_text: Therefore, that reality not only [vivifies] the organs; it also, by vivifying even the knower — who is suspected to be [merely] its impeller — makes him a vessel for activity and the like. By which, this self-attribution arises: 'I impel the organs.' || VSpkC_1.8:2

children.text: * spandatattvānuvedhaṃ vināpi tu sa eva na kiṃciditi karaṇānāṃ grāhakasya ca svaraśmicakraprasarānuvedhena cetanībhāvāpādakaṃ tattvaṃ parīkṣyamiti yuktameva || VSpkC_1.8:3
children.translated_text: However, without the pervasion of the <s>spanda</s> reality, that [knower] himself is nothing. And so it is entirely proper [to say] that the reality which brings about the state of consciousness for both the organs and the perceiver through the pervasion of its own ray-circle (<s>svaraśmicakra</s>) is to be examined. || VSpkC_1.8:3

children.text: * yadi punar icchākhyena pratodarūpeṇa karaṇāntareṇa karaṇāni prerayet tad apīcchākhyaṃ karaṇaṃ preryatvāt karaṇāntaraṃ svapreraṇāyāpekṣeta tadapy anyad ity anavasthā syāt || VSpkC_1.8:4
children.translated_text: Furthermore, if [one were to say that] the organs are impelled by another organ called desire, in the form of a goad — then that organ called desire too, being something to be impelled, would require yet another organ for its own impulsion, and that [would require] another, resulting in infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>). || VSpkC_1.8:4

children.text: * yat tūktam asmākamicchā na tatra pravartitum utsahate iti tatrāpyādyaṃ ślokārdham abhyupagamena paraṃ tūttaratayā yojyam || VSpkC_1.8:5
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'our desire does not venture to engage in that [examination]' — to that also, the first half-verse is to be taken as a concession, while the second half is to be connected as the [actual] answer. || VSpkC_1.8:5

children.text: * satyaṃ nāyaṃ puruṣastattvaparīkṣārtham icchāṃ pravartayituṃ śaknoti necchayā tattvaṃ viṣayīkartuṃ kṣamas tasyāvikalpyatvād api tu viṣayān anudhāvantīm icchāṃ tadupabhogapuraḥsaraṃ praśamayya yadā tv antarmukhamātmabalaṃ spandatattvaṃ svakaraṇānāṃ ca cetanāvahaṃ spṛśati tadā tatsamo bhavet tatsamāveśāt tadvat sarvatra svatantratām āsādayatyeva yasmād evaṃ tasmāt tattvaṃ parīkṣyam ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.8:6
children.translated_text: True, this person is not able to direct desire toward the examination of reality, nor is desire capable of making reality its object, because [reality] is beyond conceptual determination (<s>avikalpya</s>). However, having pacified desire — which runs after objects — through first enjoying them, when he then touches inwardly the power of the Self, the <s>spanda</s> reality, which brings consciousness to his own organs, then he becomes equal to That. Through absorption in That, he attains autonomy everywhere, just like That. Since this is so, therefore the reality is to be examined — this is the meaning. || VSpkC_1.8:6

children.text: * śaktibhūmeḥ sparśāpradhānatvād ātmabalasparśādity uktam || VSpkC_1.8:7
children.translated_text: Because contact is not the primary aspect in the domain of power (<s>śaktibhūmi</s>), it is said 'from contact with the power of the Self.' || VSpkC_1.8:7

children.text: * nanu cāyaṃ kṣetrī parameśvaramayo 'pi kiṃ na sadā pāripūrṇyena sphurati kasmād antarmukhātmabalasparśam apekṣata ity āśaṅkyāha || VSpkC_1.8:8]
children.translated_text: But this knower (<s>kṣetrin</s>), even though constituted of the Supreme Lord, why does he not always shine forth in complete fullness? Why does he require inward contact with the power of the Self? — Anticipating this [objection], he says: || VSpkC_1.8:8
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: nijāśuddhyāsamarthasya kartavyeṣvabhilāṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who is incapable due to his own impurity, who craves for things to be done,

children.text: yadā kṣobhaḥ pralīyeta tadā syātparamaṃ padam // VSpk_1.9 //
children.translated_text: when the agitation (<s>kṣobha</s>) subsides, then the supreme state (<s>paramaṃ padam</s>) arises. // VSpk_1.9 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* nijā svātmīyā svasvātantryollāsitā yeyaṃ svarūpāvimarśasvabhāvā icchāśaktiḥ saṃkucitā satyapūrṇaṃmanyatārūpā aśuddhir āṇavaṃ malaṃ tanmalotthitakañcukapañcakāvilatvāt jñānaśaktiḥ krameṇa bhedasarvajñatvakiṃcijjñatvāntaḥkaraṇabuddhīndriyatāpattipūrvam atyantaṃ saṃkocagrahaṇena bhinnavedyaprathārūpaṃ māyīyaṃ malamaśuddhir eva kriyāśaktiḥ krameṇa bhedasarvakartṛtvakiṃcitkartṛtvakarmendriyarūpasaṃkocagrahaṇapūrvam atyantaṃ parimitatāṃ prāptā śubhāśubhānuṣṭhānamayaṃ kārmaṃ malam apyaśuddhiḥ tayāsamarthasya pūryajñatvakartṛtvavikalpasya tata eva kartavyeṣu laukikaśāstrīyānuṣṭhāneṣv abhilāṣiṇo 'bhīṣṭānavāpter nityam abhilāṣavyākulasya tata eva kṣaṇam apy alabdhasvarūpaviśrānteḥ yadā uktavakṣyamāṇopapattyanubhavāvaṣṭambhato 'bhilāṣavivaśagrāhakābhimānātmā kṣobhaḥ pralīyeta anātmany ātmābhimānanivṛttipuraḥsaram ātmany anātmābhimānopaśāntiparyantena prakarṣeṇa līyeta tadā paramaṃ spandatattvātmakaṃ padaṃ syād asya pratyabhijñāviṣayatāṃ yāyād ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.9:1
children.translated_text: His own — belonging to His own self, displayed by His own autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>) — this will-power (<s>icchāśakti</s>), whose nature is the awareness of one's own essential nature, [when] contracted, taking the form of the delusion of considering oneself incomplete (<s>apūrṇaṃmanyatā</s>), becomes the impurity (<s>aśuddhi</s>) [known as] the <s>āṇava mala</s> (the innate impurity of individuality). Due to being clouded by the five coverings (<s>kañcuka</s>) arising from that <s>mala</s>, the knowledge-power (<s>jñānaśakti</s>), through the progressive contraction of [universal] omniscience-in-differentiation into limited knowledge (<s>kiṃcijjñatva</s>), taking on the forms of internal organ, intellect, and sense-faculties, by assuming extreme contraction, [becomes] the form of apprehension of differentiated knowables — that is the <s>māyīya mala</s> (the impurity of illusion), which is indeed impurity. The action-power (<s>kriyāśakti</s>), through the progressive contraction of [universal] omnipotence-in-differentiation into limited agency (<s>kiṃcitkartṛtva</s>), taking on the forms of action-organs, by assuming extreme limitation, [becomes] the <s>kārma mala</s> (the impurity of action), consisting of good and bad deeds, which is also impurity. For one rendered incapable by that [impurity], whose [capacity for] knowing and acting is merely conceptual, who therefore constantly desires worldly and scriptural performances among things to be done, who is perpetually agitated by desire because of never attaining what is wished for, and who therefore does not even for a moment rest in his own essential nature — when, through the support of reasonings stated and to be stated, and of experience, the disturbance (<s>kṣobha</s>), which is the ego-sense of the grasping subject overpowered by desire, would dissolve — would thoroughly dissolve, preceded by the cessation of the identification of the self with the non-self and culminating in the subsiding of the identification of the non-self with the self — then the supreme state, whose nature is the <s>spanda</s> (vibration) principle, would become [manifest]; it would become the object of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) — this is the meaning. (1.9:1)

children.text: * na tu tadaiva bhavati tasya nityatvāt || VSpkC_1.9:2
children.translated_text: But it does not [come into being] only at that time, since it is eternal. (1.9:2)

children.text: * uktaṃ ca vijñānabhairave |
children.translated_text: And it has been stated in the <s>Vijñānabhairava</s>:

children.text: * mānasaṃ cetanā śaktirātmā ceti catuṣṭayam /
children.translated_text: 'The mental [apparatus], consciousness (<s>cetanā</s>), power (<s>śakti</s>), and the self (<s>ātman</s>) — [these are] the fourfold [set].',

children.text: * yadā priye parikṣīṇaṃ tadā tadbhairavaṃ vapuḥ // VSpkC_1.9:3 //
children.translated_text: 'When, O beloved, [this fourfold set] is completely exhausted, then that is the body of <s>Bhairava</s>.' (1.9:3)
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.9:4
* nijāśuddhiśabdenamalaṃ nāma dravyaṃ pṛthagbhūtam astīti ye pratipannāste dūṣyatvena kaṭākṣitāḥ || VSpkC_1.9:5
children.translated_text: By the word 'one's own impurity' (<s>nijāśuddhi</s>), those who have understood that <s>mala</s> (impurity) is a separate substance are glanced at [i.e., criticized] as being refutable. (1.9:5)

children.text: * nanu ca grāhakāhambhāvātmani kṣobhe kṣīṇe nistaraṅgajaladhiprakhyam aspandameva tattvaṃ prasaktam ityāśaṅkāṃ śamayati || VSpkC_1.9:6]
children.translated_text: Now, when the disturbance in the ego-sense of the grasping subject is exhausted, it would follow that the principle is entirely motionless (<s>aspanda</s>), like an ocean without waves — to allay this apprehension: (1.9:6)

children.text: tadāsyākṛtrimo dharmo jñatvakartṛtvalakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then his innate quality, characterized by knowing and acting,

children.text: yatas tadepsitaṃ sarvaṃ jānāti ca karoti ca // VSpk_1.10 //
children.translated_text: by which he knows and does all that is desired, [becomes manifest]. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.10)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* tadetyupadeśyāpekṣayā akṛtrimaḥ sahajo dharmaḥ prāṅ nirdiṣṭasvatantratārūpaḥ parameśvarasvabhāvo jñatvakartṛtve sāmarasyāvasthitaprakāśānandātmanī jñānakriye lakṣaṇamavyabhicāri svarūpaṃ yasya tādṛk tadā kṣobhopaśame 'sya puruṣasya syād abhivyajyata ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.10:1
children.translated_text: 'Then' — with reference to the one being instructed — the innate (<s>akṛtrima</s>), inborn quality (<s>dharma</s>), which is the nature of the supreme Lord in the form of autonomy (<s>svātantratā</s>) previously indicated, whose distinguishing mark — the invariable essential nature — is knowing and acting, [which are] knowledge and action resting in the equilibrium of luminosity-and-bliss (<s>prakāśānanda</s>) — such [a quality] would become manifest for this person at the time of the subsidence of disturbance — this is the meaning. (1.10:1)

children.text: * kuta etad abhivyajyata ityāha yatastadā paramapadapraveśasamaye sarvam īpsitamiti yadyaj jijñāsitaṃ cikīrṣitaṃ vāsya tat pravivikṣāyām abhūt tattaj jānāti ca karoti ca || VSpkC_1.10:2
children.translated_text: How does this become manifest? He says: 'by which' (<s>yataḥ</s>) — then, at the time of entering the supreme state, 'all that is desired' — whatever he wished to know or wished to do that was present at the moment of his aspiration to enter [that state] — that he knows and does. (1.10:2)

children.text: * cakārāv atra yaugapadyam āhatuḥ na tu yathaike cakārābhyāṃ jñānakriyayor aikātmyaṃ sūcayatīti taddhi jñatvakartṛtvalakṣaṇa ity anenaivaikadharmaviśeṣaṇena sambandhinirdeśena vāstavasvarūpābhidhāyinoktam || VSpkC_1.10:3
children.translated_text: The two 'ca' particles here express simultaneity — and it is not [the case], as some maintain, that the two 'ca' particles indicate the identity of knowledge and action; for that has already been stated by the single qualifying attribute 'characterized by knowing and acting' in designating the related [quality], which expresses the actual essential nature. (1.10:3)

children.text: * atha yataḥ karaṇeti nijāśuddhīti sūtrapratipāditonmeṣakramasamādhānasākṣātkṛtasya spandatattvasya dṛḍhāvaṣṭambhād vyutthānamapi samādhyekarasaṃ kurvato bhavocchedo bhavatītyāha || VSpkC_1.10:4]
children.translated_text: Now, because of the firm grounding in the <s>spanda</s> principle directly realized through the gradual settling process of unfolding (<s>unmeṣa</s>) taught in the <s>sūtras</s> 'since the group of instruments' and 'one's own impurity,' even the state of emergence from meditation (<s>vyutthāna</s>) becomes of one flavor with <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), and thus the cessation of worldly existence (<s>bhavoccheda</s>) occurs — this he states: (1.10:4)
[<s>Spandakārikā-nirṇaya</s>]

children.text: tamadhiṣṭhātṛbhāvena svabhāvamavalokayan /
children.translated_text: He who, observing his own nature in the state of being a presider (<s>adhiṣṭhātṛbhāva</s>),

children.text: smayamāna ivāste yas tasyeyaṃ kusṛtiḥ kutaḥ // VSpk_1.11 //
children.translated_text: abides as if smiling [in wonder] — for him, whence this wretched course [of worldly existence]? (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.11)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
children.translated_text: [<s>Spandakārikā-nirṇaya</s>]

children.text: * uktopapattyupalabdhyanuśīlanapratyabhijñātaṃ taṃ spandatattvātmakaṃ svabhāvam ātmīyam adhiṣṭhātṛbhāvena vyutthānadaśāyām api vyāpnuvantam avalokayaṃś cinvānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Observing — contemplating — his own nature, whose essence is the <s>spanda</s> principle, recognized through the cultivation of the reasonings and perceptions stated [above], as pervading even in the state of emergence from meditation (<s>vyutthāna</s>), in the capacity of a presider (<s>adhiṣṭhātṛbhāva</s>) —

children.text: * na vrajen na viśecchaktir marudrūpā vikāsite /
children.translated_text: 'The power in the form of breath (<s>marud</s>) should neither go out nor enter; when expanded,',

children.text: * nirvikalpatayā madhye tayā bhairavarūpadhṛk || VSpkC_1.11:1
children.translated_text: 'through freedom from conceptualization (<s>nirvikalpatā</s>), in the center, by that [power one] bears the form of <s>Bhairava</s>.' (1.11:1)

children.text: * iti tathā /
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: * sarvāḥ śaktīś cetasā darśanādyāḥ sve sve vedye yaugapadyena viṣvak /
children.translated_text: 'All the powers — seeing and the rest — casting them simultaneously in all directions upon their respective objects with the mind,

children.text: * kṣiptvā madhye hāṭakastambhabhūtas tiṣṭhan viśvākāra eko 'vabhāsi || VSpkC_1.11:2
children.translated_text: standing in the center like a pillar of gold, you alone shine forth as having the form of the universe.' (1.11:2)

children.text: * iti śrīvijñānabhairavakakṣyāstotranirdiṣṭasampradāyayuktyā nimīlanonmīlanasamādhinā yugapadvyāpakamadhyabhūmyavaṣṭambhād adhyāsitaitadubhayavisargāraṇivigalitasakalavikalpo 'kramasphāritakaraṇacakraḥ || VSpkC_1.11:3
children.translated_text: Thus, by the method of the tradition taught in the <s>Vijñānabhairava</s> and the <s>Kakṣyāstotra</s>, through the <s>samādhi</s> of closing and opening [the eyes], by firmly grounding [oneself] in the central ground that pervades simultaneously — having entered into both [inward and outward] emissions [of consciousness] as their substratum — with all conceptual constructions dissolved, with the circle of instruments expanded in a non-sequential manner (<s>akrama</s>) — (1.11:3)

children.text: * antarlakṣyo bahir dṛṣṭinimeṣonmeṣavarjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'With the gaze directed inward but the eyes outward, free from closing and opening [the eyelids],

children.text: * iyaṃ sā bhairavī mudrā sarvatantreṣu gopitā || VSpkC_1.11:4
children.translated_text: this is the <s>Bhairavī mudrā</s> (the seal of <s>Bhairava</s>), concealed in all <s>tantras</s>.' (1.11:4)

children.text: * ity āmnātabhagavadbhairavamudrānupraviṣṭo mukurāntarnimajjadunmajjannānāpratibimbakadambakalpamanalpaṃ bhāvarāśiṃ cidākāśa evoditam api tatraiva vilīyamānaṃ paśyan janmasahasrāpūrvaparamānandaghanalokottarasvasvarūpapratyabhijñānāt jhaṭiti truṭitasakalavṛttiḥ smayamāno vismayamudrāpraviṣṭa iva mahāvikāsāsādanāc ca sahasaiva samuditasamucitatāttvikasvabhāvo yo yogīndra āste tiṣṭhati na tv avaṣṭambhāc chithilībhavati tasyeyamiti sakalajagatkampakāriṇī kutsitā jananamaraṇādiprabandharūpā sṛtiḥ pravṛttiḥ kuto nijāśuddhilakṣaṇasya taddhetor abhāvān naiva bhavatītyarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.11:5
children.translated_text: Thus, having entered the <s>mudrā</s> of the Lord <s>Bhairava</s> as transmitted in scripture, seeing — like a multitude of various reflections submerging and emerging within a mirror — the vast mass of entities as having arisen in the very sky of consciousness (<s>cidākāśa</s>) and as dissolving right there itself, [the yogin], through the recognition of his own supramundane essential nature — a mass of supreme bliss unprecedented through thousands of births — with all mental modifications instantaneously severed, as if entering the <s>mudrā</s> (gesture) of wonder, smiling, and through attaining the great expansion (<s>mahāvikāsa</s>), with the appropriate actual essential nature suddenly arising — this supreme lord of <s>yogins</s> abides, remains — he does not become lax from [his] firm grounding. For him, this — [the question is:] whence this wretched course (<s>kusṛti</s>), which is the continuous stream of birth, death, and the rest, that makes the entire world tremble — since the cause of that, namely one's own impurity (<s>nijāśuddhi</s>), is absent, it simply does not occur — this is the meaning. (1.11:5)

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre /
children.translated_text: As stated in the sacred <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s> (the prior scripture):

children.text: * tattve niścalacittas tu bhuñjāno viṣayān api /
children.translated_text: 'One whose mind is steady in the truth (<s>tattva</s>), even while enjoying sense-objects,

children.text: * naiva saṃspṛśyate doṣaiḥ padmapattram ivāmbhasā || VSpkC_1.11:6
children.translated_text: is not touched by faults, like a lotus petal by water.' (1.11:6)

children.text: * viṣāpahārimantrādisaṃnaddho bhakṣayannapi /
children.translated_text: 'Even one who eats poison, equipped with poison-neutralizing <s>mantras</s> and the like,

children.text: * viṣaṃ na muhyate tena tadvadyogī mahāmatiḥ || VSpkC_1.11:7
children.translated_text: is not deluded by it — likewise the <s>yogin</s> of great understanding.' (1.11:7)

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.11:8

* atha ye śrutyantavidakṣapādamādhyamikādayaḥ kṣobhapralaye viśvocchedarūpam abhāvātmakameva tattvam avaśiṣyata ity upādikṣan tān pratibodhayituṃ tadupagatatattvaprātipakṣyeṇa lokottaratāṃ prakaraṇaśarīrasya spandatattvasya nirūpayati || VSpkC_1.11:9]
children.translated_text: Now, as for the followers of the <s>Śrutyantavid</s> (i.e., <s>Vedāntins</s>), <s>Akṣapāda</s> (i.e., <s>Naiyāyikas</s>), <s>Mādhyamikas</s> (Buddhist middle-way proponents), and others who have taught that when disturbance dissolves, what remains is a reality consisting of non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), of the nature of the annihilation of the universe — in order to awaken them, he demonstrates the supramundane nature of the <s>spanda</s> principle, which is the body of this treatise, by contrasting it with the principle they have adopted. (1.11:9)

children.text: nābhāvo bhāvyatāmeti na ca tatrāsty amūḍhatā /
children.translated_text: Non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) cannot become an object of contemplation, nor is there an undeluded state therein;

children.text: yato 'bhiyogasaṃsparśāt tadāsīd iti niścayaḥ // VSpk_1.12 //
children.translated_text: since from the contact of effort [i.e., upon emerging], there is the certainty 'that [state] existed.' (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.12)

children.text: atas tat kṛtrimaṃ jñeyaṃ sauṣuptapadavat sadā /
children.translated_text: Therefore that [state] should always be known as artificial (<s>kṛtrima</s>), like the state of deep sleep (<s>sauṣuptapada</s>);

children.text: na tv evaṃ smaryamāṇatvaṃ tat tattvaṃ pratipadyate // VSpk_1.13 //
children.translated_text: but that <s>tattva</s> (principle/reality) is not apprehended as merely something [subsequently] remembered. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.13)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* asad evedam agra āsīt || VSpkC_1.12-13:1
children.translated_text: 'In the beginning, this [universe] was indeed non-existent (<s>asat</s>).' (1.12-13:1)

children.text: * ityādyuktyā śrutyantavidādyabhimato 'bhāvo bhāvyatāṃ naiti bhāvanāyā bhāvyavastuviṣayatvād abhāvasya na kiṃcittvād bhāvyamānatāyāṃ vā kiṃcittve satyabhāvatvābhāvāt kiṃca bhāvakasyāpi yatrābhāvaḥ sa viśvocchedaḥ kathaṃ bhāvanīyaḥ bhāvakābhyupagame tu na viśvocchedo bhāvakasyāvaśiṣyamāṇatvād iti na viśvābhāva eva tattvam || VSpkC_1.12-13:2
children.translated_text: By reasonings such as this, the non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) maintained by the <s>Śrutyantavid</s> and others cannot become an object of contemplation (<s>bhāvyatā</s>), since contemplation has an existent object as its domain and non-existence is nothing at all; or if [non-existence] were something in becoming an object of contemplation, it would [by that fact] lose its character as non-existence. Moreover, the total annihilation of the universe, where even the contemplator is absent — how can that be contemplated? But if a contemplator is admitted [to remain], there is no total annihilation of the universe, since the contemplator persists. Therefore, the absolute non-existence of the universe is not the ultimate reality (<s>tattva</s>). (1.12-13:2)

children.text: * atha kalpito 'yaṃ bhāvako viśvocchedaṃ vikalpakalpyamānaṃ bhāvayan bhāvanāpariniṣpattau bhāvyatādātmyād abhāvarūpaḥ sampadyata iti pakṣaḥ || VSpkC_1.12-13:3
children.translated_text: Now, [suppose] this constructed contemplator, contemplating the annihilation of the universe as something constructed by conceptual imagination, attains the nature of non-existence through identification with the object of contemplation when the contemplation reaches completion — such is the [opposing] position. (1.12-13:3)

children.text: * tatrocyate tatrābhāvabhāvanāyāṃ nāmūḍhatā na ca tatrāsty amūḍhatā api tu moha evāsti /
children.translated_text: To that it is said: in that contemplation of non-existence, there is not an undeluded state — rather, there is only delusion (<s>moha</s>).

children.text: * yadyad evātibhāvyate /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever is intensely contemplated,

children.text: * bhāvanāpariniṣpattau tatsphuṭaṃ kalpadhīphalam || VSpkC_1.12-13:4
children.translated_text: when the contemplation reaches completion, that [becomes] clearly the fruit of a conceptual cognition (<s>kalpadhī</s>).' (1.12-13:4)

children.text: * iti nyāyād viśvocchedātmanyabhāve bhāvyamāne na kadācit paramārthāptir bhavati || VSpkC_1.12-13:5
children.translated_text: By this principle, when non-existence in the form of the annihilation of the universe is contemplated, the ultimate truth is never attained. (1.12-13:5)

children.text: * athocyate /
children.translated_text: Now it is said:

children.text: * sarvālambanadharmaiś ca sarvatattvair aśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Empty of all objective supports and their properties, of all <s>tattvas</s> (principles) without remainder,

children.text: * sarvakleśāśayaiḥ śūnyaṃ na śūnyaṃ paramārthataḥ || VSpkC_1.12-13:6
children.translated_text: empty of all latent deposits of afflictions (<s>kleśāśaya</s>) — [yet] not empty in the ultimate sense.' (1.12-13:6)

children.text: * iti nāgārjunoktam īdṛśaṃ tac chūnyamiti || VSpkC_1.12-13:7
children.translated_text: If what is meant is that the 'void' (<s>śūnya</s>) is of this kind, as stated by <s>Nāgārjuna</s> — (1.12-13:7)

children.text: * satyaṃ yadi cidānandaghanā svatantrā pāramārthikī bhittibhūtā bhūr abhyupeyate yathā vijñānabhairavādau pārameśvarīṃ dikkālakalanātītā || VSpkC_1.12-13:8
children.translated_text: True — if it is accepted that [this void] is a ground that is a mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānandaghana</s>), autonomous, ultimately real, like [what is taught] in the <s>Vijñānabhairava</s> and the like: '[the supreme] transcending the constructs of direction, time, and limitation,' (1.12-13:8)

children.text: * ityādinā pāramārthikīṃ bhittibhūtāṃ cidbhūmim avasthāpya śūnyabhāvanoktā anyathā na śūnyam iti śūnyaiveyam uktiḥ yadyad evātibhāvyate iti pratipāditatvāt || VSpkC_1.12-13:9
children.translated_text: Thus, having established the ultimate ground of consciousness (<s>cidbhūmi</s>) as the background [of all experience], the meditation on the void (<s>śūnya</s>) is described [by opponents]. Otherwise, [the statement] 'there is no void' — this very statement is itself [about] the void, since it has been established [by us] that 'whatever is intensely meditated upon' [takes on reality].

children.text: * yattu || VSpkC_1.12-13:10
children.translated_text: But [the opponents say]:

children.text: * sāvasthā kāpy avijñeyā mādṛśāṃ śūnyatocyate /
children.translated_text: 'That state, somehow unknowable, is called 'voidness' by people like us —

children.text: * na punar lokarūḍhyeva nāstikyārthānupātinī || VSpkC_1.12-13:11
children.translated_text: but not in the common worldly sense that implies nihilism.'

children.text: * ityālokamālāyām uktaṃ tat tu satyaṃ tvādṛśām avijñeyā avijñeyatvād vaktum aśakyety ucyatāṃ śūnyateti tu kutaḥ śūnyatāpi ca yāvad bhāvyate tāvad vikalpollikhitatvād asau vivejñaiya || VSpkC_1.12-13:12
children.translated_text: This is stated in the <s>Ālokamālā</s>. But [we reply]: true, for people like you it is unknowable; because it is unknowable, let it be said that it cannot be described — but why then [call it] 'voidness'? And as long as even voidness is being meditated upon, to that extent, being inscribed by conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), it is [itself] something to be known.

children.text: * yadi ca tvādṛśāṃ sā jñātumaśakyā tat tatpadasākṣātkārābhijñasadgurusaparyā kāryā na tu śūnyateti svamanīṣikayaiva vyavahṛtyātmā paraś cāgādhe mahāmohe nikṣeptavya ityalam || VSpkC_1.12-13:13
children.translated_text: And if that [state] is unknowable by people like you, then one should devote oneself to the true <s>Guru</s> who is expert in the direct realization of that state — rather than designating it as 'voidness' by one's own fancy and thereby plunging both oneself and others into the fathomless great delusion. Enough of this.

children.text: * atha kuto jñātaṃ tatra mūḍhatāstītyatrānenottaram āha yata iti || VSpkC_1.12-13:14
children.translated_text: Now, how is it known that there is delusion in that [state of void]? To this, he gives the answer with 'because' (<s>yata</s>).

children.text: * abhiyogaḥ samādhānotthitasya kīdṛgaham āsamiti tadavasthābhimukhavimarśātmābhilāpas tatsaṃsparśāt tadvaśāddhetos tad āsīd iti yato niścayaḥ gāḍhamūḍho 'ham āsam iti yato 'sti pratipattiḥ ato mohāvasthaiva sā kalpitā tathā smaryamāṇatvāt sā cānubhūyamānatvād anubhavituḥ pramātur avasthātṛrūpasya pratyuta sattām āvedayate na tv abhāvamiti viśvābhāvāvasthāyāṃ cidrūpasyākhaṇḍitameva rūpaṃ tiṣṭhatīti nāmuṣyābhāvo jātucid vaktuṃ śakyata ityuktaṃ bhavati || VSpkC_1.12-13:15
children.translated_text: 'Application' (<s>abhiyoga</s>) is the verbal expression of reflective awareness directed toward that state — 'what was I like?' — by one who has emerged from <s>samādhi</s>. From the contact with that [state], because of that [contact], [there is] the ascertainment 'that existed' — because there is the recognition 'I was deeply deluded.' Therefore that very state is posited as one of delusion, because it is remembered as such. And since it is being experienced [as delusion], it rather declares the existence of the experiencer — the knowing subject (<s>pramātṛ</s>) — who has the nature of one who persists through states. It does not [indicate] absence. Thus, in the state of the absence of the universe, the nature of the consciousness-form (<s>cidrūpa</s>) remains unbroken — therefore the absence of this [consciousness] can never be stated. This is what has been said.

children.text: * nanu dṛṣṭaṃ niścitaṃ nīlādi smaryate na ca śūnyabhūtasya nyagbhūtabuddhivṛtter niścayo 'sti tat kathamuktaṃ tad āsīd ityauttarakālikān niścayān mūḍhatā seti || VSpkC_1.12-13:16
children.translated_text: But [one objects]: blue and the like that have been seen and ascertained are remembered — yet there is no ascertainment of the void state, since the mental modification has been suppressed [in it]. So how is it said that 'from the subsequent ascertainment, that [state of delusion] existed'?

children.text: * ucyate vedyasyaiṣā gatiḥ yasmāt tadidaṃtāsāramidaṃtayā yāvatpramātrā svātmopāroheṇa na niścitaṃ tāvan na smaryate vedakastu kalpitaśūnyādyavasthāsu saṃkucito 'py asāṃketikāhaṃtāparamārtha eveti na tasya svātmani pṛthaktāstīti tanniścāyako vikalpaḥ ityahaṃvimṛśyameva tadā svasaṃvedane naiva siddhaṃ śūnyapramātṛrūpaṃ viśvapratiyogitvāc ca saṃkocasāra || VSpkC_1.12-13:17
children.translated_text: We reply: this is the nature of the knowable — because as long as its 'this-ness' (<s>idaṃtā</s>) essence has not been ascertained by the knowing subject through elevation to [the level of] the self, it is not remembered. But the knower, though contracted in states posited as void and the like, is in ultimate reality nothing other than non-conventional 'I'-ness (<s>ahaṃtā</s>) — hence there is no separateness of it from its own self. Therefore, the conceptual construction that ascertains it — being reflected upon as 'I' at that time — in self-awareness, the form of a void-knower is not at all established; and because it is the counterpart of the entire universe, its essence is contraction.

children.text: * saduttarakālaṃ smaryata iti na kācid anupapattir yasmād evamatas tac chūnyātmakaṃ padaṃ kṛtrimam tasmād bhūtamabhūtaṃ vā yad yad evātibhāvyate /
children.translated_text: That it is remembered at a subsequent time — there is no impossibility [in that], because it is thus. Therefore that state whose nature is void is artificial. Hence, 'whether what is intensely meditated upon is real or unreal' —

children.text: * iti taduktayaiva nītyā abhūtabhāvanayaivotthāpitaṃ parameśvareṇaiva jñānagopanāyai mūḍhānām upeyatayā tathā bhāsitamityarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.12-13:18
children.translated_text: by the very principle stated [in the previous verse], [that void state] is produced by meditation on the non-existent; it is manifested as such by the Supreme Lord himself, for the purpose of concealing knowledge, as something to be adopted by the deluded — this is the meaning.

children.text: * jñeyaṃ jñātavyaṃ jñeyarūpaṃ ca sadā suṣuptavaditi dṛṣṭāntaḥ || VSpkC_1.12-13:19
children.translated_text: 'The knowable' means what is to be known; and [its] 'knowable form' is always as in deep sleep — this is the illustration.

children.text: * ayaṃ bhāvaḥ sadā suṣuptaṃ moharūpamaprayāsasiddhaṃ sarvasyāstyeva tat kim anena samādhiprayatnopārjitenānyena śūnyena kṛtyaṃ dvayasyāpyavastutvāviśeṣād iti || VSpkC_1.12-13:20
children.translated_text: The purport is this: deep sleep, which has the form of delusion and is effortlessly attained, exists for everyone. So what is the use of another void that is earned through the effort of <s>samādhi</s>? — since there is no difference in the unreality of both.

children.text: * prāyaścāsmin śūnye duruttare mahāmohārṇava eva vedāntavidakṣapādasāṃkhyasaugatādiprāyā bahavo 'nupraviṣṭāḥ || VSpkC_1.12-13:21
children.translated_text: And for the most part, many — including followers of <s>Vedānta</s>, <s>Akṣapāda</s> [Nyāya], <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, and Buddhism — have entered into this very void, a great ocean of delusion that is difficult to refute.

children.text: * spandatattvasamāvivikṣūṇām api ca śithilībhūtaprayatnānāṃ śūnyam etad vighnabhūtam || VSpkC_1.12-13:22
children.translated_text: And even for those who wish to enter into the <s>spanda</s> principle, this void becomes an obstacle when their effort has become slack.

children.text: * yadvakṣyati /
children.translated_text: As [the author] will say:

children.text: * tadā tasminmahāvyomni || VSpkC_1.12-13:23
children.translated_text: 'Then, in that great void [of consciousness] —'

children.text: * ityārabhya /
children.translated_text: beginning with this,

children.text: * sauṣuptapadavanmūḍhaḥ || VSpkC_1.12-13:24
children.translated_text: '[one becomes] deluded, as in the state of deep sleep.'
Thus.

children.text: * ata etaducchede granthakārasya mahān saṃrambho lakṣyate || VSpkC_1.12-13:26
children.translated_text: Therefore, the great vehemence of the author of the treatise is evident in the uprooting of this [void doctrine].

children.text: * tathā ceha heyatayaiva tan nirṇīyāpi punarapi nirṇeṣyate /
children.translated_text: And so here, having determined it as something to be rejected, it will be determined [as such] once again [later] —

children.text: * kāryonmukhaḥ prayatno yaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The effort that is directed toward an effect —'

children.text: * ityatra || VSpkC_1.12-13:27
children.translated_text: — in that [context].

children.text: * tato 'smābhir etaddūṣaṇārambhaḥ kṛta iti na naḥ kopaḥ kāryo 'trabhavadbhir upadeśanibhālanadattakarṇaiḥ || VSpkC_1.12-13:28
children.translated_text: Therefore, the undertaking of the refutation of this [void doctrine] has been made by us — hence no anger should be directed at us by the honorable [opponents] who have given ear to the examination of the teaching.

children.text: * saugateṣu dūṣiteṣu śrutyantavādādayo dūṣitā eva tulyanyāyatvād iti nābhyadhikam uktam || VSpkC_1.12-13:29
children.translated_text: When the Buddhists have been refuted, the <s>Vedānta</s> proponents and others are refuted as well, since the reasoning is the same — hence nothing additional has been said.

children.text: * tadidānīṃ prakṛtameva brūmahe tattu spandākhyaṃ tattvamevamiti śūnyavan na smaryamāṇatvaṃ pratipadyate tasya sarvadānusyūtopalabdhrekarūpasya kadācid apy anupalabhyatvāyogāt || VSpkC_1.12-13:30
children.translated_text: Now then, we speak of the topic itself: that principle named '<s>spanda</s>' does not undergo the state of being something merely remembered, as the void does — because it is impossible for [<s>spanda</s>], which is of one nature as perception (<s>upalabdhi</s>) that is always threaded through everything, to ever become unperceived.

children.text: * tathā cāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: And as they [the scriptures] say:

children.text: * vijñātāram ere kena vijānīyāt || VSpkC_1.12-13:31
children.translated_text: 'By what, indeed, could one know the knower?'
Thus.

children.text: * yadyapi ca samāveśadaśā vyutthitena prāṇādisaṃskāravaśāt smaryate tathāpi na tāvadeva spandatattvamapi tu sarvānusyūtānavacchinnaprakāśānandasāraparapramātṛrūpam eva tat || VSpkC_1.12-13:33
children.translated_text: And even though the state of absorption (<s>samāveśa</s>) is remembered by one who has emerged [from it], due to the <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions) of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — nevertheless, the <s>spanda</s> principle is not merely that [remembered state]; rather, it is the very form of the supreme knower (<s>parapramātṛ</s>), whose essence is uninterrupted luminosity and bliss, threaded through everything.

children.text: * yadvakṣyati /
children.translated_text: As [the author] will say:

children.text: * tasmācchabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ || VSpkC_1.12-13:34
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, in the contemplation of words and objects, there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>.'
Thus.

children.text: * ato'syānavacchinnacamatkārarūpasya na jātucitsmaryamāṇatvaṃ mūḍhatvaṃ vā || VSpkC_1.12-13:36
children.translated_text: Therefore, for this [<s>spanda</s> principle] whose nature is uninterrupted wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>), there is never the state of being merely remembered, nor delusion.

children.text: * yastu tattattvamitīha tacchabdenāsya nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ sa || VSpkC_1.12-13:37
children.translated_text: But the designation of it by the word 'that' (<s>tat</s>) here, [in the expression] 'that principle' (<s>tattattva</s>) —

children.text: * svātantryāmuktam ātmānam || VSpkC_1.12-13:38
children.translated_text: 'The self not released from autonomy —'

children.text: * iti śrīpratyabhijñākārikoktanītyā kalpitasyaivāpāramārthikasvarūpasya na tu tattvataḥ pāramārthikasya || VSpkC_1.12-13:39
children.translated_text: according to the principle stated in the revered <s>Pratyabhijñā-kārikās</s>, [this refers to] a fabricated, non-ultimate form only, not to [its] ultimate reality.

children.text: * na pratipadyata ityanenedam āha asya tattvasya smaryamāṇatvena pratītir eva nāstīti || VSpkC_1.12-13:40
children.translated_text: 'Does not undergo' — by this he says: there is simply no cognition of this principle in the form of [mere] remembrance.

children.text: * nanu yatra sthitamityādau cidrūpasyaiva viśvakāryarūpatāgrāhitvamuktaṃ taddhyānotthāpitaṃ kṛtrimamabhāvātmakaṃ rūpaṃ te naiva gṛhītamiti katham asyānavacchinnacamatkārarūpam amūḍhatvam ityāśaṅkāyām āha || VSpkC_1.12-13:41]
children.translated_text: Now, in the [verse] beginning with 'in which it abides' etc., it was stated that the consciousness-nature assumes the form of the varied world-effects; but [the opponents say:] that form, produced by meditation, artificial and of the nature of absence — they have not grasped it. How then [can one say] that its nature is uninterrupted wonder and non-delusion? — to this doubt he says:
[<s>Spandakārikā-nirṇaya</s>]

children.text: avasthāyugalaṃ cātra kāryakartṛtvaśabditam /
children.translated_text: And here there is a pair of states designated as 'effect-hood' and 'agent-hood';

children.text: kāryatā kṣayiṇī tatra kartṛtvaṃ punarakṣayam // VSpk_1.14 //
children.translated_text: of those, effect-hood is perishable, while agent-hood is again imperishable. (1.14)

children.text: kāryonmukhaḥ prayatno yaḥ kevalaṃ so 'tra lupyate /
children.translated_text: Only the effort that is directed toward an effect is destroyed here;

children.text: tasmiṃl lupte vilupto 'smītyabudhaḥ pratipadyate // VSpk_1.15 //
children.translated_text: when that is destroyed, the unwise person thinks 'I am destroyed.' (1.15)

children.text: na tu yo 'ntarmukho bhāvaḥ sarvajñatvaguṇāspadam /
children.translated_text: But the inward-turned state (<s>bhāva</s>), which is the abode of the quality of omniscience —

children.text: tasya lopaḥ kadācitsyād anyasyānupalambhanāt // VSpk_1.16 //
children.translated_text: its disappearance never occurs, because no other [state that could replace it] is perceived. (1.16)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* atra spandatattve kāryatvaṃ kartṛtvamiti ca śabditaṃ śabdavyavahāramātreṇa bheditamavasthāyugalamasti vastuto hi tadekameva svatantraprakāśaghanaśaṃkararūpaṃ tattvaṃ kartṛsattvāvyatiriktayā prakāśātmanā kriyayā vyāptaṃ tadabhedena prakāśamānaṃ tattvabhuvanaśarīratadabhāvādirūpatvaṃ svīkurvatkāryam ityucyate tadanyasya kasyāpi kāraṇatvāyogāt || VSpkC_1.14-16:1
children.translated_text: Here, in the <s>spanda</s> principle, the pair of states designated as 'effect-hood' and 'agent-hood' — differentiated only by verbal convention — [exists]. In reality, however, that is one single principle whose nature is autonomous, dense luminosity, the form of <s>Śaṃkara</s>. Being pervaded by activity (<s>kriyā</s>), which is of the nature of luminosity and not different from the being (<s>sattā</s>) of the agent — shining in non-difference from that [agent] — [the principle], while assuming the forms of principles, worlds, bodies, and their absence, is called 'effect' (<s>kārya</s>) — since nothing else whatsoever could be a cause [of it].

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrīpratyabhijñāyām /
children.translated_text: As stated in the revered <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>:

children.text: * jaḍasya tu na sā śaktiḥ sattā yadasataḥ sataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But the inert does not have that power — the existence of what, from non-being, [becomes] being;

children.text: * kartṛkarmatvatattvaiva kāryakāraṇatā tataḥ || VSpkC_1.14-16:2
children.translated_text: the very reality of agent-hood and object-hood — from that [comes] the relation of cause and effect.'
Thus.

children.text: * tasya cedameva kāryatvaṃ yadayaṃ vicitradeśakālādyābhāsasaṃyojanaviyojanakrameṇānantān dehanīlādyābhāsāṃś cidātmanaḥ svarūpād anatiriktān api mukurapratibimbavad atiriktān ivābhāsayati yāvac ca kiṃcidābhāsayati tat sarvam ābhāsyamānatvādeva bahirmukhena rūpeṇa kṣayadharmakaṃ kṣayaś cāsyedaṃtābhāsanimajjanenāhaṃtārūpatayāvasthānam ata eva dehādergrāhakasya yo vedyāṃśaḥ sa eva bhagavatā sṛjyate saṃhriyate ca na tv ahaṃtāprakāśātmakaṃ kartṛrūpaṃ tasya dehādyāveśe 'pi bhagavadekarūpatvāt atastatra tayoḥ kāryakartṛtvayor madhyāt kāryatā kṣayiṇī kartṛtvaṃ citsvātantryarūpaṃ punarakṣayaṃ jagadudayāpāyayor api tasya svabhāvād acalanāt || VSpkC_1.14-16:4
children.translated_text: And this very 'effect-hood' of it [the <s>spanda</s> principle] is that it manifests the infinite appearances of body, blue, and the like — which, though not different from its own nature as consciousness (<s>cidātman</s>) — as if different, like reflections in a mirror, through the sequence of conjunction and disjunction of appearances of varied place, time, and the rest. And whatever it manifests, all of that, precisely because it is being manifested, in its outward-directed form is subject to destruction. And the destruction of this [effect] is the submersion of the 'this-ness' (<s>idaṃtā</s>) appearance [back] into abiding as 'I-ness' (<s>ahaṃtā</s>). Therefore, it is only the knowable aspect of the perceiver of the body and the rest that is created and dissolved by the Blessed [Lord] — not the agent-form whose nature is the luminosity of 'I-ness', since even in its entry into body and the like, it is of one nature with the Blessed [Lord]. Therefore, between those two — effect-hood and agent-hood — effect-hood is perishable, while agent-hood, whose nature is the autonomy of consciousness (<s>cit-svātantrya</s>), is again imperishable — since even in the arising and passing away of the world, it does not move from its own nature.

children.text: * calane tu jagadudayāpāyāv api na kaucic cakāsyātām iti mūḍhādyavasthāyām apy akhaṇḍitacamatkārasāram amūḍham evaitat || VSpkC_1.14-16:5
children.translated_text: But if [<s>spanda</s>] were to move [externally only], then even the arising and dissolution of the world would not shine forth at all. Therefore, even in the deluded state, this [reality] is indeed undeluded, whose essence is unbroken wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>). || VSpkC_1.14-16:5

children.text: * nanv abhāvasamādhānaniṣpattau suṣuptādau cāsya kartṛtvaṃ nopalabhāmahe kvacidapi pravṛttyadarśanāt || VSpkC_1.14-16:6
children.translated_text: But [one may object:] in the state of deep sleep and the like, where there is an absorption into non-existence, we do not perceive its agency, because no activity whatsoever is observed. || VSpkC_1.14-16:6

children.text: * satyaṃ kāryonmukha indriyādipreraṇātmakavyāpārapravaṇo yaḥ prayatnaḥ saṃrambhaḥ so 'tra kāryakṣayapade lupyate vicchidyate tasmiṃl lupte sati abudho 'bhāvasamādhyapahāritātmarūpo mūḍho vilupto 'smīti manyate || VSpkC_1.14-16:7
children.translated_text: True — that effort or exertion (<s>saṃrambha</s>) which is directed toward an effect and inclined toward the activity of impelling the sense organs and the like — that is dissolved, is interrupted, in the state where effects have ceased. When that is dissolved, the unwise one, whose essential nature has been carried away by the absorption into non-existence, thinks 'I am a deluded, extinguished being.' || VSpkC_1.14-16:7

children.text: * yaḥ punarantarmukho 'haṃtāprakāśarūpaḥ svabhāvo 'ta eva sarvajñatvaguṇasyāspadam upalakṣaṇaṃ caitat sarvakartṛtvāder api tasya lopo na kadācit syād bhavatīti na kadācidapi saṃbhāvanīyo 'nyasya tallopam upalabdhuḥ kasyāpy anupalambhāt yadi sa kaścid upalabhyate sa evāsāv antarmukhaś cidrūpo na ced upalabhyate tarhi sā lopadaśāstīti kuto niścayaḥ || VSpkC_1.14-16:8
children.translated_text: But that which is inward-turned, whose nature is the light of 'I'-consciousness (<s>ahaṃtāprakāśa</s>), that essential nature — and for this very reason this is the abode of the quality of omniscience, and also an indication of the quality of omnipotence and the like — its dissolution could never occur. There is no possibility at all [of its dissolution]. And who could perceive its dissolution? Because no [perceiver] other [than itself] is apprehended. If someone is apprehended [perceiving that dissolution], that is itself this very inward-turned, consciousness-natured [reality]. If no one is apprehended, then how can there be certainty that the state of dissolution exists? || VSpkC_1.14-16:8

children.text: * atha cānyaḥ kaścit tallopaṃ nopalabhate 'pitu sa eva prakāśātmā tatkathaṃ tasyābhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, no one other [than itself] perceives its dissolution; rather, it is itself the nature of light. So how can there be its non-existence?

children.text: * evaṃ cānyasyānupalambhanād ity atrānyakartṛkasyopalambhasyābhāvād ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.14-16:9
children.translated_text: Thus, 'because of the non-apprehension of another' means: because of the absence of apprehension that has another [being] as its agent — this is the meaning. || VSpkC_1.14-16:9

children.text: * atha ca ghaṭābhāvo yathā ghaṭaviviktabhūtalādyupalambhanān niścīyate tathaivātmābhāvo 'pyātmaviviktasya kasyacid upalambhān niścīyeta tadupalambhakasattāvaśyambhāvinīti tadupalambhakasvātmanāstitā na sidhyati || VSpkC_1.14-16:10
children.translated_text: Furthermore, just as the absence of a pot is ascertained from the perception of the ground and the like that is distinct from the pot, so too the absence of the self would be ascertained from the perception of something distinct from the self. But the existence of the perceiver of that [absence] is necessarily entailed, and therefore the non-existence of one's own self, which is the perceiver of that [absence], cannot be established. || VSpkC_1.14-16:10

children.text: * yadi ca kāryonmukhaprayatnalope sa lupyeta tadottarakālam anyasya kasyāpyupalambho na bhavet anyopalambhābhāvaḥ prasajyetety arthaḥ || VSpkC_1.14-16:11
children.translated_text: And if [the self] were to be dissolved upon the dissolution of effort directed toward effects, then after that time there would be no perception of anything else — the absence of the perception of anything else would follow — this is the meaning. || VSpkC_1.14-16:11

children.text: * api cānyasya bahirmukhasya prayatnasya sauṣuptādāv anupalambhāt katham antarmukhasya tattvasya bāliśair lopa āśaṅkito yato 'nyasya lope 'nyasya kiṃ vṛttam || VSpkC_1.14-16:12
children.translated_text: Moreover, since the outward-directed effort is not perceived in deep sleep and the like, how can the foolish suspect the dissolution of the inward-turned reality? For what has the dissolution of one thing to do with another? || VSpkC_1.14-16:12

children.text: * atha cānyasya kāryonmukhaprayatnasyānupalambhād anupalambhaprakāśanān na kadācit prakāśātmano 'ntarmukhasya tasyopalabdhur lopaḥ yato 'sāv antarmukhobhāvaḥ sarvajñatvaguṇasyāspadaṃ tām apyabhāvadaśāṃ vettyeva anyathā saiva na sidhyediti || VSpkC_1.14-16:13
children.translated_text: And since the non-perception of outward-directed effort is [itself] the illumination of non-perception, never can there be the dissolution of that inward-turned perceiver whose nature is light. Because that inward [reality], the non-existence [of which is proposed], is the abode of the quality of omniscience — it knows even that state of absence. Otherwise, that very [state of absence] would not be established. || VSpkC_1.14-16:13

children.text: * anyasyeti kartari karmaṇi ca ṣaṣṭhī || VSpkC_1.14-16:14
children.translated_text: 'Of another' — the sixth case suffix [is used] in both the agent and object senses. || VSpkC_1.14-16:14

children.text: * antarmukhe kāryatvapratiyogitām iva kartṛtvasya sambhāvyāvasthātvam uktaṃ vastutastu uktayuktyā tasyāvasthātṛtvam eva || VSpkC_1.14-16:15
children.translated_text: Regarding the inward-turned [reality], it has been stated that agency has the character of a possible state, like the counterpart-of-being-an-effect; but in truth, by the reasoning already stated, it possesses the nature of transcending all states. || VSpkC_1.14-16:15

children.text: * antarmukha iti antaḥ pūrṇāhaṃtātmakaṃ mukhaṃ pradhānaṃ yasyeti yojyam || VSpkC_1.14-16:16
children.translated_text: 'Inward-turned' (<s>antarmukha</s>) should be construed as: that for which the inner, consisting of the full 'I'-consciousness, is the primary face (focus). || VSpkC_1.14-16:16

children.text: * evam aprabuddho bahirmukhavyāpāranirodhe grāhakasyāpyātmano 'nupapannam apyabhāvaṃ niścinuta iti pratipādya suprabuddhāprabuddhayor yādṛg ātmopalambhastaṃ nirūpayati || VSpkC_1.14-16:17]
children.translated_text: Thus, having established that the unawakened one, upon the cessation of outward activity, erroneously determines the non-existence even of the perceiving self, he [now] describes what the self-apprehension of both the fully awakened and the unawakened is like. || VSpkC_1.14-16:17
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s> commentary:]

children.text: tasyopalabdhiḥ satataṃ tripadāvyabhicāriṇī /
children.translated_text: Its apprehension, ever unwavering in the three states,

children.text: nityaṃ syātsuprabuddhasya tadādyante parasya tu // VSpk_1.17 //
children.translated_text: would always be [present] for the fully awakened one; for the other [unawakened one], at the beginning and end [of each state]. // VSpk_1.17 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* tasya prākaraṇikasvabhāvasya yopalabdhiḥ anavacchinnaḥ prakāśaḥ sā kathitayuktyavaṣṭambhāt suṣṭhu prabuddhasyāprabuddhatāsaṃskāreṇāpi śūnyasya satataṃ triṣvapi jāgarasvapnasauṣuptapadeṣu nityamiti ādau madhye'nte cāvyabhicāriṇī anapāyinī syādbhavatyeva sadāsau śaṃkarātmakasvasvabhāvatayā sphuratīty arthaḥ || VSpkC_1.17:1
children.translated_text: Its — i.e., of the essential nature under discussion — apprehension, which is uninterrupted illumination, by virtue of relying on the reasoning already stated, for the one who is fully awakened and free from even the latent impression of unawakened-ness, is always (<s>satatam</s>) — in all three states of waking, dream, and deep sleep — 'always' (<s>nityam</s>) — at the beginning, middle, and end — unwavering, non-departing. It [always] exists — meaning, it always shines forth as one's own essential nature, which is <s>Śaṃkara</s>. || VSpkC_1.17:1

children.text: * parasyāprabuddhasya punastāsāṃ daśānāṃ svocitasaṃvidrūpāṇāṃ pratyekam ādāv udbubhūṣāyām ante ca viśrāntyātmakāntarmukhatve na tu svocitārthāvabhāsāvasthitirūpe madhyapade || VSpkC_1.17:2
children.translated_text: For the other, the unawakened one, at the beginning and end of each of those states — which have consciousness-forms suited to them — that is, at the beginning, in the desire to arise [into a new state], and at the end, in the inward-turning that is the nature of repose — but not in the middle state, which consists of abiding in the manifestation of objects suited to each [state]. || VSpkC_1.17:2

children.text: * yaduktaṃ śrīśivadṛṣṭau /
children.translated_text: As stated in the venerable <s>Śivadṛṣṭi</s>:

children.text: * yāvat samagrajñānāgrajñātṛsparśadaśāsv api /
children.translated_text: Even in the states of the totality of knowledge, the foremost knower, and the touch [between them],

children.text: * sthitaiva lakṣyate sā tu tadviśrāntyāthavā phale || VSpkC_1.17:3
children.translated_text: that [apprehension] is observed to remain; but either in the repose of that, or in its fruit. || VSpkC_1.17:3

children.text: * bhaṭṭalollaṭenāpi tadādyanta ityevameva vyākhyāyi svavṛttau || VSpkC_1.17:4
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaṭṭa Lollaṭa</s> also explained 'at the beginning and end of that' in exactly this way in his own commentary. || VSpkC_1.17:4

children.text: * bhaṭṭaśrīkallaṭavṛttyakṣarāṇyapekṣya vayamapi tadvṛttyakṣarānurodhena sautram artham ativimalamapi kliṣṭakalpanayā vyākartumaśikṣitāḥ yata evāsuprabuddhasya tadādyante 'sti tadupalabdhiḥ ata evāyam ihādhikārī spandopadeśaiḥ suprabuddhīkriyate || VSpkC_1.17:5
children.translated_text: We too, looking to the syllables of the venerable <s>Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa</s>'s commentary and following those syllables, have not been trained to interpret the extremely clear meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> through forced constructions. Since the unawakened one has the apprehension of that [reality] only at the beginning and end, he is the student here, and through the teachings on <s>spanda</s> he is made fully awakened. || VSpkC_1.17:5

children.text:
* yadvakṣyati /
* ataḥ satatamudyuktaḥ spandatattvaviviktaye /
* jāgrat /
* ityādi /
* sauṣuptapadavanmūḍhaḥ prabuddhaḥ syādanāvṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text:
As will be stated:
'Therefore, always diligent in discerning the <s>spanda</s> reality,
in waking...'
and so on.
'Like the state of deep sleep, the deluded one, [upon] awakening, would become unveiled.'

children.text: * iti /
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * tathā svapne'pi /
children.translated_text: Similarly, even in dream —

children.text: * ityādi /
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: * prabuddhaḥ sarvadā tiṣṭhet || VSpkC_1.17:6
children.translated_text: 'The awakened one should always abide [in that awareness].' || VSpkC_1.17:6

children.text: * ityādi ca || VSpkC_1.17:7
children.translated_text: And so on. || VSpkC_1.17:7

children.text: * atra hi jāgarāditriṣu padeṣu ādyantakoṭivan madhyamapy arthāvasāyātmakaṃ padaṃ turyābhogamayaṃ kartuṃ prabuddhasya suprabuddhatāpādanāyopadeśaḥ pravṛttaḥ etac ca nirṇeṣyāmaḥ || VSpkC_1.17:8
children.translated_text: For here, the instruction is set forth for making the awakened one fully awakened, so that in the three states of waking and the like, he may make the middle [portion of experience] also — which consists of the determination of objects — filled with the relish of the <s>turya</s> (fourth state), just as at the initial and final moments [of each state]. And this we shall determine [in detail]. || VSpkC_1.17:8

children.text: * tathā ca śivasūtram /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>Śivasūtra</s> [states]:

children.text: * jāgratsvapnasuṣuptabhede turyābhogasambhavaḥ || VSpkC_1.17:9
children.translated_text: In the differences of waking, dream, and deep sleep, the experience of the <s>turya</s> (fourth state) is possible. || VSpkC_1.17:9

children.text: * tathā /
children.translated_text: Also:

children.text: * triṣu caturthaṃ tailavad āsecyam /
children.translated_text: The fourth [state] should be poured into the [other] three like oil.

children.text: * iti /
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * tritayabhoktā vīreśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The enjoyer of the triad [of states] is the lord of heroes (<s>vīreśa</s>).

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.17:10
children.translated_text: Thus. || VSpkC_1.17:10

children.text: * suprabuddhasya triṣu padeṣu yādṛśy upalabdhis tāṃ vibhāgena darśayati || VSpkC_1.17:11]
children.translated_text: He [now] shows in detail what the apprehension of the fully awakened one is like in the three states. || VSpkC_1.17:11
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: jñānajñeyasvarūpiṇyā śaktyā paramayā yutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with the supreme power, whose nature is knowledge and the knowable,

children.text: padadvaye vibhurbhāti tadanyatra tu cinmayaḥ // VSpk_1.18 //
children.translated_text: the all-pervading one shines in two states; in the other, however, [he shines as] pure consciousness. // VSpk_1.18 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* suprabuddhasya bhūmnā jñānajñeyasvarūpayā madhyame pade jñānāgraparyantayos tu svasvarūpayaiva spandatattvātmanā parāśaktyā yukto vibhuḥ śaṃkarātmā svabhāvo jāgarāsvapnarūpe padadvaye bhāti || VSpkC_1.18:1
children.translated_text: For the fully awakened one, with fullness, the supreme power (<s>parāśakti</s>), whose nature is knowledge and the knowable, and in the middle state extending up to the foremost [point] of knowledge, is [present] in its own essential nature, as the <s>spanda</s> reality. Endowed with that [power], the all-pervading one, whose essential nature is <s>Śaṃkara</s>, shines in the two states that have the form of waking and dream. || VSpkC_1.18:1

children.text: * tatra hi viśvamasau sadāśiveśvaravatsvāṅgavat paśyati tadanyatra tu suṣupte na tu yathānye suṣuptaturyayor iti tripadāvyabhicāriṇī iti prakrānte turyasyāprastutatvāt tadupalabdher eva ca turyarūpatvāt asau vibhuś cinmaya evāsya bhāti aśeṣavedyopaśamād ity etat suprabuddhābhiprāyam eva na tu vastuvṛttānusāreṇa tadanyatra tu cinmayaḥ ity asyānupapannatvāpatteḥ loke sauṣuptasya mohamayatvāt śivāpekṣayā tu jāgratsvapnayorapi cinmayatvāt evamapi ca prakṛtānupayuktatvāt || VSpkC_1.18:2
children.translated_text: For there, he sees the universe as his own limb, like <s>Sadāśiva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>. In the other [state], however — in deep sleep — [he shines], but not [in the manner that] others [understand both] deep sleep and the fourth state (<s>turya</s>). Since in the context where 'unwavering in the three states' has been commenced, the fourth state is not under discussion — and because its apprehension itself has the nature of the fourth state — that all-pervading one shines as pure consciousness only, because of the subsidence of all that is knowable. This is to be understood as the intention of the fully awakened one, not as following the actual state of affairs. For otherwise, 'in the other, however, [he shines as] pure consciousness' would be untenable, since deep sleep in the ordinary world is of the nature of delusion, and since from <s>Śiva</s>'s perspective, even waking and dream are of the nature of pure consciousness. Even so, [this interpretation is preferable] because of the irrelevance [of the alternative] to the topic under discussion. || VSpkC_1.18:2

children.text: * itaḥ prabhṛti prathamaniḥṣyandānto granthaḥ prabuddhasya suprabuddhatāyai sthito yathā ṭīkākārairna cetitas tathā parīkṣyatāṃ svayameva kiyatpratipadaṃ likhāmaḥ || VSpkC_1.18:3
children.translated_text: From this point onward, up to the end of the first flow [of verses], the text stands for [the purpose of] making the awakened one fully awakened. Let it be examined independently how [this has not been] understood by the commentators. We shall write something on each point. || VSpkC_1.18:3

children.text: * yatheyaṃ jāgarādimadhyadaśāpi prabuddhaṃ na pratibadhnāti tathopapādayati || VSpkC_1.18:4]
children.translated_text: He demonstrates how even the middle state of waking and the like does not bind the awakened one. || VSpkC_1.18:4
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: guṇādispandaniḥṣyandāḥ sāmānyaspandasaṃśrayāt /
children.translated_text: The effusions of the <s>spanda</s> of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and the like, by virtue of taking refuge in the universal <s>spanda</s>,

children.text: labdhātmalābhāḥ satataṃ syur jñasyāparipanthinaḥ // VSpk_1.19 //
children.translated_text: having attained their [true] self, would always be non-obstructive for the knower. // VSpk_1.19 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* guṇāḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi yeṣāṃ prakṛtitattvaṃ vibhavabhūte māyātattvāvasthitā ihābhipretāḥ || VSpkC_1.19:1
children.translated_text: The <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — whose source is the <s>prakṛti</s> principle, situated in the <s>Māyā</s> principle which is the domain of [their] glory — these are what is intended here. || VSpkC_1.19:1

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrīsvacchande māyāmasūrakavinyāse /
children.translated_text: As stated in the venerable <s>Svacchanda</s> [Tantra], in the arrangement of the <s>Māyā</s> matrix:

children.text: * adhaśchādanamūrdhvaṃ ca raktaṃ śuklaṃ vicintayet /
children.translated_text: Below the covering and above, one should contemplate the red and white [forms];

children.text: * madhye tamo vijānīyādguṇās tv ete vyavasthitāḥ || VSpkC_1.19:2
children.translated_text: in the middle, one should know <s>tamas</s> (darkness) — these <s>guṇas</s> are established thus. || VSpkC_1.19:2

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.19:3
children.translated_text: Thus. || VSpkC_1.19:3

children.text: * ta ādayo yeṣāṃ kalādīnāṃ kṣityantānāṃ spandānāṃ viśeṣaprasarāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ye niḥṣyandāstanukaraṇabhuvanaprasarāḥ nīlasukhādisaṃvidaś ca tathā yogyapekṣayā bindunādādayas te satataṃ jñasya suprabuddhasya kasyacid evāpaścimajanmano 'paripanthinaḥ svasvabhāvācchādakā na bhavantīti niścayaḥ yatas te sāmānyaspandamuktarūpam āśritya yatra sthitam ityatra nirṇītadṛśā labdhātmalābhās tata evotpannās tanmayāś cetyarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.19:4
children.translated_text: Those beginning with 'ta' — the particular expansions (<s>spandas</s>) of <s>kalā</s> and the rest, ending with earth — and their emanations in the form of body, organs, and worlds, as well as cognitions of blue, pleasure, and the like, and also <s>bindu</s>, <s>nāda</s>, and so forth relative to the qualified [yogin] — these do not obstruct, that is, do not conceal the own essential nature of, a certain fully awakened one (<s>suprabuddha</s>) who is in his final birth. This is certain, because they, having obtained their existence by taking refuge in the form released by the universal <s>spanda</s> — as ascertained in 'where it is established' — have arisen from that very [spanda] and are of its nature.

children.text: * tathāhi /
children.translated_text: For thus:

children.text: * svāṅgarūpeṣu bhāveṣu patyurjñānaṃ kriyā ca yā /
children.translated_text: The knowledge and activity of the Lord with respect to entities that are His own limbs —

children.text: * māyātṛtīye ta eva paśoḥ sattvaṃ rajastamaḥ || VSpkC_1.19:5
children.translated_text: in the third [level] of <s>Māyā</s>, those very [powers] become <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> for the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>).

children.text: * iti śrīpratyabhijñoktadṛśā citiśaktireva pārameśvarī jñānakriyāmāyāśaktitritayatayā śrīsadāśivādipade sphuritvā saṃkocaprakarṣātsattvarajastamorūpaṃ krīḍāśarīraṃ śrayati yato nijacicchaktisphāramayatvāt tadadhiṣṭhitameva sarvadā sarvaṃ jānan suprabuddho guṇādiviśeṣaspandān anucchindann api spandatattvāveśamaya eva || VSpkC_1.19:6
children.translated_text: Thus, from the perspective stated in the revered <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>, the <s>citi-śakti</s> (power of consciousness) belonging to the Supreme Lord, having pulsated as the triad of knowledge-power, action-power, and <s>māyā</s>-power at the level of <s>Sadāśiva</s> and the rest, assumes — due to the intensification of contraction — a play-body (<s>krīḍāśarīra</s>) in the form of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. Since everything is always pervaded by the expansion of one's own <s>cit-śakti</s> (consciousness-power), the fully awakened one (<s>suprabuddha</s>), knowing [all to be] presided over by that [power], even without cutting off the particular <s>spandas</s> (vibrations) of the <s>guṇas</s> and the like, remains immersed in the <s>spanda</s>-principle itself.

children.text: * yathā tv aprabuddhān badhnanty ete tat pratipādayati || VSpkC_1.19:7]
children.translated_text: But how these [guṇa-spandas] bind the unawakened — that he sets forth:
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: aprabuddhadhiyas tv ete svasthitisthaganodyatāḥ /
children.translated_text: But for those whose intellects are unawakened, these [guṇa-vibrations], striving to conceal their own [true] state,

children.text: pātayanti duruttāre ghore saṃsāravartmani // VSpk_1.20 //
children.translated_text: cast [them] down upon the terrible, hard-to-cross path of <s>saṃsāra</s>. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.20)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* aprabuddhadhiyaḥ prāyaḥ sarvān apratyabhijñātapārameśvarīśaktyātmakanijaspandatattvān dehātmamānino laukikān prāṇādyātmābhimāninaś ca mitayoginas tv ete pūrvoktā guṇādispandaniḥṣyandāḥ svasyāḥ spandatattvātmanaḥ sthiteḥ sthaganāyodyatā nityaṃ tadudyamaikasārāḥ duḥkhenottāryante 'smād daiśikair jantucakramiti duruttāre laṅghayitum aśakye ghore duḥkhamaye saṃsaraṇamārge pātayanti || VSpkC_1.20:1
children.translated_text: Those whose intellects are unawakened — meaning most all worldly persons who identify with the body, not having recognized the <s>spanda</s>-principle whose nature is the power of the Supreme Lord, as well as limited <s>yogins</s> who identify with <s>prāṇa</s> and the like as the self. 'These' previously mentioned emanations of the <s>guṇa</s>-<s>spandas</s> and the like, striving to conceal their own state whose nature is the <s>spanda</s>-principle — always having that striving alone as their essence — cast [them] down on the path of transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>), which is terrible, full of suffering, and hard to cross — impossible to leap over, from which beings are extracted with great difficulty by teachers.

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrīmālinīvijaye /
children.translated_text: As stated in the revered <s>Mālinīvijaya</s>:

children.text: * viṣayeṣveva saṃlīnānadho'dhaḥ pātayantyaṇūn /
children.translated_text: The <s>Rudrāṇī</s> powers, which are remembered as lower and more terrible,

children.text: * rudrāṇūnyāḥ samāliṅghaya ghorataryo 'parāḥ smṛtāḥ || VSpkC_1.20:2
children.translated_text: embracing the <s>aṇus</s> (individual souls) immersed in sense objects, cast them down lower and lower.

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.20:3
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * tathā hi pūrvaṃ pratipāditā yeyaṃ spandatattvātmā parāśaktiḥ saiva viśvasyāntarbahiś ca vamanāt saṃsāravāmācāratvāc ca vāmeśvarīśaktiḥ tadutthāpitāni tu khecarīgocarīdikcarībhūcarīrūpāṇi catvāri devatācakrāṇi suprabuddhasya parabhūmisaṃcārīṇi aprabuddhānāṃ tu adharādharasaraṇiprerakāṇi || VSpkC_1.20:4
children.translated_text: For thus, the supreme power (<s>parāśakti</s>) whose nature is the <s>spanda</s>-principle, previously established, is herself the <s>Vāmeśvarī-śakti</s> — because she vomits forth the universe both internally and externally, and because she is the left-handed practice of <s>saṃsāra</s>. The four circles of deities raised by her — in the forms of <s>Khecarī</s>, <s>Gocarī</s>, <s>Dikcarī</s>, and <s>Bhūcarī</s> — for the fully awakened one, move in the supreme ground; but for the unawakened, they drive [them] on an ever-lower path.

children.text: * tathā hi yā eva suprabuddhasya khe bodhagagane carantyaḥ khecaryo 'kālakalitatvābhedasarvakartṛtvasarvajñatvapūrṇatvavyāpakatvaprathāhetavas tā evāprabuddhasya śūnyapramātṛpadacāriṇyaḥ kañcukarūpatayā sthitāḥ kālakalitatvakiṃcitkartṛtākiṃcijjhatābhiṣvaṅganiyamahetavaḥ || VSpkC_1.20:5
children.translated_text: For thus: those very [powers] which for the fully awakened one move in the sky (<s>kha</s>) — the firmament of awareness — as <s>Khecarīs</s>, causing the manifestation of non-temporality, non-difference, omnipotence, omniscience, fullness, and all-pervasiveness — those very same [powers] for the unawakened one, moving in the station of the void-perceiver, existing in the form of the coverings (<s>kañcukas</s>), become causes of temporality, limited agency, limited knowledge, attachment, and restriction.

children.text: * gaur vāk tadupalakṣitāsu saṃjalpamayīṣu buddhyahaṃkāramanobhūmiṣu carantyo gocaryaḥ suprabuddhasya svātmābhedamayādhyavasāyābhimānasaṃkalpāñ janayanti mūḍhānāṃ tu bhedaikasārān || VSpkC_1.20:6
children.translated_text: The <s>Gocarīs</s>, 'go' meaning speech, moving in the planes characterized by that [speech] — the planes of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and <s>manas</s> (mind) suffused with discourse — for the fully awakened one, they generate determinations, self-conceptions, and intentions pervaded by non-difference from one's own self; but for the deluded, [they generate those] whose sole essence is difference.

children.text: * dikṣu daśasu bāhyendriyabhūmiṣu carantyo dikcaryaḥ suprabuddhasyādvayaprathāsārāḥ anyeṣāṃ dvayaprathāhetavaḥ || VSpkC_1.20:7
children.translated_text: The <s>Dikcarīs</s>, moving in the ten directions — the planes of the external sense organs — for the fully awakened one, have as their essence the manifestation of non-duality; for others, they are the cause of the manifestation of duality.

children.text: * bhūrūpādipañcakātmakaṃ meyapadaṃ tatra carantyo bhūcaryas tadā bhogamayyā āśyānībhāvatayā tanmayatvamāpannāḥ bhūcaryaḥ suprabuddhasya citprakāśaśarīratayātmānaṃ darśayantya itareṣāṃ sarvato 'py avacchinnatāṃ prathayantyaḥ sthitāḥ ity evaṃ pramātrantaḥkaraṇabahiṣkaraṇaprameyarūpatayaiva tāni catvāri cakrāṇi guṇādispandamayāny aprabuddhabuddhīṃl laukikāṃs tathā bindunādādiprathāmātrasaṃtuṣṭān yoginas tattattvaprasararūpe saṃsāre pātayanti || VSpkC_1.20:8
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhūcarīs</s>, moving in the domain of the knowable (<s>meya-pada</s>) consisting of the fivefold [group] of earth-form and the like — at that time, having become full of enjoyment and having attained identity with those [objects] through the state of being immersed — the <s>Bhūcarīs</s> for the fully awakened one reveal themselves as having a body of the light of consciousness; for others, they manifest complete limitation everywhere. Thus, in the form of the subject, inner organs, outer organs, and the knowable, these four circles, consisting of the <s>guṇa</s>-<s>spandas</s> and the like, cast down worldly persons of unawakened intellects, and also <s>yogins</s> who are content merely with the manifestation of <s>bindu</s>, <s>nāda</s>, and the like, into <s>saṃsāra</s> whose form is the expansion of those respective principles.

children.text: * yata evam || VSpkC_1.20:9]
children.translated_text: Since this is so:
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>]

children.text: ataḥ satatamudyuktaḥ spandatattvaviviktaye /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who is constantly engaged in discerning the <s>spanda</s>-principle,

children.text: jāgradeva nijaṃ bhāvam acireṇādhigacchati // VSpk_1.21 //
children.translated_text: while fully awake, attains one's own [true] state before long. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.21)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
children.translated_text: [<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>]

children.text: * uktavakṣyamāṇarūpasya spandatattvasya viviktaye vimarśanāya satatam udyuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is constantly engaged in discerning — reflecting upon — the <s>spanda</s>-principle, whose nature has been stated and will be stated,

children.text: * mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate || VSpkC_1.21:1
