children.translated_text: Those who, with minds absorbed in Me, constantly united, worship Me — (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s>)

children.text: * iti gītoktadṛśā satatam evāntarmukhasvarūpanibhālanapravaṇo yaḥ sa jāgradeva jāgarāvasthāsthita eva nijamātmīyaṃ śaṃkarātmakaṃ svasvabhāvam acireṇādhigacchati tathā asya śaṃkarātmā āntaraḥ svabhāvaḥ svayam evonmajjati yena prabuddho nityoditasamāveśāsādanāt suprabuddho jīvanmukto bhavatītyarthaḥ || VSpkC_1.21:2
children.translated_text: in accordance with the perspective stated in the <s>Gītā</s>, one who is constantly inclined toward the contemplation of one's own inward-turned essential nature — he, 'while fully awake,' that is, while established in the waking state itself, attains before long his own nature, which belongs to the self, which is of the nature of <s>Śaṃkara</s>. In other words, his inner essential nature, which is of the nature of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, itself emerges, by which, being awakened, through the attainment of the ever-risen <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption), he becomes fully awakened — a <s>jīvanmukta</s> (one liberated while living). This is the meaning.

children.text: * yathāsyodyuktasya balavadālambanavaśoditānāyāsatadanyasakalavṛttikṣayamayīṣu niyatāsu yāsvavasthāsu spandanidhānam unmudritam abhimukhībhūtam āste tā etāḥ prathamam udyogasya viṣayā ityupadeṣṭum āha || VSpkC_1.21:3]
children.translated_text: In order to teach that the particular states in which the treasure of <s>spanda</s> becomes unveiled and turns toward [the yogin] — for one who is thus engaged, through the cessation of all other mental activities arising from the force of a powerful support — are first the objects of exertion, he says:

children.text: atikruddhaḥ prahṛṣṭo vā kiṃ karomīti vā mṛśan /
children.translated_text: When extremely angry, or greatly delighted, or deliberating 'what shall I do?',

children.text: dhāvanvā yatpadaṃ gacchet tatra spandaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ // VSpk_1.22 //
children.translated_text: or running — whatever state one reaches, there <s>spanda</s> is established. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.22)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* sarvatra tāvad upāyamārge samastetaravṛttipraśamapūrvam ekāgrībhavanti yoginaḥ etāsvatikrodhādyavasthāsu svarasata eva samastāparavṛttikṣayamayīṣu yadi spandatattvaviviktaye satatam udyukto jhaṭity antarmukhībhavanti yoginas tatsamīhitam acireṇaiva labhante || VSpkC_1.22:1
children.translated_text: Everywhere on the path of spiritual practice, <s>yogins</s> become one-pointed only after first pacifying all other mental activities equally. But in these states of extreme anger and the like, which are by their own momentum naturally constituted by the cessation of all other mental activities — if [the yogin is] constantly engaged in discerning the <s>spanda</s>-principle, the <s>yogins</s> suddenly become inward-turned and attain the desired [goal] before long.

children.text: * ayoginastvatra mūḍhā eveti tātparyam || VSpkC_1.22:2
children.translated_text: But non-<s>yogins</s> remain deluded in these [states] — this is the purport.

children.text: * tathāhi samanantaravihitadāruṇopaghātaśatrudarśanān marmasparśitattadvacanākarṇanād vā prathamam evonmiṣatsaṃjihīrṣādevatābalād antarmukhībhavadraśmicakro 'tikruddhaḥ ciraprārthitaprāṇeśīvadanendudarśanād eva tatkṣaṇam evonmajjatpūrṇābhilāṣadevatāvaśavikāsitānudhāvatsamastakaraṇacakraḥ prahṛṣṭo vā balavadātatāyibalena sarvato valitatvāt kāndiśīkaḥ kiṃ karomīti mṛśan vikalpayan saṃśayadhārādhirohātmani pade 'nupraviṣṭaḥ kṣīṇasakalālambanavikasatsaṃśayasaṃvinnirālambanīkṛtavṛttiprasaro vā mattavāraṇādyanubadhyamāno dhāvan śarīranirapekṣam eva svātmapravaṇīkṛtetaravṛttiprasaradudyogadevīpreraṇayātitvaritapalāyanakriyāviṣṭo vā evam anyāsv apy evamprāyāsu siṃhājagarādyavalokanajanitamahātrāsādyavasthāsu yad vṛttikṣayātmakaṃ padaṃ gacched adhitiṣṭhet spandatattvaviviktaye satatam udyukto yo yogijanas tasya tatra vṛttikṣayātmake pade 'vasthāviśeṣe spandaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ spandatattvam abhimukhībhūtameva tiṣṭhati || VSpkC_1.22:3
children.translated_text: For thus: one who is extremely angry — from seeing an enemy who has just inflicted terrible harm, or from hearing words that strike at the vital points — by the force of the deity of the desire to seize that first arises, with the circle of rays becoming inward-turned; or one who is greatly delighted — from seeing the face of a long-desired beloved, at that very moment, with the entire circle of organs running after [the experience] as it unfolds, expanded by the force of the deity of the arising complete fulfillment of desire; or one who is bewildered, deliberating 'what shall I do?' — having entered a state whose nature is the ascent of the stream of doubt, with all supports dissolved and the expanding doubt-consciousness rendering the stream of mental activities without support, due to being surrounded on all sides by the force of a powerful assailant; or one who is running — impelled by the deity of exertion whose nature is the stream of [mental] activity directed entirely toward one's own self, regardless of the body, when engaged in the activity of extremely rapid flight from a mad elephant and the like pursuing him. Likewise in other similar states — such as the state of great terror born from seeing a lion, a python, and the like — whatever state constituted by the cessation of [ordinary] mental activities one reaches, for the <s>yogin</s> who is constantly engaged in discerning the <s>spanda</s>-principle, there, in that particular state constituted by the cessation of mental activities, '<s>spanda</s> is established' — the <s>spanda</s>-principle remains turned toward [him].

children.text: * tasmād etad vṛttikṣayapadaṃ saṃcetya jhaṭiti kūrmāṅgasaṃkocayuktyā krodhasaṃśayavṛttīḥ praśamayya mahāvikāsavyāptiyuktyā vā praharṣadhāvanavṛttīr visphāryābhimukhībhūtanijaspandaśaktivimarśavatā yoginā bhayam || VSpkC_1.22:4
children.translated_text: Therefore, having recognized this state of the cessation of mental activities, suddenly, by the method of contracting like a tortoise's limbs, pacifying the mental activities of anger and doubt, or by the method of expansion and pervasion through great unfolding, spreading open the mental activities of delight and running — the <s>yogin</s> who possesses the reflective awareness of the <s>spanda</s>-power that has turned toward him should [realize] —

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrīvijñānabhairave /
children.translated_text: As stated in the revered <s>Vijñānabhairava</s>:

children.text: * kāmakrodhalobhamohamadamātsaryagocare /
children.translated_text: In the domain of desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, and envy,

children.text: * buddhiṃ nistimitāṃ kṛtvā tat tattvam avaśiṣyate || VSpkC_1.22:5
children.translated_text: having made the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) completely still, that reality alone remains.

children.text: * ānande mahati prāpte dṛṣṭe vā bāndhave cirāt || VSpkC_1.22:6
children.translated_text: When great joy has been attained, or when a relative has been seen after a long time,

children.text: * ānandam udgataṃ dhyātvā tallayas tanmanā bhavet || VSpkC_1.22:7
children.translated_text: by meditating on the joy that has arisen, one becomes absorbed in that, with mind united with that.

children.text: * kṣutādyante bhaye śoke gahvare vāraṇadrute /
children.translated_text: At the end of sneezing and the like, in fear, in sorrow, at the edge of a precipice, in flight from an elephant,

children.text: * kutūhale kṣudhādyante brahmasattā samīpagā || VSpkC_1.22:8
children.translated_text: at the onset of curiosity, at the end of hunger and the like — the state of <s>Brahman</s> is near.

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_1.22:9
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * evam etāsv avasthāsūktayuktyā prathamaṃ spandaśaktiṃ pariśīlya tadanu tām evānusaṃdadhat sarvāsvavasthāsu taddārḍhyānupraveśamayīṃ jīvanmuktatām āharet satatodyukta ityupadiśati || VSpkC_1.22:10]
children.translated_text: Thus, having first cultivated the <s>spanda</s>-power through the stated reasoning in these [various] states, and then continuously contemplating it, one should attain the state of living liberation (<s>jīvanmuktatā</s>), which consists of firm entry into that [<s>spanda</s>-power] in all states — [this is taught by the phrase] 'being constantly vigilant' (<s>satatodyukta</s>).
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>]

children.text: yāmavasthāṃ samālambya yadayaṃ mama vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: Having grasped that state, 'Whatever this [<s>spanda</s> principle] will tell me,

children.text: tadavaśyaṃ kariṣye 'hamiti saṃkalpya tiṣṭhati // VSpk_1.23 //
children.translated_text: that I will certainly do' — thus resolving, one remains [steadfast]. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.23)

children.text: tāmāśrityordhvamārgeṇa candrasūryāv ubhāv api /
children.translated_text: Taking refuge in that [state], by the upward path, both moon and sun (<s>candra</s> and <s>sūrya</s>, i.e., <s>apāna</s> and <s>prāṇa</s>),

children.text: sauṣumne'dhvany astamito hitvā brahmāṇḍagocaram // VSpk_1.24 //
children.translated_text: having set in the <s>suṣumṇā</s> channel, abandoning the domain of the <s>brahmāṇḍa</s> (individual body-sphere), (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.24)

children.text: tadā tasminmahāvyomni pralīnaśaśibhāskare /
children.translated_text: then, in that great void (<s>mahāvyoman</s>), when moon and sun have dissolved,

children.text: sauṣuptapadavan mūḍhaḥ prabuddhaḥ syād anāvṛtaḥ // VSpk_1.25 //
children.translated_text: the deluded one (<s>mūḍha</s>) becomes like one in the state of deep sleep (<s>sauṣupta</s>), [but] the awakened one (<s>prabuddha</s>) becomes uncovered (<s>anāvṛta</s>). (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 1.25)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* ayaṃ śaṃkarātmā svabhāvo yan mama vakṣyati abhivyaktaṃ sat yac cidānandaghanam anubhūtapūrvaṃ svarūpaṃ māṃ vimarśayiṣyati tadavaśyamahaṃ kariṣye bahirmukhatāṃ hitvā tatpravaṇa eva bhaviṣyāmi iti saṃkalpya niścitya yām atikrodhādyavasthāsv anubhūtacarīṃ cidānandaghanāṃ spandātmikām avasthām avalambya prāpyatvenābhisaṃdhāya tiṣṭhati śamitavikalpagatim avikalpām avasthām avicalatvena bhajate yo yogī tadīyāṃ tāmavasthāṃ samāśritya candrasūryau apānaḥ prāṇaś cobhāv api hṛdayabhūmau militvā yugapadeva sauṣumne'dhvani brahmanāḍyām ūrdhvamārgeṇodānapathenāstamitaḥ śāmyataḥ kathaṃ brahmāṇḍalakṣaṇaṃ gocaraṃ hitvā brahmabilādhiṣṭhātṛbrahmādhiṣṭhitamaṇḍaṃ muktvā ūrdhvakavāṭāntāṃ dehavyāptiṃ tyaktvā tadā collaṅghitadehavyāptike 'ta eva prakarṣeṇa līnāv uktarūpau śaśibhāskarau yatra tasmin mahāvyomni niḥśeṣavedyopaśamarūpe paramākāśe prāpte 'pi yaḥ śithilaprayatnatayā khecaryādyātmanā guṇādispandaniḥṣyandena vyāmohitatvāt sauṣuptapadavad bhavati sauṣuptena ca suptamapy upalakṣitaṃ tena ca svapnasuṣuptavat yaḥ śūnyādibhūmim evādhitiṣṭhati sa yogī samyaganabhivyaktasvasvabhāvo mūḍha ity ucyate || VSpkC_1.23-35:1
children.translated_text: 'This essential nature, whose self is <s>Śaṃkara</s> — that which will tell me' — that is, that which, being manifest, will cause me to reflect upon the previously experienced essential nature, which is a mass of consciousness-bliss (<s>cidānandaghana</s>) — 'that I will certainly do' — I will abandon outward-directedness and become solely inclined toward that — thus 'resolving,' i.e., determining; having grasped ('taking hold of') the state that has been experienced in the conditions of extreme anger and the like — which is a mass of consciousness-bliss, whose nature is <s>spanda</s> — i.e., having directed oneself toward it as something to be attained; 'one remains' — the <s>yogin</s> who, having pacified the movement of conceptual thought, abides unwaveringly in the concept-free state. Having taken refuge in that state of his, the moon and sun — that is, <s>apāna</s> (downward breath) and <s>prāṇa</s> (upward breath) — both, having merged in the heart-ground, simultaneously by the upward path, the <s>udāna</s> channel, 'set' — i.e., become quiescent — in the <s>suṣumṇā</s> channel, the <s>brahma-nāḍī</s>. How? 'Abandoning the domain characterized as <s>brahmāṇḍa</s>' — i.e., leaving the sphere presided over by <s>Brahmā</s> who presides over the <s>brahma-bila</s> (aperture of <s>Brahmā</s>), relinquishing the pervading of the body up to the upper gate. Then, when the body-pervasion has been transcended, the moon and sun of the aforesaid form, having dissolved therein to a great degree, in that <s>mahāvyoman</s> (great void) — which has the nature of the supreme space (<s>paramākāśa</s>), the form of the complete repose of all that is knowable — even upon reaching [that state], the one who, due to laxity of effort, through the overflow of <s>spanda</s> of the <s>guṇas</s> and the like in the form of <s>khecarī</s> and other [<s>mudrās</s>], becomes bewildered, 'becomes like one in the state of deep sleep' — and by 'deep sleep,' the state of dreaming is also indicated, and by that, [a state] like dream-sleep — the <s>yogin</s> who merely abides in the ground of void (<s>śūnya</s>) and the like, without having properly manifested his own essential nature, is called '<s>mūḍha</s>' (deluded).

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrībhaṭṭakallaṭena /
children.translated_text: As stated by the revered <s>Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa</s>:

children.text: * yāṃ spandātmikām avasthām avalambya /
children.translated_text: 'Having grasped that state, whose nature is <s>spanda</s>,

children.text: * iti yoginaḥ || VSpkC_1.23-35:2
children.translated_text: of the <s>yogin</s>...'

children.text: * iti ca /
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: * yasya svasvabhāvābhivyaktir na samyak vṛttā sa svapnādinā muhyamāno 'prabuddho niruddhaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: 'He whose manifestation of his own essential nature has not occurred properly — he, being deluded by dream and the like, becomes unawakened (<s>aprabuddha</s>), [i.e.,] obstructed.'
Thus.

children.text: * yastu tatrāpi prayatnapāṭavād udyantṛtābalāt kṣaṇamapi na śithilībhavati sa tamasānabhibhūtatvāt cidākāśamayatvenaivāvasthitaḥ prabuddha ucyate ata eva satatodyogavataiva yoginā bhavitavyam ityādiṣṭaṃ gurubhiḥ iti śivam || VSpkC_1.23-35:4]
children.translated_text: But the one who, even there, through the skill of effort and the power of arising (<s>udyantṛtā</s>), does not become slack even for a moment — he, being unconquered by <s>tamas</s> (darkness), abiding as the very nature of consciousness-space (<s>cidākāśa</s>), is called '<s>prabuddha</s>' (awakened). It is for this reason that the teacher has instructed that the <s>yogin</s> must be constantly vigilant. Thus, auspiciousness (<s>śivam</s>).
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: spandakārikā, dvitīyo niḥṣyandaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Spandakārikā</s>, Second Outflow (<s>Dvitīyo Niḥṣyandaḥ</s>)

children.text: tadākramya balaṃ mantrāḥ sarvajñabalaśālinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Taking resort to that power, <s>mantras</s>, endowed with the power of omniscience (<s>sarvajñabala</s>),

children.text: pravartante'dhikārāya karaṇānīva dehinām // VSpk_2.1 //
children.translated_text: proceed to carry out their functions — like the organs (<s>karaṇas</s>) of embodied beings. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 2.1)

children.text: tatraiva sampralīyante śāntarūpā nirañjanāḥ /
children.translated_text: They dissolve back into that very [source], their forms at peace, untainted (<s>nirañjana</s>);

children.text: sahārādhakacittena tenaite śivadharmiṇaḥ // VSpk_2.2 //
children.translated_text: together with the mind of the worshipper — therefore, these have the nature of <s>Śiva</s> (<s>śivadharmiṇaḥ</s>). (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 2.2)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* tat spandatattvātmakaṃ balaṃ prāṇarūpaṃ vīryamākramya abhedena āśrayatayāvaṣṭabhya bhagavanto 'nantavyomavyāpyādayo mantrāḥ sarvajñabalena sarvajñatvādisāmarthyena ślāghamānā jṛmbhamāṇā adhikārāya dehināṃ pravartante sṛṣṭisaṃhāratirodhānānugrahādi kurvantītyarthaḥ || VSpkC_2.1:1
children.translated_text: 'That' — taking resort to the power in the form of vitality (<s>vīrya</s>) whose nature is <s>prāṇa</s>, whose essence is the <s>spanda</s> reality, in non-difference — i.e., taking hold of it as their support — the blessed <s>mantras</s> such as <s>Anantavyomavyāpī</s> and others, proud of and flourishing with the power of omniscience, i.e., the capacity for omniscience and the like, 'proceed to carry out their functions' — they perform creation, dissolution, concealment, grace, and the like for embodied beings — this is the meaning.

children.text: * sarvajñaśabdo bhāvapradhānaḥ sarvakartṛtvādy upalakṣayati || VSpkC_2.1:2
children.translated_text: The word '<s>sarvajña</s>' (omniscient) has its primary sense in the state [of being]; it indicates by implication also universal agency (<s>sarvakartṛtva</s>) and the like.

children.text: * yathā dehināṃ karaṇāny upapāditadṛśā tadbalamākramya viṣayaprakāśādau pravartante iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ || VSpkC_2.1:3
children.translated_text: Just as the organs of embodied beings, taking resort to that power with their capacity for perception already endowed [by it], proceed to illuminate objects and the like — this is the illustration.

children.text: * tathā nirañjanāḥ kṛtakṛtyatvān nivṛttādhikāramalāḥ śāntaviśiṣṭavācakātmasvarūpās tatraiva spandātmake bale samyagabhedāpattyā prakarṣeṇāpunarāvṛttyā līyante adhikamalānmucyante ārādhakacittena upāsakalokasaṃvedanena saha || VSpkC_2.1:4
children.translated_text: Similarly, 'untainted' (<s>nirañjana</s>) — having fulfilled their purpose, having retired from the impurity of their office, with their forms of distinct <s>vācaka</s> (designating sounds) at peace — they dissolve back in that very <s>spanda</s>-power properly, by the arrival of non-difference, thoroughly, never to return — i.e., they are freed from their further impurities — together with the mind of the worshipper, i.e., together with the consciousness of the devotee.

children.text: * yathoktam /
children.translated_text: As stated:

children.text: * anugṛhyāṇusaṃghātaṃ yātāḥ padam anāmayam || VSpkC_2.1:5
children.translated_text: 'Having graced the assemblage of limited selves (<s>aṇu</s>), [the <s>mantras</s>] have gone to the state that is free from disease.'

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_2.1:6
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * yataśca tata evoditāstadbalena visṛṣṭās tatraiva līyante tenaite mantramantreśvarādayaḥ śivasya parameśvarasya sambandhī dharmaḥ svabhāvo vidyate yeṣāṃ te tathā sāmānyaspandasārā ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_2.1:7
children.translated_text: And since, having arisen from that very [source] and having been sent forth by that power, they dissolve back into that very [source] — therefore these <s>mantras</s>, <s>mantreśvaras</s>, and the rest have <s>Śiva</s>'s nature (<s>dharma</s>), i.e., their essential quality, as their own: they are of the essence of the universal <s>spanda</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: * nanu karaṇānāṃ mantrāṇāṃ ca tat udayādau tulye kimiti karaṇāni na sarvajñādirūpāṇi || VSpkC_2.1:8
children.translated_text: But [objection]: since the organs and <s>mantras</s> are alike in arising [from that source] and the like, why are the organs not of the form of omniscience and the like?

children.text: * ucyate parameśvaro māyāśaktyā śarīrakaraṇāni bhedamayāni nirmimīte vidyāśaktyā tv ākāśīyavicitravācakaparāmarśaśarīrān mantrān || VSpkC_2.1:9
children.translated_text: It is said: the <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord), by his <s>Māyā</s>-power, creates the body and organs, which are pervaded by differentiation; but by his <s>Vidyā</s>-power, he [creates] <s>mantras</s>, whose bodies are the various <s>vācaka</s> (designating) reflective awarenesses (<s>parāmarśa</s>) of the spatial [nature].

children.text: * vācakasya māyāpade 'pi || VSpkC_2.1:10
children.translated_text: Even in the domain of <s>Māyā</s>, the <s>vācaka</s> (designating [awareness]) —

children.text: * ghaṭo 'yam ityadhyavasā nāmarūpātirekiṇī /
children.translated_text: 'The determinate cognition "This is a pot" — the transcendent form of reflective awareness (<s>nāmarūpa</s>),

children.text: * pareśaśaktirātmeva bhāsate na tv idaṃtayā || VSpkC_2.1:11
children.translated_text: the power of the Supreme Lord — shines as the very self, not as mere "this-ness" (<s>idaṃtā</s>).'

children.text: * iti pratyabhijñoktanītyā pramātṛbhūmyanatikrānter na śarīrapuryaṣṭakādivadbodhasaṃkocakatvam astīti yuktamevaiṣāṃ sarvajñatvādi || VSpkC_2.1:12
children.translated_text: — according to the method stated in the <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>, since [the <s>vācaka</s>] does not transcend the ground of the knowing subject (<s>pramātṛ</s>), it does not have the capacity to contract consciousness as the body, <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body), and the like do. Therefore, their omniscience and the like is entirely proper.

children.text: * etac ca /
children.translated_text: And this [has been shown in]:

children.text: * bhede tv ekarase bhāte || VSpkC_2.1:13
children.translated_text: 'But when difference shines as of one taste (<s>ekarasa</s>)...'

children.text: * iti śrīpratyabhijñākārikāṭīkāyāṃ vitatya darśitam || VSpkC_2.1:14
children.translated_text: — in the commentary on the <s>Pratyabhijñā Kārikās</s>, this has been shown at length.

children.text: * evaṃ vidyāpadāvasthitasṛṣṭyādikāryanantabhaṭṭārakādyapekṣayaitad vyākhyeyam || VSpkC_2.1:15
children.translated_text: Thus, this is to be commented upon with reference to <s>Ananta Bhaṭṭāraka</s> and others who are established in the <s>Vidyā</s> level and whose function is creation and the like.

children.text: * tathā dīkṣādipravṛttānām ācāryādīnāṃ karaṇarūpāḥ sarve mantrās tatspandatattvarūpaṃ balam ākramya anuprāṇakatvena avaṣṭabhya ācāryādīnām eva sambandhinārādhakacittena saha mokṣabhogasādhanādyadhikārāya pravartante tatraiva śāntavācakaśabdātmakaśarīrarūpā ata eva ca nirañjanāḥ śuddhāḥ samyak pralīyante viśrāmyanti || VSpkC_2.1:16
children.translated_text: Similarly, all <s>mantras</s>, which are in the form of instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>) for preceptors (<s>ācāryas</s>) and others engaged in <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and the like, taking resort to that power whose form is the <s>spanda</s> reality — i.e., taking hold of it as that which animates — proceed, together with the mind of the worshipper connected with the <s>ācāryas</s> themselves, to carry out their functions regarding <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), <s>bhoga</s> (enjoyment), and the means thereof. In that very [source], having the form of bodies consisting of the pacified <s>vācaka</s> sounds — and being therefore 'untainted,' i.e., pure — they properly dissolve, i.e., they come to rest.

children.text: * atra vyākhyāne sahārādhakacittena iti pūrvaślokena yojyam || VSpkC_2.1:17
children.translated_text: In this interpretation, 'together with the mind of the worshipper' is to be connected with the preceding verse.

children.text: * evaṃ ca mantrāṇāmudayapralayakoṭivyāpi pravṛttāv api bhittibhūtamiti abhihitam || VSpkC_2.1:18
children.translated_text: And thus, it has been stated that [the <s>spanda</s> reality] serves as the screen (<s>bhitti</s>) even for the activity of <s>mantras</s> that pervades the extremes of arising and dissolution.

children.text: * evaṃ ca daśāṣṭādaśādibhedena bhinne śaive mantrāṇāṃ spandatattvasārataivetyuktaṃ bhavati || VSpkC_2.1:19
children.translated_text: And thus, it is stated that even when <s>Śaiva</s> [traditions] differ as having ten, eighteen, and other divisions, the <s>mantras</s> have the <s>spanda</s> reality as their essence.

children.text: * evaṃ mantramantreśvarādirūpā śuddhābhimatā sṛṣṭiḥ śivasvabhāveti pratipādyādhunā aśuddhābhimatāpi sā māyādirūpā śivasvarūpaiva iti upapādayan śrīmataśāstrādirahasyadṛṣṭim api upakṣipati || VSpkC_2.1:20]
children.translated_text: Having thus established that the creation considered 'pure' — in the form of <s>mantras</s>, <s>mantreśvaras</s>, and the like — is of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, now, in order to demonstrate that even what is considered 'impure' creation — in the form of <s>Māyā</s> and the like — is also of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, he also introduces the esoteric perspective of the sacred scripture.
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: yasmātsarvamayo jīvaḥ sarvabhāvasamudbhavāt /
children.translated_text: Since the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) is constituted of everything, because of its origination from all states of being,

children.text: tatsaṃvedanarūpeṇa tādātmyapratipattitaḥ // VSpk_2.3 //
children.translated_text: and because of its apprehension of identity through the form of experience of that [totality], (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 2.3)

children.text: tasmācchabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: therefore, in the contemplation of word, meaning, and thought, there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: bhoktaiva bhogyabhāvena sadā sarvatra saṃsthitaḥ // VSpk_2.4 //
children.translated_text: the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) himself is always established everywhere in the form of the experienced (<s>bhogya</s>). (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 2.4)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* yato jīvo grāhakaḥ sarvamayaḥ śivavad viśvarūpaḥ tena hetunā śabdeṣu vācakeṣu artheṣu vācyeṣu cintāsu vikalpajñānādirūpāsu ādimadhyāntarūpā sāvasthā nāsti yā śivo na bhavati sarvameva śivasvarūpam ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_2.3-4:1
children.translated_text: Since the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), i.e., the apprehending subject (<s>grāhaka</s>), is constituted of everything — of the nature of the universe like <s>Śiva</s> — for that reason, in words, i.e., <s>vācakas</s> (designators), in meanings, i.e., <s>vācyas</s> (designated objects), and in contemplations, i.e., in the form of conceptual cognition and the like — there is no state of beginning, middle, and end that is not <s>Śiva</s>. Everything whatsoever is of the nature of <s>Śiva</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: * yataś caivamato bhoktaiva cidātmā grāhako bhogyabhāvena dehanīlādirūpeṇa sadā nityaṃ sarvatra vicitratattvabhuvanādipade samyaganūnādhikatayā sthitaḥ na tu bhogyaṃ nāma kiṃcidbhoktur bhinnam asti || VSpkC_2.3-4:2
children.translated_text: And since it is so, therefore the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) — the knowing subject (<s>grāhaka</s>) whose nature is consciousness (<s>cidātman</s>) — is always, i.e., eternally, established in the form of the experienced (<s>bhogya</s>), i.e., in the form of body, blue, and the like, everywhere — in the domain of the various <s>tattvas</s> (realities) and worlds — completely, neither more nor less. There is nothing called 'the experienced' (<s>bhogya</s>) that is separate from the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>).

children.text: * jīva ityupakramya śiva ityupasaṃhāreṇa jīvaśivayorvāstavo na ko 'pi bhedaḥ iti dehādyavasthāsu na kāsucid apyapūrṇamanyatā mantavyā api tu cidghanaśivasvabhāvataiveti bhaṅgyopadiśati || VSpkC_2.3-4:3
children.translated_text: By beginning with '<s>jīva</s>' (individual soul) and concluding with '<s>Śiva</s>' — [the author] indirectly instructs that there is, in reality, no difference whatsoever between <s>jīva</s> and <s>Śiva</s>. Therefore, in none of the states such as embodiment and the like should one consider oneself incomplete; rather, one's nature is nothing other than <s>Śiva</s>, [who is] a mass of consciousness (<s>cidghana</s>) — this he teaches by suggestion.

children.text: * yathoktam śarīramapi ye ṣaṭtriṃśattattvamayaṃ śivarūpatayā paśyanti arcayanti ca te sidhyanti ghaṭādikam iva tathābhiniviśya paśyanti arcayanti ca te 'pīti nāstyatra vivādaḥ iti śrīpratyabhijñāṭīkāyām || VSpkC_2.3-4:4
children.translated_text: As stated [in the <s>Pratyabhijñā-ṭīkā</s>]: 'Those who see the body — which consists of the thirty-six principles — as having the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, and worship it [accordingly], they attain perfection. And those who view and worship it as [mere] pot and the like, having fixated upon it thus — they too [attain accordingly].' Thus [says] the revered <s>Pratyabhijñā-ṭīkā</s> — there is no dispute in this.

children.text: * bhaṭṭaśrīvāmanenāpyuktam /
children.translated_text: The revered <s>Bhaṭṭa Vāmana</s> has also said:

children.text: * ālambya saṃvidaṃ yasmāt saṃvedyaṃ na svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Since the knowable, by its very nature, [exists only] by relying on awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) —

children.text: * tasmātsaṃviditaṃ sarvamiti saṃvinmayo bhavet || VSpkC_2.3-4:5
children.translated_text: therefore everything is [something] known; hence [everything] is of the nature of awareness.'

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_2.3-4:6
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * kasmāt jīvaḥ sarvamayaḥ ityatra hetuḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ samudbhavād utpattihetutvāt apādānabhāvapradhānaśca nirdeśaḥ || VSpkC_2.3-4:7
children.translated_text: Why is the individual self (<s>jīva</s>) made of everything? The reason for this is: because of being the source of the arising of all existents — i.e., because of being the cause of their origination. And the expression has the predominant sense of the ablative (<s>apādāna</s>).

children.text: * pramātṛmitimānameyamayabhedajātasya te vihāra iha hetutāṃ samupayāti yasmāt tvayi /
children.translated_text: 'The sport of the multitude of divisions consisting of the knower, the measure, the means of measuring, and the measurable — because this has the nature of causality within you —

children.text: * nivṛttavivṛtau kvacit tad apayāti tenādhvādhunā nayena punarīkṣyate jagati jātucitkenacit || VSpkC_2.3-4:8
children.translated_text: at some point, in cessation and manifestation, that withdraws; therefore, the path is never seen again in the world by anyone [in the ordinary sense].'

children.text: * iti śrījñānagarbhastotroktanītyā saṃvidyeva prasṛtāyāṃ jagataḥ sadbhāvāt sarvabhāvasamudbhavatvaṃ jīvasya yataśca jīvādeva udayati viśvamato'yaṃ sarvamayo viśvaśaktiriti yāvat || VSpkC_2.3-4:9
children.translated_text: According to the principle stated in the revered <s>Jñānagarbha-stotra</s>, because the world has its existence only when awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) has expanded, the individual self's being the source of all existents [is established]. And because the universe arises from the individual self itself, therefore this [self] is made of everything — that is, it is the universal power (<s>viśvaśakti</s>).

children.text: * nirṇītaṃ caitad dvitīyasūtravṛttau || VSpkC_2.3-4:10
children.translated_text: And this has been determined in the commentary on the second <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: * sarvamayatve hetvantaramāha tatsaṃvedana ityardhena || VSpkC_2.3-4:11
children.translated_text: He states another reason for [the self's] being made of everything, in the half-verse 'by the awareness of that'.

children.text: * tasya sarvasya nīlasukhāderyatsaṃvedanaṃ prakāśastena rūpeṇa svabhāvena tādātmyapratipatteḥ sarvamayatvasyopalambhāt || VSpkC_2.3-4:12
children.translated_text: By the awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>), the illumination, of all that — blue, pleasure, and the like — because of the apprehension of identity with that nature, the state of being made of everything is perceived.

children.text: * evamanena ślokadvayena rahasyacaryāḥ sarvabhedapādaponmūlopapattiparighaṭitāś ca jñānopadeśakathāḥ prathamacaramasūtrābhyāṃ mahārthatattvaṃ jāgradādisūtreṇa ṣaḍardhaparamārthaḥ tadākramya ity anena sarvopāsāsāratetyādyupakṣiptam iti spandatattvenaiva viśvopadeśāḥ svīkṛtāḥ || VSpkC_2.3-4:13
children.translated_text: Thus, by these two verses, the esoteric practices (<s>rahasyacaryā</s>), the discourses of knowledge-instruction fitted together with the uprooting of all foundations of differentiation, the great truth (<s>mahārtha-tattva</s>) through the first and last <s>sūtras</s>, the sixfold ultimate meaning through the <s>sūtra</s> on waking and the like, [and] what is indicated by 'the essence of all worship' etc. — all the teachings of the universe have been encompassed through the <s>spanda</s> principle alone.

children.text: * athaitatpratipattisārataiva mokṣa ityādiśati || VSpkC_2.3-4:14]
children.translated_text: Now he teaches that the very essence of this realization is liberation:
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: iti vā yasya saṃvittiḥ krīḍātvenākhilaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: Or, he whose awareness [perceives] the entire world as play (<s>krīḍā</s>) —

children.text: sa paśyansatataṃ yukto jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ // VSpk_2.5 //
children.translated_text: he, constantly seeing [thus], is [truly] united (<s>yukta</s>) — he is liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>), without doubt. (2.5)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* vāśabdaḥ prathamaniḥṣyandoktanimīlanasamādhiprakāraṃ vikalpayan asyāḥ samāpatter durlabhatāṃ dhvanayati || VSpkC_2.5:1
children.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>), by offering an alternative to the type of closed-eye <s>samādhi</s> described in the first outflow, suggests the difficulty of attaining that [other type of] absorption.

children.text: * tenāyamarthaḥ īdṛśī tāvatsaṃvittiḥ durlabhā yasya kasyacid evāpaścimajanmano bhavati so 'khilaṃ jagatkrīḍātvena paśyan nijasaṃvidunmeṣanimeṣābhyāṃ sṛjan saṃharaṃś ca /
children.translated_text: Hence the meaning is: such awareness is difficult to attain; it arises only for some person in his final birth. He, seeing the entire world as play — creating and dissolving it through the opening and closing of his own awareness —

children.text: * mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate || VSpkC_2.5:2
children.translated_text: 'Those who, with minds absorbed in me, ever-united, worship me' —

children.text: * iti sthityā satatasamāviṣṭo mahāyogī jīvann eva prāṇādimān api vijñānāgninirdagdhāśeṣabandhano dehapāte tu śiva eva jīvaṃścedṛṅmukta eva na tu kathaṃcid api baddhaḥ || VSpkC_2.5:3
children.translated_text: in accordance with this, the great <s>yogin</s>, constantly absorbed [in <s>Śiva</s>], even while living, even while possessing <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, having had all bonds burnt by the fire of knowledge — at the fall of the body, he is <s>Śiva</s> himself. But while living, such a one is liberated indeed — and in no way whatsoever is he bound.

children.text: * na saṃśayaḥ ityanena idaṃ dhvanayati dīkṣādinā gurupratyayato muktiḥ īdṛśāt tu jñānāt samācārādvā svapratyayata eveti || VSpkC_2.5:4
children.translated_text: 'Without doubt' — by this he suggests: through initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and the like, liberation [comes] from the conviction [given by] the <s>Guru</s>; but from such knowledge or from [the corresponding] practice, it comes from one's own direct conviction.

children.text: * iyameva mahāsamāpattiḥ sādhakācāryādīnām abhīṣṭaprāptihetuḥ iti ślokadvayenāha || VSpkC_2.5:5]
children.translated_text: This very great absorption (<s>mahāsamāpatti</s>) is the cause of attaining the desired [fruit] for practitioners (<s>sādhakas</s>), preceptors (<s>ācāryas</s>), and others — this he states in two verses:
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s> commentary:]

children.text: ayamevodayastasya dhyeyasya dhyāyicetasi /
children.translated_text: This alone is the arising, in the mind of the meditator, of the object of meditation —

children.text: tadātmatāsamāpattir icchataḥ sādhakasya yā // VSpk_2.6 //
children.translated_text: the absorption into identity with that (<s>tadātmatā-samāpatti</s>), which [arises] for the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) who wills it. (2.6)

children.text: yamevāmṛtaprāptir ayam evātmano grahaḥ /
children.translated_text: This alone is the attainment of the nectar [of immortality]; this alone is the grasping of the Self;

children.text: iyaṃ nirvāṇadīkṣā ca śivasadbhāvadāyinī // VSpk_2.7 //
children.translated_text: this is the initiation into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, which bestows the true being of <s>Śiva</s>. (2.7)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
children.translated_text: [<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s> commentary:]

children.text: * iha śivo bhūtvā śivaṃ yajet iti yad udghoṣyate tatra dhyāyinaś cetasi saṃvedane tasyeti na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ iti pratipāditaśivasvabhāvasya dhyeyasya anyasya vā kasyacit tattatsiddhihetor mantradevatāviśeṣasya ayam evodayaḥ prakaṭībhāvaḥ yā sādhakasya dhyāturācāryādeḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in accordance with the proclamation 'having become <s>Śiva</s>, one should worship <s>Śiva</s>' — in the awareness, the mind, of the meditator, this alone is the arising, the manifestation, of the object of meditation — whose <s>Śiva</s>-nature has been established [by the verse] 'there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>' — or of any particular <s>mantra</s>-deity that is the cause of the particular <s>siddhi</s> [desired] — [this manifestation occurs] for the practitioner, the meditator, the preceptor, and so on.

children.text: * tasmācchabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ || VSpkC_2.6-7:1
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, in the contemplation of words and objects, there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>' —

children.text: * iti pratipāditarūpā tadātmatāsamāpattiḥ śivaikyāveśo na tu pañcavaktrādervyatiriktasyākārasya darśanaṃ na tu niścayamātreṇa tadātmatāsamāpattiḥ api tu icchato 'vikalpaviśvāhaṃtātmakaśivaikyarūpecchāparāmarśādhirūḍhasya || VSpkC_2.6-7:2
children.translated_text: in accordance with this established principle, the 'absorption into identity with that' (<s>tadātmatā-samāpatti</s>) is the immersion into oneness with <s>Śiva</s> — not the vision of a [particular] form different [from oneself], such as the five-faced [<s>Śiva</s>] and the like; nor is the absorption into identity [achieved] merely by determination alone; rather, it is for one who wills it — one who has ascended to the reflective awareness of the will whose form is oneness with <s>Śiva</s> as the non-conceptual, universal 'I'-ness.

children.text: * etad uktaṃ bhavati ahameva tatsaṃvedanarūpeṇa tādātmyapratipattito viśvaśarīraś cidānandaghanaḥ śiva iti saṃkalpo yasyāvikalpaśeṣībhūtatvena phalati tasya dhyeyamantradevatādi kiṃ na nāma abhimukhībhavati sarvasyaitadadvayaprathālagnatvāt || VSpkC_2.6-7:3
children.translated_text: What has been said amounts to this: the resolution (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) 'I myself, through the realization of identity in the form of that awareness, am <s>Śiva</s> — the universal-bodied, the dense mass of consciousness and bliss' — for one in whom this [resolution] bears fruit by becoming residual-free as a non-conceptual [reality], what object of meditation, what <s>mantra</s>-deity, does not present itself to him? — since everything is attached to this non-dual manifestation.

children.text: * yathoktamasmatparameṣṭhipādaiḥ /
children.translated_text: As stated by our supreme master (<s>Parameṣṭhin</s>):

children.text: * sākṣādbhavanmaye nātha sarvasmin bhuvanāntare /
children.translated_text: 'O Lord, since you directly pervade the entire range of worlds —

children.text: * kiṃ na bhaktimatāṃ kṣetraṃ mantraḥ kvaiṣāṃ na sidhyati || VSpkC_2.6-7:4
children.translated_text: what is not a [sacred] field for the devoted? Where does their <s>mantra</s> not achieve perfection?'

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_2.6-7:5
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * iyameva ca samāpattiḥ paramādvayarūpasyāmṛtasya prāptiḥ anyasmiṃs tv amṛte katipayakālaśarīradārḍhyadāyini prāpte'pi sādhakairmaraṇamavaśyamavāpyata evety evakārāśayaḥ || VSpkC_2.6-7:6
children.translated_text: And this very absorption is the attainment of the nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) that is the supreme non-dual [reality]. But when another [kind of] nectar is obtained — one that gives firmness to the body for a limited time — practitioners still inevitably encounter death. Such is the import of the word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>).

children.text: * evaṃ sarvatrānenaivāśayena śrīsvacchande sthūladṛṣṭyāmṛtaprāptiprakaraṇe /
children.translated_text: Thus, everywhere with this very import, in the revered <s>Svacchanda</s> [Tantra], in the section on the attainment of nectar from the gross perspective —

children.text: * naiva cāmṛtayogena kālamṛtyujayo bhavet || VSpkC_2.6-7:7
children.translated_text: 'Not indeed by the yoga of [physical] nectar is the conquest of time and death achieved' —

children.text: * ityuktyopasaṃhṛtya tāttvikas tatprāptiprakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: having concluded [the gross approach] with this statement, the true method of its attainment [is given]:

children.text: * athavā paratattvasthaḥ sarvakālairna bādhyate || VSpkC_2.6-7:8
children.translated_text: 'Or rather, one who is established in the supreme principle is not afflicted by any time' —

children.text: * ityādinā || VSpkC_2.6-7:9
children.translated_text: and so on.

children.text: * sarvaṃ śivaśaktimayaṃ smaret || VSpkC_2.6-7:10
children.translated_text: 'One should remember everything as pervaded by <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>' —

children.text:
* iti madhyena /
* jīvann eva vimukto 'sau yasyeyaṃ bhāvanā sadā /
* yaḥ śivaṃ bhāvayen nityaṃ na kālaḥ kalayettu tam /
children.translated_text: he who constantly contemplates <s>Śiva</s> — time does not consume him;

children.text: * yogī svacchandayogena svacchandagaticāriṇā /
children.translated_text: the <s>yogin</s>, through the <s>yoga</s> of <s>Svacchanda</s> (the Autonomous One), moving with the movement of <s>Svacchanda</s> —

children.text: * sa svacchandapade yuktaḥ svacchandasamatāṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: he, united with the state of <s>Svacchanda</s>, attains equality with <s>Svacchanda</s>;

children.text: * svacchandaścaiva svacchandaḥ svacchando vicaret sadā || VSpkC_2.6-7:11
children.translated_text: <s>Svacchanda</s> [becomes] indeed <s>Svacchanda</s>; he moves about always as <s>Svacchanda</s> (the Autonomous One).'

children.text: * ityanena sahajasaṃdarbheṇa sapraśaṃsaṃ paścādupadiṣṭaḥ || VSpkC_2.6-7:12
children.translated_text: By this natural composition, [the state of liberation] has been taught at the end with praise.

children.text: * ayamevātmano graho jñānaṃ yaducyate ātmā jñātavya iti tatredam eva sarvajñasarvakartṛsvatantraśivasvarūpatayā pratyabhijñānam ātmano jñānaṃ na tu /
children.translated_text: 'This alone is the grasping of the Self' — the knowledge that is spoken of [in scripture] as 'the Self is to be known' — here, this very recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) of [oneself] as having the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, who is omniscient, omnipotent, and autonomous — this is the knowledge of the Self. Not, however, [that stated by]

children.text: * puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam || VSpkC_2.6-7:13
children.translated_text: '<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this' —

children.text: * iti śrutyantaviduktam /
children.translated_text: as stated by the <s>Vedānta</s> proponents.

children.text: * ta ātmopāsakāḥ sarve na gacchanti paraṃ padam || VSpkC_2.6-7:14
children.translated_text: 'Those worshippers of the [mere] Self — they do not reach the supreme state' —

children.text: * ityāmnāyokteḥ || VSpkC_2.6-7:15
children.translated_text: because of this scriptural declaration.

children.text: * tathā dīkṣāvasare yojanikādyarthamayameva śiṣyātmano'nugrahaḥ imāmeva samāpattiṃ vidvānācāryaḥ śiṣyātmānaṃ śive yojayannācāryo bhavatītyarthaḥ || VSpkC_2.6-7:16
children.translated_text: Similarly, at the occasion of initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>), for the purpose of <s>yojanikā</s> and the like, this alone is the grace [bestowed upon] the disciple's self — the learned preceptor (<s>ācārya</s>), uniting the disciple's self with <s>Śiva</s> through this very absorption, becomes [truly] a preceptor — this is the meaning.

children.text: * iyaṃ svapratyayasiddhā putrakādeḥ śivātmanaḥ sadbhāvasya pāramārthikasvarūpasya dāyinī nirvāṇadīkṣā || VSpkC_2.6-7:17
children.translated_text: This <s>nirvāṇa-dīkṣā</s> (initiation into liberation), established by one's own direct conviction, bestows the true being — the ultimate essential nature — of <s>Śiva</s>-Self for the <s>putraka</s> (son-initiate) and others.

children.text: * yathoktam /
children.translated_text: As stated:

children.text: * evaṃ yo veda tattvena tasya nirvāṇadāyinī /
children.translated_text: 'For one who knows thus in reality, the initiation that bestows <s>nirvāṇa</s> —

children.text: * dīkṣā bhavatyasaṃdigdhā tilājyāhutivarjitā || VSpkC_2.6-7:18
children.translated_text: that occurs without doubt, devoid of sesame, ghee, and oblations.'

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_2.6-7:19
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * hautrī dīkṣāpi dīkṣaiva tatra mā bhūt kasyacid anāśvāsa ityāśayenātraivakāro na kṛtaḥ śrīmahāgurupravareṇeti śivam || VSpkC_2.6-7:20]
children.translated_text: The word 'alone' (<s>eva</s>) was not placed here [in the verse] by the revered foremost great <s>Guru</s>, with the intention that: 'let no one lose confidence [thinking] that the ritual initiation (<s>hautrī dīkṣā</s>) is also a [valid] initiation' — and so, auspiciousness (<s>śivam</s>).
through this middle [portion]. 'He is liberated even while living, for whom this contemplation is constant;

children.text: spandakārikā, tṛtīyo niḥṣyandaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Spandakārikā</s>, Third Outflow (<s>Tṛtīyo Niḥṣyandaḥ</s>)

children.text: yathecchābhyarthito dhātā jāgrato 'rthān hṛdi sthitān /
children.translated_text: Just as the bestower (<s>dhātā</s>), entreated by desire, for one who is awake, the objects established in the heart —

children.text: somasūryodayaṃ kṛtvā sampādayati dehinaḥ // VSpk_3.1 //
children.translated_text: causing the arising of moon and sun, accomplishes [them] for the embodied being; (3.1)

children.text: tathā svapne'pyabhīṣṭārthān praṇayasyānatikramāt /
children.translated_text: so too in dream, the desired objects, because of not transgressing one's earnest desire —

children.text: nityaṃ sphuṭataraṃ madhye sthito'vaśyaṃ prakāśayet // VSpk_3.2 //
children.translated_text: [the bestower,] stationed in the center, always more clearly, will certainly illuminate [them]. (3.2)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* dhatte sarvamātmanīti dhātā śaṃkarātmā svabhāvaḥ sa yathā jāgrataḥ jāgarāyāmabhivyaktasvasvātantryasya dehino dehabhūmikāmeva prakaṭībhūtapiṇḍasthajñānasya yoginaḥ sambandhinyecchayābhyarthito 'ntarmukhasvarūpavimarśabalena prasādito hṛdi cetasi sthitānarthāniti bindunādādijñānapuraḥ kṣobhapratibhācālanabodhastobhajñānasaṃcārādiprayojanāni sampādayati || VSpkC_3.1-2:1
children.translated_text: He who holds everything in Himself — the Supporter (<s>dhātā</s>), whose nature is <s>Śaṃkara</s>, that own essential nature — just as, for one who is awake — for a <s>yogin</s> in the waking state, with his own autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>) manifest, in the plane of the body, whose knowledge established in the body (<s>piṇḍastha-jñāna</s>) has become apparent — when entreated by the will of a connected [person], propitiated by the power of inward-turned self-awareness, [the Supporter] who is established in the heart, in the mind, accomplishes the purposes of knowledge such as <s>bindu</s>, <s>nāda</s>, and the rest — namely, the purposes of agitation of creative insight (<s>pratibhā</s>), movement, awakening, astonishment, knowledge-transmission, and the like. (3.1-2:1)

children.text: * kathaṃ somasūryayor jñānakriyāśaktyor udayaṃ kṛtvā jñānaśaktyā bhāsyamānaṃ hi tattatkriyāśaktyonmīlyate || VSpkC_3.1-2:2
children.translated_text: How? Having brought about the arising of <s>Soma</s> and <s>Sūrya</s> — the powers of knowledge and action — what is illuminated by the knowledge-power is unfolded by the action-power. (3.1-2:2)

children.text: * samāveśonmiṣatpratibhātmakamūlāvaṣṭambhayuktisphāritajñānakriyāvyāptisārasavyetaramarīcivisphāraṇakrameṇa tattadvedhasaṃkramaṇādi sampādayati yogiśarīrānupraviṣṭaḥ parameśvaraḥ || VSpkC_3.1-2:3
children.translated_text: The supreme Lord, who has entered the body of the <s>yogin</s>, by the method of expanding the left and right rays — whose essence is the pervasion of knowledge and action expanded through the technique of grounding in the root [experience] whose nature is the creative insight (<s>pratibhā</s>) that flashes forth in <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption) — accomplishes the penetration of various [planes] and the like. (3.1-2:3)

children.text: * yathā caivaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: And just as this is so, likewise:

children.text: * anāgatāyāṃ nidrāyāṃ vinaṣṭe bāhyagocare /
children.translated_text: 'When sleep has not yet arrived and the external sense-field has disappeared,

children.text: * sāvasthā manasā gamyā parā devī prakāśate || VSpkC_3.1-2:4
children.translated_text: that state, attainable by the mind, is where the supreme Goddess (<s>parā devī</s>) shines forth.' (3.1-2:4)

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_3.1-2:5
* pīnāṃ ca durbalāṃ śaktiṃ dhyātvā dvādaśagocare /
children.translated_text: 'Having meditated upon the power — [alternately] full and subtle — in the domain of the twelve [sense-loci],

children.text: * praviśya hṛdaye dhyāyan svapnasvātantryam āpnuyāt || VSpkC_3.1-2:6
children.translated_text: entering the heart through meditation, one attains freedom in the dream state.' (3.1-2:6)

children.text: * iti sampradāyasthityā vamanagrāsasaktatadubhayavisargāraṇicitiśaktiparāmarśamukhena nityaṃ praṇayam anatikrāmato bhagavatprārthanāparasya yoganidrārūḍhasya sphuṭataram anācchāditarūpatayā madhye sauṣumnadhāmani sthito dhātā svapne 'pyabhīṣṭān evāṇavaśāktaśāmbhavasamāveśādīn anyān api samāveśābhyāsarasonmṛṣṭamatimukurasya jijñāsitān arthān avaśyaṃ prakaṭīkaroti nāsya yoginaḥ svapnasuṣuptayor vyāmoho bhavatītyarthaḥ || VSpkC_3.1-2:7
children.translated_text: Thus, by the method of the tradition, through the reflective awareness of the <s>citi-śakti</s> (consciousness-power) that is the substrate of emission in the forms of vomiting forth (<s>vamana</s>), devouring (<s>grāsa</s>), and both together — for one who never transgresses his constant devotion, who is intent upon the worship of the Lord, who has ascended to yogic sleep (<s>yoganidrā</s>) — the Supporter (<s>dhātā</s>), standing in the <s>suṣumnā</s> channel in the center with His form most clearly unconcealed, even in the dream state, certainly manifests the desired [experiences] such as <s>āṇava</s>, <s>śākta</s>, and <s>śāmbhava samāveśa</s> (absorptions), and also other objects of inquiry for [the yogin] whose mirror of mind has been polished by the relish of the practice of absorption. The meaning is: for this <s>yogin</s>, there is no delusion in dream and deep sleep. (3.1-2:7)

children.text: * svapnena sauṣuptam apyupalakṣitam || VSpkC_3.1-2:8
children.translated_text: By 'dream,' deep sleep is also indicated by implication. (3.1-2:8)

children.text: * atrābhīṣṭārthaprakāśe āvṛttyā ayameva hetuḥ praṇayasya prārthanāyā antarmukhasvarūpapariśīlanopāsāsaṃpādyasya māyākāluṣyopaśamalakṣaṇasya prasādasya bhagavatānatikramāt || VSpkC_3.1-2:9
children.translated_text: Regarding the manifestation of desired objects, this alone is the repeated cause: because [the yogin] does not transgress the grace (<s>prasāda</s>) of the Lord — the grace characterized by the subsidence of the turbidity of <s>Māyā</s>, to be accomplished through the inward-turned cultivation of one's own essential nature as devotion and supplication. (3.1-2:9)

children.text: * parameśvaro hi cidātmā yady antarmukhocitasevākrameṇārthyate tat tat saṃpādayata eva jāgrataḥ iti paratattve jāgarūkasya jāgarāvasthāsthasya ceti śleṣoktyā vyākhyeyam || VSpkC_3.1-2:10
children.translated_text: For the supreme Lord, whose nature is consciousness (<s>cidātmā</s>), if He is worshipped through the method of inward-turned proper practice, certainly accomplishes this or that. 'For one who is awake' (<s>jāgrataḥ</s>) — this should be explained through the double meaning: [both] for one who is vigilant regarding the supreme principle, and for one established in the waking state. (3.1-2:10)

children.text: * yadi punarevaṃ sāvadhāno na bhavati tadā nāsya yogitetyāha || VSpkC_3.1-2:11]
children.translated_text: But if one is not thus attentive, then 'this is not his <s>yoga</s>' — thus he says: (3.1-2:11)
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s> commentary:]

children.text: anyathā tu svatantrā syāt sṛṣṭis taddharmakatvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, the creative emanation would be autonomous, due to having that nature,

children.text: satataṃ laukikasyeva jāgratsvapnapadadvaye // VSpk_3.3 //
children.translated_text: always — just like for an ordinary person — in the two states of waking and dream. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.3)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* yadyuktayuktyā nityaṃ nārādhyate dhātā tadā svasvarūpasthityabhāve satataṃ pratyahaṃ laukikasyeva cāsya yogino 'pi jāgarāyāṃ svapne ca sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇārthaprakāśanatanniścayanādisvabhāvā pārameśvarī sṛṣṭiḥ svatantrā syāllaukikavadyoginam api saṃsārāvaṭa evāsau pātayed ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_3.3:1
children.translated_text: If the Supporter (<s>dhātā</s>) is not constantly worshipped by the stated method, then in the absence of abiding in one's own essential nature, constantly, every day, just as for an ordinary person, so too for this <s>yogin</s> — the divine (<s>pārameśvarī</s>) emanation, whose nature is the illumination of ordinary and extraordinary objects, their determination, and so forth, would be autonomous — it would cast even the <s>yogin</s> into the pit of <s>saṃsāra</s>, just like an ordinary person — this is the meaning. (3.3:1)

children.text: * yathoktam /
children.translated_text: As stated:

children.text: * pravṛttir bhūtānāmaiśvarī /
children.translated_text: 'The activity of beings is divine (<s>aiśvarī</s>).' (3.3:2 quote)

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_3.3:2
* taddharmakatvataḥ iti svapnajāgarādipadaprakāśane bhagavatsṛṣṭeḥ svātantryasvabhāvād ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_3.3:3
children.translated_text: 'Due to having that nature' (<s>taddharmakatvataḥ</s>) — the meaning is: because the Lord's emanation, in illuminating the states of dream, waking, and the rest, has autonomy (<s>svātantrya</s>) as its nature. (3.3:3)

children.text: * evaṃ svapnasauṣuptanirdalanopāyaṃ svaprabuddhatāyai saṃsādhya spandatattvasamāveśopāyaṃ suprabuddhasya dṛṣṭāntayuktipūrvakaṃ nirūpayati jijñāsitārthajñaptir apītthaṃ bhavatītyādiśati || VSpkC_3.3:4]
children.translated_text: Having thus accomplished the means for destroying [the obscuration of] dream and deep sleep for the sake of self-awakening, he now demonstrates — with an analogy and reasoning — the means of absorption into the <s>spanda</s> principle for the fully awakened one, and teaches that even the knowledge of desired objects comes about in this way: (3.3:4)
[<s>Spandakārikā-nirṇaya</s>]

children.text: yathā hy artho 'sphuṭo dṛṣṭaḥ sāvadhāne'pi cetasi /
children.translated_text: Just as an object seen unclearly, even in an attentive mind,

children.text: bhūyaḥ sphuṭataro bhāti svabalodyogabhāvitaḥ // VSpk_3.4 //
children.translated_text: shines forth more clearly again when cultivated through the exertion of one's own power, (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.4)

children.text: tathā yatparamārthena yena yatra yathā sthitam /
children.translated_text: so too, that which abides in the ultimate sense, in whatever [place], by whatever [means], in whatever manner,

children.text: tattathā balamākramya na cirāt sampravartate // VSpk_3.5 //
children.translated_text: by appropriating that power, manifests before long in that very manner. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.5)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* hiśabdaḥ kilaśabdārthe || VSpkC_3.4-5:1
children.translated_text: The particle 'hi' is used in the sense of 'kila' (indeed). (3.4-5:1)

children.text: * sāvadhāne'pi cetasi dūratvādidoṣair yathā kilārtho 'sphuṭo dṛṣṭo bhūyo 'dhyakṣanirīkṣaṇātmanā svabalodyogena bhāvito bhṛśam ālokito na kevalaṃ sphuṭo yāvat sphuṭataro'pi bhāti tathā yatspandatattvātmakaṃ balaṃ yenānandaghanatātmanā paramārthena yatreti śaṃkarātmani svasvabhāve yatheti abhedavyāptyā sthitaṃ tatkartṛ tatheti svabalodyogena antarmukhatadekātmatāpariśīlanaprayatnena saṃbhāvitaṃ śīghrameva sphuṭataratvena pravartate abhivyajyate || VSpkC_3.4-5:2
children.translated_text: 'Even in an attentive mind' — just as an object seen unclearly due to defects of distance and the like, when cultivated — that is, intensely observed — again through the exertion of one's own power in the form of direct perceptual examination, shines forth not merely clearly but even more clearly; so too, 'that' power whose nature is the <s>spanda</s> principle, which by whatever ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>) whose nature is a mass of bliss (<s>ānandaghanatā</s>), 'in which' — that is, in <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s own essential nature — 'in whatever manner' — through pervasion in non-difference — is established, that agent, 'in that manner' — through the exertion of one's own power, through the effort of cultivating identity with that by turning inward — manifests, becomes apparent, swiftly and most clearly. (3.4-5:2)

children.text: * kathamākramyārādhakasya kalpitadehādipramātṛbhūmiṃ svātmanyeva nimagnāṃ kṛtvātha ca spandātmakaṃ balamākramya sthitasya kalpitadehabuddhipramātṛbhūmim asakṛd uttejayataḥ sādhakasya yogino yajjijñāsitaṃ nidhānādi yatra deśādau yena hemādinā paramārthena yathā saṃniveśena sthitaṃ tathā tadacirād eva prakāśate || VSpkC_3.4-5:3
children.translated_text: How? By 'appropriating' — the worshipper, having caused the plane of the constructed subject consisting of body and the rest to submerge into his own self, and then, having appropriated the power whose nature is <s>spanda</s> and being established [therein], repeatedly intensifying the plane of the constructed subject of body and intellect — for the practicing <s>yogin</s>, whatever he wishes to know — a treasure and the like, in whatever place and the like, consisting of gold and the like, in whatever arrangement, in the ultimate sense — that manifests before long. (3.4-5:3)

children.text: * kartṛśaktyādir apyamuta eva balāt prādurbhavatītyāha || VSpkC_3.4-5:4]
children.translated_text: The power of agency and the rest also emerge right from this [<s>spanda</s>] by [its] force — thus he says: (3.4-5:4)
[<s>Spandakārikā-nirṇaya</s>]

children.text: durbalo'pi tadākramya yataḥ kārye pravartate /
children.translated_text: Even one who is weak, by appropriating that [power], is able to engage in [any] task;

children.text: ācchādayedbubhukṣāṃ ca tathā yo 'tibubhukṣitaḥ // VSpk_3.6 //
children.translated_text: likewise, one who is extremely hungry can cover [i.e., satisfy] his hunger. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.6)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* yathā kṣīṇadhātur ṛṣiprāyaḥ so 'pi spandātmakaṃ balam ākramya spandasamāveśabalena prāṇapramātṛbhūmim asakṛd uttejya kārye 'vaśyakartavye karmaṇi pravartate aśakyam api vastu tadbalākramaṇenaiva karotītyarthaḥ || VSpkC_3.6:1
children.translated_text: Just as one whose bodily constituents (<s>dhātu</s>) are depleted, resembling a <s>ṛṣi</s> [in emaciation] — even he, by appropriating the power whose nature is <s>spanda</s>, through the force of <s>spanda</s>-absorption (<s>spandasamāveśa</s>), repeatedly intensifying the plane of the <s>prāṇa</s>-subject, engages in a task — an action that must be performed — even accomplishes what is [ordinarily] impossible by the very appropriation of that power — this is the meaning. (3.6:1)

children.text: * tathā yo 'pyatibubhukṣitaḥ so 'pi tadbalākrāntyā kṣutpipāsādi śamayati || VSpkC_3.6:2
children.translated_text: Likewise, one who is extremely hungry — even he, through the appropriation of that power, pacifies hunger, thirst, and the like. (3.6:2)

children.text: * na hi cidghanāṃ bhūmim anupraviṣṭasya dvaṃdvābhibhavaḥ kaścit prāṇādibhuva eva tadāśrayatvāttasyāś ceha cidbhūmau nimagnatvāt || VSpkC_3.6:3
children.translated_text: For one who has entered the ground of the mass of consciousness (<s>cidghana</s>), there is no overpowering by the pairs of opposites whatsoever, since these [opposites] have their basis only in the plane of <s>prāṇa</s> and the like, and since that [plane] is here submerged in the ground of consciousness. (3.6:3)

children.text: * yata evam uktasūtropapattikramānusāreṇedṛk siddhisamudāyo 'smād bhavatītyataḥ || VSpkC_3.6:4]
children.translated_text: Since in this manner the accumulation of <s>siddhis</s> (attainments) arises from this [<s>spanda</s> principle], following the order of reasoning of the stated <s>sūtras</s>, therefore: (3.6:4)
[<s>Spandakārikā-nirṇaya</s>]

children.text: anenādhiṣṭhite dehe yathā sarvajñatādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as omniscience and the other [powers] arise when this [<s>spanda</s>] presides over the body,

children.text: tathā svātmanyadhiṣṭhānāt sarvatraivaṃ bhaviṣyati // VSpk_3.7 //
children.translated_text: so too, by its presiding over one's own self, it will be thus everywhere. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.7)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* anena svasvabhāvātmanā spandatattvenādhiṣṭhite vyāpte dehe sati yathā tadavasthocitārthānubhavakaraṇādirūpāḥ sarvajñatāsarvakartṛtādayo dharmā āvirbhavanti dehinaḥ tathā yadyayaṃ kūrmāṅgasaṃkocavat sarvopasaṃhāreṇa mahāvikāsayuktyā vā svasminnanapāyinyātmani cidrūpe adhiṣṭhānaṃ karoti uktābhijñānapratyabhijñāte tatraiva samāveśasthitiṃ badhnāti tadā sarvatreti śivādau kṣityante evam iti śaṃkarataducitasarvajñatāsarvakartṛtādirūpo bhaviṣyati || VSpkC_3.7:1
children.translated_text: When the body is presided over — pervaded — by this [<s>spanda</s>], whose nature is one's own essential nature, the <s>spanda</s> principle, then just as the qualities (<s>dharmas</s>) such as omniscience, omnipotence, and the rest, appropriate to that state — in the form of experiencing objects, performing actions, and the rest — become manifest for the embodied being; so too, if this [<s>yogin</s>], through complete withdrawal like the contraction of a tortoise's limbs, or through the method of great expansion (<s>mahāvikāsa</s>), makes his presidence in his own imperishable self whose nature is consciousness (<s>cidrūpa</s>) — [that is,] if he fastens his state of absorption (<s>samāveśa</s>) in that very [self] which is recognized through the stated recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) — then 'everywhere,' from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth, 'thus' — he will become of the form of omniscience, omnipotence, and the rest, appropriate to <s>Śaṃkara</s> and His [manifestations]. (3.7:1)

children.text: * idam apyetatprasādenetyāha || VSpkC_3.7:2]
children.translated_text: This too [comes about] by that [<s>spanda</s>'s] grace — thus he says: (3.7:2)
[<s>Spandakārikā-nirṇaya</s>]

children.text: glānir viluṇṭhikā dehe tasyāścājñānataḥ sṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Languor (<s>glāni</s>) is a robber in the body, and its course arises from ignorance;

children.text: tadunmeṣaviluptaṃ cet kutaḥ sā syādahetukā // VSpk_3.8 //
children.translated_text: if that [ignorance] is destroyed by the unfolding [of <s>spanda</s>], how could that [languor] arise without a cause? (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.8)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* mnā sarvakeśānāmāspadaṃ tataśca dehe yā glāniḥ arthāddehābhimāninaḥ puṃso yo harṣakṣayo'sau viluṇṭhikā parasaṃviddraviṇāpahāreṇa pārimityadaurgatyapradā tasyāśca glāner ajñānataś cidānandaghanasvasvarūpāpratyabhijñānāt sṛtir udbhavo 'vasthitiśca || VSpkC_3.8:1
children.translated_text: ... the abode of all afflictions; and therefore in the body, the languor (<s>glāni</s>) — which means the depletion of vitality for the person who identifies with the body — is a robber (<s>viluṇṭhikā</s>), bestowing poverty and destitution through the theft of the treasure of supreme consciousness (<s>parasaṃvid</s>). And the course (<s>sṛti</s>) — the arising and persistence — of that languor is from ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), from the non-recognition of one's own essential nature which is a mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānandaghana</s>). (3.8:1)

children.text: * tadajñānaṃ pradarśayiṣyamāṇasvarūpeṇonmeṣarūpeṇa cedviluptaṃ nikṛttaṃ tadāsau glānirajñānātmano hetorabhāvāt kutaḥ syānna bhaved ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_3.8:2
children.translated_text: If that ignorance is destroyed — cut off — by the unfolding (<s>unmeṣa</s>) whose nature is about to be demonstrated, then that languor, since the cause which is of the nature of ignorance is absent — whence could it arise? It would not arise — this is the meaning. (3.8:2)

children.text: * glānyabhāve ca dehe 'vaśyambhāvinyo vyādhyādisaṃtāpāvasthā api yathā yathā yogino 'pakṛṣyante tathā tathā hemna ivātitāpyamānasya kālikāpagame svasvarūpaṃ dedīpyata eva || VSpkC_3.8:3
children.translated_text: And in the absence of languor, even the states of affliction from disease and the like that inevitably occur in the body — the more they are drawn upon [i.e., attack] the <s>yogin</s>, the more his own essential nature blazes forth, just as gold, when intensely heated, [shines forth] with the removal of impurities. (3.8:3)

children.text: * evaṃ ca dehāvasthitasyāpi sarvadā glānyabhāva eva parayogino vibhūtiḥ || VSpkC_3.8:4
children.translated_text: And thus, the glory of the supreme <s>yogin</s> is always the very absence of languor, even while abiding in the body. (3.8:4)

children.text: * yathoktaṃ paramayoginyā madālasayā bāladārakān prayogīkurvatyā /
children.translated_text: As stated by the supreme <s>yoginī</s> <s>Madālasā</s>, while instructing her young sons:

children.text: * tvaṃ kañcuke śīryamāṇe nije'smin dehe heye mūḍhatāṃ mā vrajethāḥ /
children.translated_text: When this sheath of yours, your own body, is decaying — being worthy of abandonment — do not fall into delusion!

children.text: * śubhāśubhaiḥ karmabhir dehametanmadādibhiḥ kañcukaste nibaddhaḥ || VSpkC_3.8:5
children.translated_text: This body is your sheath, bound by auspicious and inauspicious <s>karmas</s>, and by [the coverings of] pride and the like. || VSpkC_3.8:5

children.text: * iti mitasiddhyabhilāṣiṇo yoginaḥ samāveśābhyāsarasena dehaṃ vidhyato valīpalitādivyādhijayo bhavatītyapi bhaṅgyānena pratipāditam || VSpkC_3.8:6
children.translated_text: Thus, it is also indirectly taught that for the <s>yogin</s> who aspires to limited <s>siddhis</s> (powers), conquest over diseases such as wrinkles, gray hair, and the like occurs through piercing the body with the essence of the practice of <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption). || VSpkC_3.8:6

children.text: * atha yo 'yam unmeṣaḥ sa kiṃsvarūpaḥ kim upāyalabhyaś cety ākāṅkṣāyām āha || VSpkC_3.8:7]
children.translated_text: Now, what is the nature of this <s>unmeṣa</s> (blossoming of consciousness)? And by what means is it attained? In response to this expectation, he says: || VSpkC_3.8:7
[<s>Spandakārikā-nirṇaya</s>]

children.text: ekacintāprasaktasya yataḥ syād aparodayaḥ /
children.translated_text: When, for one who is absorbed in a single thought, there arises another [thought],

children.text: unmeṣaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ svayaṃ tamupalakṣayet // VSpk_3.9 //
children.translated_text: that is to be known as <s>unmeṣa</s> (the blossoming); one should perceive it by oneself. // VSpk_3.9 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
children.translated_text: [From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: * bhāve tyakte niruddhā cinnaiva bhāvāntaraṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: When a cognition is arrested after an object is abandoned, it does not move to another object;

children.text: * tadā tanmadhyabhāvena vikasatyatibhāvanā || VSpkC_3.9:1
children.translated_text: then, by means of the state in between, the supreme <s>bhāvanā</s> (contemplative realization) blossoms forth. || VSpkC_3.9:1

children.text: * iti nītyā ekasyāṃ kasyāṃcid ālambanaviśeṣanibhṛtavikārātmikāyāṃ cintāyāṃ prasaktasya ekāgrībhūtasya yogino yata iti tadekāgratāprakarṣollasatsaṃvitsphāratas tadālambananimīlanājjhaṭiti grastasamastacintāsaṃtater agnīṣomāvibhedātmanaḥ spandatattvādapara evodayaściccamatkārātmānya eva lokottara ullāsaḥ syāt sa taccamatkāronmeṣakatvād evonmeṣo vijñātavyo 'nveṣaṇīyaḥ ittham eva yoginā jñātuṃ śakyaḥ tataśca svayamiti idaṃtāviṣayatvābhāvād akṛtakaprayatnātmanāvadhānenāhaṃtayaivopetyātmani lakṣayet asādhāraṇena camatkārātmanā pratyabhijānīyāt || VSpkC_3.9:2
children.translated_text: Following this principle: for a <s>yogin</s> who is absorbed — that is, who has become one-pointed — in a single thought, which is of the nature of a subtle modification focused on a particular support (<s>ālambana</s>), from the expansion of awareness that flashes forth through the intensification of that one-pointedness, from the closing of the eyes upon that support, suddenly devouring the entire stream of thought — there arises from the <s>spanda</s> reality, which is of the nature of the non-duality of <s>Agni</s> (fire) and <s>Soma</s> (moon) — a different, supramundane delight whose essence is the wonder of consciousness (<s>ciccamatkāra</s>). That is to be known as <s>unmeṣa</s>, because it causes the blossoming of that wonder — it is to be sought. It can be known by the <s>yogin</s> only in this way. Therefore, 'by oneself' — because of the absence of objectifiability as 'this,' through natural, effortless attention, one should perceive it through 'I'-consciousness alone; one should recognize it through the incomparable essence of wonder. || VSpkC_3.9:2

children.text: * yata ekasyāṃ viṣayavicārādicintāyāṃ prasaktasya aparasyāś cintāyā jhaṭityudayaḥ syāt sa cintādvayavyāpaka unmeṣaḥ ityanye || VSpkC_3.9:3
children.translated_text: Others [say]: when one who is absorbed in a single thought of deliberation on an object and the like, suddenly another thought arises, that <s>unmeṣa</s> pervades both thoughts. || VSpkC_3.9:3

children.text: * idānīṃ mitayogijanaprayatnasādhyāsvapi tāsu tāsu siddhiṣūnmeṣaṇapariśīlanamātroditāsu parayogino heyatvam eva mantavyam ityādiśati || VSpkC_3.9:4]
children.translated_text: Now he instructs that even regarding those various <s>siddhis</s> (powers) that arise merely from the cultivation of <s>unmeṣa</s>, attainable through the effort of <s>yogins</s> of limited [attainment], the supreme <s>yogin</s> should consider them as something to be abandoned. || VSpkC_3.9:4

children.text: ato bindur ato nādo rūpam asmād ato rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: From this [<s>unmeṣa</s> arise] <s>bindu</s> (luminous point), from this <s>nāda</s> (inner sound), form from this, from this taste;

children.text: pravartante 'cireṇaiva kṣobhakatvena dehinaḥ // VSpk_3.10 //
children.translated_text: they arise without delay, as agitators of the embodied being. // VSpk_3.10 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* ata unmeṣād upalakṣyamāṇād apralīyamānasthūlasūkṣmādidehāhambhāvasya yogino 'cireṇaiva bhrūmadhyādau tārakāprakāśarūpo bindur aśeṣavedyasāmānyaprakāśātmā nādaḥ sakalavācakāvibhediśabdanarūpo 'nāhatadhvanirūpo rūpamandhakāre 'pi prakāśanaṃ tejaḥ rasaśca rasanāgre lokottara āsvādaḥ kṣobhakatvena spandatattvasamāsādanavighnabhūtatāvatsaṃtoṣapradatvena vartante || VSpkC_3.10:1
children.translated_text: From that <s>unmeṣa</s> being perceived — for a <s>yogin</s> whose sense of 'I' as the gross, subtle, and other bodies has not dissolved — without delay: <s>bindu</s>, in the form of the light of the star [that appears] between the eyebrows and elsewhere; <s>nāda</s>, whose nature is the unstruck sound (<s>anāhatadhvani</s>), having the form of sound that is undifferentiated from all signifiers, whose essence is the universal illumination of all that is knowable; form (<s>rūpa</s>), the radiance that illuminates even in darkness; and taste (<s>rasa</s>), the supramundane savor at the tip of the tongue — these arise as agitators, providing satisfaction proportional to their capacity to obstruct the attainment of the <s>spanda</s> reality. || VSpkC_3.10:1

children.text: * yadāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: As they say:

children.text: * te samādhāv upasargā vyutthāne siddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These are obstacles in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption); in the ordinary state they are <s>siddhis</s> (powers).'

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_3.10:2
children.translated_text: Thus. || VSpkC_3.10:2

children.text: * evamunmeṣanibhālanodyuktasyāpi dehātmamānino yogino bindunādādayaḥ kṣobhakā bhavantītyuktam || VSpkC_3.10:3
children.translated_text: Thus it is stated that for a <s>yogin</s> who identifies with the body, even when striving to observe <s>unmeṣa</s>, <s>bindu</s>, <s>nāda</s>, and the like become agitators. || VSpkC_3.10:3

children.text: * idānīmatronmeṣātmani svabhāve dehapramātṛtāṃ nimajjayati tadākārāmapi parapramātṛtāṃ labhata ityāha || VSpkC_3.10:4]
children.translated_text: Now he says that one who submerges the body-based subjectivity into the <s>unmeṣa</s> as one's own nature attains the supreme subjectivity whose form is that [<s>unmeṣa</s>]. || VSpkC_3.10:4
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: didṛkṣayeva sarvārthān yadā vyāpyāvatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: When, with the mere desire to see, pervading all objects, one remains established,

children.text: tadā kiṃ bahunoktena svayam evāvabhotsyate // VSpk_3.11 //
children.translated_text: then, what need is there of much talk? One will know by oneself. // VSpk_3.11 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* yathā paśyantīrūpāvikalpakadidṛkṣāvasare didṛkṣito 'rtho 'ntarabhedena sphurati tathaiva svacchandādyadhvaprakriyoktān dharādiśivāntāntarbhāvino 'śeṣānarthān vyāpyeti sarvam aham iti sadāśivavat svavikalpānusaṃdhānapūrvakam avikalpāntam abhedavimarśāntaḥkroḍīkāreṇācchādya yadāvatiṣṭhate asyāḥ samāpatterna vicalati tāvad aśeṣavedyaikīkāreṇonmiṣattāvadvedyagrāsīkārimahāpramātṛtāsamāveśacamatkārarūpaṃ yat phalaṃ tat svayam evāvabhotsyate svasaṃvidevānubhaviṣyati kim atra bahunā pratipāditena || VSpkC_3.11:1
children.translated_text: Just as at the moment of the non-conceptual desire to see, which has the form of <s>paśyantī</s> (the visionary level of speech), the desired object shines forth without internal differentiation — in exactly that way, when, having pervaded all objects — all things from earth to <s>Śiva</s> contained within, as described in the path-system of the <s>Svacchanda</s> and other [texts] — [the yogin], like <s>Sadāśiva</s>, preceded by the reflective awareness of his own determination 'I am everything,' having covered and concealed [all objects] through the encompassing of the reflective awareness of non-difference, ending in the non-conceptual — remains established and does not waver from this absorption — then the fruit, whose nature is the wonder of the absorption into the great subjectivity that devours all that is knowable through unification with the totality of the knowable and that blossoms forth [as consciousness], one will know by oneself — will experience through one's own awareness alone. What need is there of much explanation here? || VSpkC_3.11:1

children.text: * tasyopalabdhiḥ satatam iti pratijñāya tadanantaram upapāditam upāyajātaṃ pariśīlayataḥ satataṃ spandatattvasamāviṣṭatvaṃ suprabuddhasya bhavatīti tadanantaprameyasaṃbhinnatvād upadeśyahṛdaye smārayann anupraveśayuktyupasaṃhārabhaṅgyāha || VSpkC_3.11:2]
children.translated_text: Having promised 'its apprehension is constant,' and then having established the set of means [for this], he now says — by way of conclusion using the device of re-entry, reminding the heart of the one being instructed that constant absorption in the <s>spanda</s> reality, for the fully awakened one who cultivates [these means], [occurs] because of being merged with infinite objects of knowledge: || VSpkC_3.11:2
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: prabuddhaḥ sarvadā tiṣṭhejjñānenālokya gocaram /
children.translated_text: The awakened one should always remain, having illuminated the field of experience with knowledge;

children.text: ekatrāropayetsarvaṃ tato 'nyena na pīḍyate // VSpk_3.12 //
children.translated_text: he should place everything upon the One; then he is not afflicted by anything else. // VSpk_3.12 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* sarvadā jāgarāsvapnasuṣuptasaṃvidādimadhyāntapadeṣu prabuddhas tiṣṭhet unmīlitaspandatattvāvaṣṭambhadivyadṛṣṭiḥ suprabuddhatām eva bhajeta || VSpkC_3.12:1
children.translated_text: At all times — at the initial, middle, and final moments of the states of waking, dream, and deep sleep — the awakened one should remain; having disclosed the divine vision that supports the <s>spanda</s> reality, he should indeed attain full awakening. || VSpkC_3.12:1

children.text: * kathaṃ jñānena bahirmukhenāvabhāsena sarvaṃ gocaraṃ nīlasukhādirūpaṃ viṣayam ālokya /
children.translated_text: How? Having illuminated — having reflected upon — with knowledge, that is, with outward-directed manifestation — all objects of experience, the domain of blue, pleasure, and the like,

children.text: * tasmācchabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, in contemplation of words, meanings, and thoughts, there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>';

children.text: * ityupapāditadṛśā vimṛśya ekatra sraṣṭari śaṃkarātmani svabhāve sarvam āropayet nimīlanonmīlanadaśayos tadabhedena jānīyāt pūrvāparakoṭyavaṣṭambhadārḍhyān madhyabhūmim api cidrasāśyānatārūpatayaiva paśyed ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_3.12:2
children.translated_text: — having reflected with the vision established thus, he should place everything upon the One — upon the creator, upon one's own essential nature whose nature is <s>Śaṃkara</s>. He should know [all] as non-different from that, in both the states of closing and opening [of consciousness]; through the firmness of grasping the initial and final moments, he should see even the middle ground as having the nature of being saturated with the essence of consciousness — this is the meaning. || VSpkC_3.12:2

children.text: * evaṃ ca na kenacid anyena vyatiriktena vastunā bādhyate sarvasmin svātmanaḥ svīkṛtatvāt || VSpkC_3.12:3
children.translated_text: And thus, he is not obstructed by anything other or separate, because everything has been appropriated as one's own self. || VSpkC_3.12:3

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrīpratyabhijñākāreṇa /
children.translated_text: As stated by the author of the revered <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>:

children.text: * yo 'vikalpam idam artham aṇḍajaṃ paśyatīśa nikhilaṃ bhavadvapuḥ /
children.translated_text: O Lord, he who sees this non-conceptual, entire universe born from the cosmic egg as Your body,

children.text: * svātmapakṣaparipūrite jagatyasya nityasukhinaḥ kuto bhayam /
children.translated_text: in a world made complete by his own self — from where [could there be] fear for him, the eternally happy?

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_3.12:4
children.translated_text: Thus. || VSpkC_3.12:4

children.text: * tato 'nyena na pīḍyate iti yaduktaṃ tatra ko 'sāv anyaḥ pīḍakaḥ kaś ca pīḍyo yataḥ śivātmakam eva viśvamuktam ityāśaṅkya pāśānāṃ paśośca svarūpaṃ nirṇetum āha || VSpkC_3.12:5]
children.translated_text: Since it has been said 'he is not afflicted by anything else' — who then is this 'other' that afflicts, and who is the one afflicted? For it has been stated that the universe is <s>Śiva</s> in nature. Anticipating this [doubt], in order to determine the nature of the bonds (<s>pāśas</s>) and the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), he says: || VSpkC_3.12:5
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: śabdarāśisamutthasya śaktivargasya bhogyatām /
children.translated_text: Having gone to the state of being an object of enjoyment for the host of powers arising from the mass of phonemes (<s>śabdarāśi</s>),

children.text: kalāviluptavibhavo gataḥ sansa paśuḥ smṛtaḥ // VSpk_3.13 //
children.translated_text: with his glory (<s>vibhava</s>) stolen by <s>kalā</s>, he is called a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>). // VSpk_3.13 //

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
children.translated_text: [From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: * iha yo 'yaṃ prakāśātmā svasvabhāvaḥ śāṃkara uktaḥ asau /
children.translated_text: Here, that which has been called the essential nature (<s>svasvabhāva</s>) belonging to <s>Śaṃkara</s>, whose nature is light — he,

children.text: * vyavasthitaḥ karotyeṣa viśvakāraṇam īśvaraḥ /
