children.translated_text: 'Being established, this Lord, the cause of the universe, performs

children.text: * sṛṣṭiṃ sthitiṃ ca saṃhāraṃ tirodhānamanugraham || VSpkC_3.13:1
children.translated_text: creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment, and grace.' || VSpkC_3.13:1

children.text: * iti śrīsvacchandaśāstradṛṣṭyā nijaśaktyāśliṣṭaḥ sadā pañcavidhakṛtyakārī svatantraḥ spandalaliteśvarādiśabdair āgameṣūdghoṣyate || VSpkC_3.13:2
children.translated_text: According to the perspective of the revered <s>Svacchanda</s> scripture, embraced by his own power, always performing the fivefold cosmic act, autonomous — he is proclaimed in the <s>āgamas</s> (sacred texts) by the words <s>Spanda</s>, <s>Laliteśvara</s>, and the like. || VSpkC_3.13:2

children.text: * svātantryaśaktir evāsya sanātanī pūrṇāhaṃtārūpā parā matsyodarī mahāsattā sphurattormiḥ sāraṃ hṛdayaṃ bhairavī devī śikhā ityādibhir asaṃkhyaiḥ prakārais tatra tatra nirucyate || VSpkC_3.13:3
children.translated_text: His very power of autonomy (<s>svātantryaśakti</s>), which is eternal, whose form is the full 'I'-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhaṃtā</s>) — [is known as] the supreme (<s>parā</s>), <s>Matsyodarī</s>, the great existence (<s>mahāsattā</s>), the shining wave (<s>sphurattormi</s>), the essence, the heart, <s>Bhairavī</s>, the goddess, the flame (<s>śikhā</s>), and by innumerable other designations it is described in various [texts]. || VSpkC_3.13:3

children.text: * pūrṇāhaṃtaiva cāsyānuttarānāhataśaktisaṃpuṭīkārasvīkṛtādikṣāntavarṇabhaṭṭārikā tata eva svīkṛtānantavācyavākarūpaṣaḍadhvasphāramayāśeṣaśakticakrakroḍīkārāntaḥ kṛtaniḥśeṣasargapralayādiparamparāpyakramavimarśarūpaiva nityoditānuccāryamahāmantramayī sarvajīvitabhūtā parā vāk || VSpkC_3.13:4
children.translated_text: And this very full 'I'-consciousness, which has as its queen the host of phonemes from 'a' to 'kṣa' that have been embraced within the seal of the <s>anuttara</s> (supreme) and <s>anāhata</s> (unstruck) power — which therefore encompasses within its embrace the infinite circle of all powers whose nature is the expansion of the six courses (<s>ṣaḍadhva</s>) consisting of signifiers and signified — having made the entire series of creation and dissolution and the like the content of its non-sequential reflective awareness — is the ever-risen, unutterable great <s>mantra</s>, the life-force of all beings, the supreme speech (<s>parā vāk</s>). || VSpkC_3.13:4

children.text: * eṣaiva bhagavata iyadviśvavaicitryacalattām iva svātmani prathayantī spandate ityarthānugamāt spanda iti ihocyate || VSpkC_3.13:5
children.translated_text: This very [supreme speech] of the Lord, manifesting in itself a semblance of the movement constituting the diversity of this universe, vibrates (<s>spandate</s>) — and therefore, following the meaning, it is called <s>spanda</s> here. || VSpkC_3.13:5

children.text: * evaṃ ceyad viśvaśaktikhacitaparāśaktisundarasya svātmanaḥ svarūpagopanakrīḍayā svātmabhittāv evāṃśāṃśikayā nirbhāsanaṃ bhagavān yāvaccikīrṣati tāvadekaivābhinnāpyasau tadīyā vimarśaśaktiricchātvaṃ pratipadya jñānakriyārūpatayā sthitvā śivaśaktiparāmarśātmakabījayonibhedena dvidhā bhūtvā vargabhedena tatkalābhedena ca navadhā pañcāśaddhā ca sphurantī tadvimarśasārair aghoraghoraghorataraiḥ saṃvittidevatātmabhiḥ rūpaiḥ prathamānā bhagavataḥ pañcavidhakṛtyakāritāṃ nirvahati || VSpkC_3.13:6
children.translated_text: Thus, of one's own self — which is beautiful with the supreme power studded with the powers of the universe — as long as the Lord desires this manifestation, which is partial, upon the canvas of his own self, through the play of concealing his own essential nature — so long does that single, undivided reflective power of his, assuming the form of will (<s>icchā</s>), abiding as knowledge and action, becoming twofold in the form of seed (<s>bīja</s>) and womb (<s>yoni</s>) characterized by the reflective awareness of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, then ninefold through the division of the letter-groups, and fifty-fold through the division of the individual <s>kalās</s> — shining forth, manifesting through forms that are the deities of consciousness, whose essence is the reflective awareness — <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Ghora</s>, and <s>Ghoratara</s> — carries out the Lord's fivefold cosmic activity. || VSpkC_3.13:6

children.text: * yathoktaṃ śrīmālinīvijayottare /
children.translated_text: As stated in the revered <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s>:

children.text: * yā sā śaktirjagaddhātuḥ kathitā samavāyinī /
children.translated_text: That power which is said to be concomitant with the Creator of the world —

children.text: * icchātvaṃ tasya sā devī sisṛkṣoḥ pratipadyate || VSpkC_3.13:7
children.translated_text: That [power] of the one who desires to create assumes the form of His desire (<s>icchā</s>).

children.text: * saikāpi satyanekatvaṃ yathā gacchati tacchṛṇu /
children.translated_text: That [power], though one, how it attains multiplicity — hear that:

children.text: * evametaditi jñeyaṃ nānyatheti suniścitam || VSpkC_3.13:8
children.translated_text: 'It is thus to be known, and not otherwise' — [when it functions] as determined certainty,

children.text: * jñāpayantī jagatyatra jñānaśaktirnigadyate /
children.translated_text: making known in this world, it is called the knowledge-power (<s>jñāna-śakti</s>);

children.text: * evaṃ bhavatvidaṃ sarvamiti kāryonmukhī yadā || VSpkC_3.13:9
children.translated_text: when it becomes oriented toward effect, [thinking] 'let all this come into being thus' —

children.text: * jātā tadaiva tadvastu kurvatyatra kriyocyate /
children.translated_text: then that very [power], actually producing that thing, is called the action-power (<s>kriyā-śakti</s>).

children.text: * evameṣā dvirūpāpi punarbhedairanantatām || VSpkC_3.13:10
children.translated_text: Thus, even though of twofold form, it again attains infinitude

children.text: * arthopādhivaśād yāti cintāmaṇiriveśvarī /
children.translated_text: through the conditioning of objects, like a wish-fulfilling gem — this sovereign [power].

children.text: * tatra tāvatsamāpannā mātṛbhāvaṃ vibhidyate || VSpkC_3.13:11
children.translated_text: There, having first assumed the nature of the knowing subject, she divides

children.text: * dvidhā ca navadhā caiva pañcāśaddhā ca mālinī /
children.translated_text: in two ways, in nine ways, and in fifty ways — [she is] <s>Mālinī</s>.

children.text: * bījayonyātmakādbhedāddvidhā bījaṃ svarā matāḥ || VSpkC_3.13:12
children.translated_text: From the division into seed (<s>bīja</s>) and womb (<s>yoni</s>), [the division is] twofold: the vowels are considered the seed,

children.text: * kādayaśca smṛtā yonirnavadhā vargabhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: and the consonants beginning with 'ka' are considered the womb; [the division is] ninefold through the division into classes (<s>vargas</s>);

children.text: * pṛthagvarṇavibhedena śatārdhakiraṇojjvalā || VSpkC_3.13:13
children.translated_text: through the division of individual letters, she shines with fifty rays.

children.text: * bījamatra śivaḥ śaktir yonir ityabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Here, the seed is <s>Śiva</s>; <s>Śakti</s> is called the womb.

children.text: * vargāṣṭakamiti jñeyamaghorādyamanukramāt || VSpkC_3.13:14
children.translated_text: The eightfold group of classes is to be known in sequence beginning with <s>Aghora</s> and the rest.

children.text: * tadeva śaktibhedena māheśvaryādi cāṣṭakam /
children.translated_text: That same [group], through the division of powers, is also the eightfold [group] of <s>Māheśvarī</s> and the rest.

children.text: * śatārdhabhedabhinnā ca tatsaṃkhyānāṃ varānane || VSpkC_3.13:15
children.translated_text: And divided into fifty divisions, O beautiful-faced one,

children.text: * rudrāṇāṃ vācakatvena kalpitā parameṣṭhinā /
children.translated_text: they have been designated by the Supreme Lord as the signifiers of an equal number of <s>Rudras</s>,

children.text: * tadvadeva ca śaktīnāṃ tatsaṃkhyānāmanukramāt || VSpkC_3.13:16
children.translated_text: and likewise of an equal number of <s>Śaktis</s> in sequence.

children.text: * ityādi || VSpkC_3.13:17
children.translated_text: And so forth.

children.text: * tathā /
children.translated_text: Likewise:

children.text: * viṣayeṣveva saṃlīnānadho'dhaḥ pātayantyaṇūn /
children.translated_text: The <s>Rudrāṇī</s> powers, embracing the <s>aṇus</s> (individual souls) immersed in sense objects,

children.text: * rudrāṇūnyāḥ samāliṅgya ghorataryo 'parāstu tāḥ || VSpkC_3.13:18
children.translated_text: cast them down lower and lower — those more terrible, lower ones.

children.text: * miśrakarmaphalāsaktiṃ pūrvavajjanayanti yāḥ || VSpkC_3.13:19
children.translated_text: Those which generate attachment to the fruits of mixed <s>karma</s>, as before,

children.text: * muktimārganirodhinyastāḥ syur ghorāḥ parāparāḥ || VSpkC_3.13:20
children.translated_text: and which obstruct the path of liberation — those are the terrible (<s>ghorā</s>), intermediate ones.

children.text: * pūrvavajjantujātasya śivadhāmaphalapradāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those which, as before, grant the fruit of the abode of <s>Śiva</s> to living beings,

children.text: * parāḥ prakathitās tajjñair aghorāḥ śivaśaktayaḥ || VSpkC_3.13:21
children.translated_text: are declared by knowers of that [reality] to be the supreme, non-terrible (<s>aghorā</s>) powers of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_3.13:22
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * evaṃ śabdarāśeḥ samutthito varganavakarūpo yo brāhmyādidevatāvargaḥ śivasahitastasya bhogyatāṃ pāśyatāṃ gataḥ sansa eva śaṃkarātmā svabhāvaḥ paśuḥ smṛtaḥ āgameṣu tathoktaḥ || VSpkC_3.13:23
children.translated_text: In this way, the group of deities beginning with <s>Brāhmī</s> and the rest, which has arisen from the mass of sounds in the form of nine classes of consonants together with <s>Śiva</s> — that very one, having become the object of enjoyment and having entered the state of bondage — is called in the scriptures the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), whose essential nature is <s>Śaṃkara</s>.

children.text: * nanu kathaṃ bhoktā maheśvara imāmavasthāṃ prāptaḥ ityāśaṅkāśāntyai viśeṣaṇadvāreṇa hetumāha kalāviluptavibhava iti || VSpkC_3.13:24
children.translated_text: Now, the objection [arises]: how has this supreme Lord, the enjoyer, reached this state? To allay this doubt, he states the reason by way of a qualifier: 'whose powers have been diminished by <s>kalā</s>.'

children.text: * kalayati bahiḥ kṣipati pārimityena paricchinattīti kalā māyāśaktiḥ tayā viluptavibhavaḥ svamāyayā gūhitaiśvaryaḥ sthita ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_3.13:25
children.translated_text: <s>Kalā</s> — that which projects outward, limits through finitude, circumscribes — is the power of <s>Māyā</s>. 'Whose powers have been diminished by that' means: one whose sovereignty has been concealed by his own <s>Māyā</s>, and who remains thus.

children.text: * atha ca kalayā kiṃcitkartṛtvopodbalanātmanā śaktyā tadupalakṣitena kalāvidyākālaniyatirāgātmanā kañcukena viluptavibhavaḥ sthagitapūrṇatvakartṛtvādidharmaḥ || VSpkC_3.13:26
children.translated_text: And furthermore, [he is one] whose powers have been diminished by <s>kalā</s> — the power that bolsters limited agency — [and] by the covering (<s>kañcuka</s>) characterized by <s>kalā</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, <s>kāla</s>, <s>niyati</s>, and <s>rāga</s> [collectively] indicated by that [term]; whose attributes of fullness, agency, and the like have been concealed.

children.text: * bhavatvevaṃ bhogyatāṃ tu kathamasau śaktivargasya gataḥ ityatraitad evottaram || VSpkC_3.13:27
children.translated_text: Granted it is so; but how has he come to be the object of enjoyment for the group of powers? To this, this itself is the answer:

children.text: * kalābhir akārādivargādhiṣṭhāyikābhir brāhmyādibhis tadvarṇabhaṭṭārakādhiṣṭhātṛbhūtābhiś ca śrīmālinīvijayoktadevatārūpābhiḥ kalābhir akārādivarṇair viluptavibhavaḥ saṃkucito'smi apūrṇo 'smi karavāṇi kiṃcididam upādade idaṃ jahāmi ityādivicitravikalpakāvikalpakapratipattikadambakāntaranupraviṣṭasthūlasūkṣmaśabdānuvedhakadarthito harṣaśokādirūpatāṃ nenīyamāna iva kṣaṇam api svarūpasthitiṃ na labhate yataḥ ato'sāv uktarūpaḥ śaktivargeṇa bhujyamānaḥ paśur uktaḥ || VSpkC_3.13:28
children.translated_text: By the <s>kalās</s> — the [deities] <s>Brāhmī</s> and others who preside over the classes beginning with 'a' — and by the letter-lords who preside over those phonemes — who are of the nature of the deities described in the revered <s>Mālinīvijaya</s> — by the <s>kalās</s>, that is, by the phonemes beginning with 'a' — his powers have been diminished. 'I am contracted, I am incomplete, let me do this little, I take up this, I abandon that' — having entered into a mass of varied conceptual and non-conceptual cognitions, tormented by the permeation of gross and subtle words, being led as it were to the condition of joy, sorrow, and the like — he does not obtain even a moment's establishment in his own essential nature. Because of this, he, being of the described nature, being consumed by the group of powers, is called a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>).

children.text: * kalayā akhyātyātmanāṃśena viluptavibhavaḥ saṃkucita iva na tu tattvataḥ śivātmā svabhāvo 'sya kvāpi gataḥ tadabhāve hi sa eva na sphuret || VSpkC_3.13:29
children.translated_text: By <s>kalā</s> — by the aspect whose nature is non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>) — his powers have been diminished, [meaning he has] contracted as it were; but not in reality, [because] his essential nature as <s>Śiva</s> has not gone anywhere. For in its absence, he himself would not manifest at all.

children.text: * tathāvabhāsamānaireva kalābhiḥ saṃkucitaiḥ śabdair jñānaiś ca viluptavibhavas tathārūpam ātmānaṃ na vimraṣṭuṃ kṣama ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_3.13:30
children.translated_text: And by the <s>kalās</s> — contracted words and cognitions appearing thus — his powers have been diminished, meaning he is unable to reflect upon himself in his true form.

children.text: * adhunā paśuḥ saṃkucitadṛkśaktibādhyaḥ pāśyaś cetyetad vibhajati || VSpkC_3.13:31]
children.translated_text: Now he distinguishes [the fact] that the bound soul, whose power of seeing is contracted, is subject to bondage:

children.text: parāmṛtarasāpāyas tasya yaḥ pratyayodbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The arising of cognitions (<s>pratyaya</s>) for him is the loss of the nectar-essence of the Supreme (<s>parāmṛtarasa</s>);

children.text: tenāsvatantratāmeti sa ca tanmātragocaraḥ // VSpk_3.14 //
children.translated_text: by that he enters a state of non-autonomy (<s>asvatantratā</s>), and that [cognition] has as its domain only the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.14)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* tasya paśoryaḥ pratyayānāṃ laukikaśāstrīyavikalpānāṃ tadadhivāsitānāṃ bhinnārthajñānānāṃ vikalpānām apyudbhavaḥ vināśāghrāta utpādaḥ sa parasyāmṛtarasasya cidghanasyānandaprasarasyāpāyo nimajjanam || VSpkC_3.14:1
children.translated_text: For this bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), the arising — i.e., the birth without touching destruction — of <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions), namely worldly and scriptural conceptual constructs, and also the non-conceptual cognitions of differentiated objects conditioned by those [constructs], is the submersion — the loss — of the supreme nectar-essence (<s>parāmṛtarasa</s>), which is a solid mass of consciousness and an effusion of bliss.

children.text: * uditeṣu bhinnārtheṣu pratyayeṣu cidbhūmiḥ sthitāpy aparāmṛśyamānatvād asthiteva lakṣyate tata evam uktam || VSpkC_3.14:2
children.translated_text: When differentiated object-cognitions have arisen, the ground of consciousness (<s>cidbhūmi</s>), though remaining, is perceived as if not remaining because it is not being reflectively apprehended. Therefore it is said thus.

children.text: * tena ca pratyayodbhavenāyam asvatantratām eti tadvaśaḥ sampadyate || VSpkC_3.14:3
children.translated_text: And by that arising of cognitions, this [soul] enters a state of non-autonomy (<s>asvatantratā</s>) — comes under the power of those [cognitions].

children.text: * yaduktaṃ śrīśivasūtreṣu jñānaṃ bandhaḥ iti || VSpkC_3.14:4
children.translated_text: As stated in the revered <s>Śivasūtras</s>: 'Knowledge is bondage.'

children.text: * śrīmadvyāsamunināpi mātāpitṛmayo bālye iti || VSpkC_3.14:5
children.translated_text: The revered sage <s>Vyāsa</s> also [said]: 'In childhood, [one is] constituted by mother and father...'

children.text: * śrīmadālasayāpi || VSpkC_3.14:6
children.translated_text: By the revered <s>Ālasā</s> also:

children.text: * tāteti kiṃcittanayeti kiṃcit ambeti kiṃciddayiteti kiṃcit /
children.translated_text: 'Father' by some, 'son' by some, 'mother' by some, 'beloved' by some,

children.text: * mameti kiṃcin na mameti kiṃcit bhautaṃ saṃghaṃ bahudhā mā lapethāḥ || VSpkC_3.14:7
children.translated_text: 'mine' by some, 'not mine' by some — do not prattle in many ways about this material aggregate.

children.text: * iti || VSpkC_3.14:8
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: * pratyayasyodbhavastanmātrāṇi tīvrātīvrabhedasāmānyavṛttayo gocaro yasya tathābhūto bhinnavedyaviṣaya ityarthaḥ || VSpkC_3.14:9
children.translated_text: The arising of cognition has as its domain the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — meaning [cognitions] whose activities are of the nature of intense and very intense differentiation and generality — having differentiated knowable objects as its field.

children.text: * anenedamāha yāvadiyaṃ bhinnavedyaprathā tāvad baddha eva yadā tūktopadeśayuktyā sarvam ātmamayam evāvicalapratipattyā pratipadyate tadā jīvanmukta iti || VSpkC_3.14:10
children.translated_text: By this he says: as long as this manifestation of differentiated knowables [persists], one is bound; but when, through the instruction and reasoning stated, one recognizes everything as pervaded by the self alone with unwavering certainty, then one is a <s>jīvanmukta</s> (one liberated while living).

children.text: * yathoktam iti vā yasya saṃvittiḥ ityādi || VSpkC_3.14:11
children.translated_text: As stated: 'Or, one whose cognition...' and so forth.

children.text: * evaṃ ca yat pūrvam uktaṃ tasmācchabdārthacintāsu na sāvasthā na yā śivaḥ ityādi na tena saha parāmṛtarasāpāyas tasya yaḥ pratyayodbhavaḥ ityasya vaiṣamyaṃ kiṃcit || VSpkC_3.14:12
children.translated_text: And thus, what was previously stated — 'therefore, in the reflection on word and meaning, there is no state that is not <s>Śiva</s>' — there is no contradiction whatsoever between that and 'the arising of cognitions for him is the loss of the supreme nectar-essence.'

children.text: * nanu yadi pratyayodbhavo 'pyasya parāmṛtarasāpāyaḥ tatkatham uktaṃ śaktivargasya bhogyatāṃ gata ityāśaṅkāṃ pariharati || VSpkC_3.14:13]
children.translated_text: Objection: if the arising of cognitions is itself the loss of the supreme nectar-essence for him, then how was it said that he has become the object of enjoyment for the group of powers? He resolves this doubt:
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>]

children.text: svarūpāvaraṇe cāsya śaktayaḥ satatotthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the powers, constantly arisen, [serve] to conceal his own nature,

children.text: yataḥ śabdānuvedhena na vinā pratyayodbhavaḥ // VSpk_3.15 //
children.translated_text: because the arising of cognition does not [occur] without the permeation of word (<s>śabda</s>). (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.15)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* caḥ śaṅkāṃ dyotayan tatparihārarūpaṃ prameyāntaraṃ samuccinoti || VSpkC_3.15:1
children.translated_text: The word 'ca' (and), indicating the doubt, gathers another point of established meaning in the form of resolving it.

children.text: * asya paśoḥ svasya śivātmano rūpasyāvaraṇe bhittibhūtatvena prathamānasyāpi samyagaparāmarśane tannimittaṃ vyākhyātarūpāḥ śaktayaḥ satatam utthitāḥ yāvaddhi parāmṛtarasātmakasvasvarūpapratyabhijñānam asya na vṛttaṃ tāvad etāḥ svasvarūpāvaraṇāyodyacchantyeva || VSpkC_3.15:2
children.translated_text: For this bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), the powers are constantly arisen for the concealment of his own nature — his form as <s>Śiva</s> — serving as a wall [of concealment], even as it manifests; [that is,] for the thorough non-apprehension of that [nature] due to those [powers]. The powers of the described nature are constantly arisen — for as long as the recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) of one's own essential nature, which is of the nature of the supreme nectar-essence, has not occurred for him, until then these [powers] indeed strive to conceal his own essential nature.

children.text: * yato'sya yaḥ pratyayodbhavo vikalpakāvikalpakajñānaprasaraḥ sa śabdānuvedhena ahamidaṃ jānāmi ityādinā sūkṣmāntaḥśabdānurañjanena sthūlābhilāpasaṃsargeṇa ca vinā na bhavati iti tiraścām apyasāṃketikaḥ nirdeśaprakhyaḥ svātmani ca śironirdeśaprakhyo 'ntarabhyupagamarūpaḥ śabdanavimarśo 'styeva anyathā bālasya prathamasaṃketagrahaṇaṃ na ghaṭeta antarūhāpohātmakavimarśaśūnyatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because the arising of cognition for him — the stream of conceptual and non-conceptual knowledge — does not occur without the permeation of word (<s>śabda</s>) — without the coloring of subtle inner speech such as 'I know this' and without the association of gross verbal expression. Thus even for animals, there exists a non-conventional mode of indication, a word-reflective-awareness (<s>śabdana-vimarśa</s>) manifest in themselves, in the form of pointing with the head. Otherwise, the initial grasping of convention by a child would not be possible, due to the absence of the inner reflective awareness consisting of postulation and exclusion.

children.text: * sthūlaśabdānuvedhamayas tu vikalpaḥ sarvasya svānubhavasiddhaḥ || VSpkC_3.15:3
children.translated_text: But conceptual construction pervaded by gross verbal expression is established for everyone by one's own experience.

children.text: * ślokatrayoktam artham upasaṃharanniyataḥ prameyasya sāmānyaspandatattvādabhinnatāṃ prāguktām anubadhnan tatpratyabhijñānāpratyabhijñānamayau bandhamokṣau iti lakṣayati || VSpkC_3.15:4]
children.translated_text: Summarizing the meaning stated in the three verses, he ties together the previously stated non-difference of the knowable from the universal <s>spanda</s>-principle, and indicates that bondage and liberation consist in the non-recognition and recognition of that [identity].
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>]

children.text: seyaṃ kriyātmikā śaktiḥ śivasya paśuvartinī /
children.translated_text: This very power of <s>Śiva</s>, which is of the nature of activity (<s>kriyā</s>), residing in the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>),

children.text: bandhayitrī svamārgasthā jñātā siddhyupapādikā // VSpk_3.16 //
children.translated_text: is the binder [when] situated on its own path; [but] when known, it becomes the bestower of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment). (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.16)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* seti ślokatrayanirṇītatvāt iyamiti prameyaparyantena rūpeṇa sphurantī svasvabhāvarūpasya cidātmanaḥ śivasya sambandhinī spandatattvātmikā parābhaṭṭārikaiva viśvavaicitryāvasthitikāritvāt kriyāśaktiḥ prāṅnirṇītadṛśā śiva eva gṛhītapaśubhūmike vartamānā prāṇapuryaṣṭakarūpam amuṃ kartṛtātmanāhaṃtāvipruṣā prokṣitaṃ kurvāṇā tathārūpeṇāpratyabhijñāya svarūpāvārakatvād dhānādānādiparikleśahetutvācca bandhayitrī bhavati || VSpkC_3.16:1
children.translated_text: 'She' (<s>sā</s>) — since it has been ascertained by a triad of verses — 'this' (<s>iyam</s>) — appearing in the form extending as far as the knowable (<s>prameya</s>) — the <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action) that belongs to <s>Śiva</s>, whose nature is the self of consciousness (<s>cidātman</s>), whose form is his own essential nature — [she is] the supreme Goddess (<s>Parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>) herself, whose nature is the <s>spanda</s> reality, because of effecting the variegated states of the universe. [However,] when situated in one who has assumed the ground of the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) — as previously ascertained — taking on the form of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body), sprinkling [the limited self] with a drop of 'I'-consciousness (<s>ahaṃtā</s>) that is the nature of agency (<s>kartṛtā</s>), and [thereby] not being recognized in her true form, she becomes the binder — because she covers one's own essential nature and because she becomes the cause of the affliction of loss and gain and the like.

children.text: * yadā tu svasya śivātmano rūpasya yo mārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: But when the path to the recognition of one's own nature as <s>Śiva</s> —

children.text: * śaktyavasthāṃ praviṣṭasya nirvibhāgena bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: 'For one who has entered the state of [<s>Śiva</s>'s] power, contemplation is without division (<s>nirvibhāga</s>);

children.text: * tadāsau śivarūpī syācchaivī mukham ihocyate || VSpkC_3.16:2
children.translated_text: then one becomes of the form of <s>Śiva</s> — the face of <s>Śaivī</s> [power] is declared here.'

children.text: * iti śrīvijñānabhaṭṭārakoktanītyā prāptyupāyaḥ parāśaktistadātmatayāsau kriyāśaktirjñāyate yoginā yadā vā vikalpakāvikalpakaprasare 'pi śivasvarūpasya svātmano 'ṃśabhūtam evāśeṣavedyam anenekṣyate tadāsyāsau parānandamayīṃ parāṃ siddhim upapādayati || VSpkC_3.16:3]
children.translated_text: — according to the method stated by the revered <s>Vijñānabhaṭṭāraka</s>, the means of attainment is the supreme power (<s>Parā Śakti</s>); when [that <s>kriyāśakti</s>] is known by the <s>yogin</s> as being of the nature of that [<s>Parā Śakti</s>], or when by [this power] he perceives all that is knowable as nothing but a portion of his own self — whose nature is <s>Śiva</s> — even in the expansion of both conceptual and non-conceptual [awareness], then she bestows upon him the supreme <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), which is filled with supreme bliss (<s>parānanda</s>).
[<s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>]

children.text: tanmātrodayarūpeṇa mano'hambuddhivartinā /
children.translated_text: Confined by the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body), which operates through mind (<s>manas</s>), ego (<s>aham</s>), and intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), in the form of the arising of the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements),

children.text: puryaṣṭakena saṃruddhas tadutthaṃ pratyayodbhavam // VSpk_3.17 //
children.translated_text: he experiences enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) that arises from cognitions (<s>pratyaya</s>),

children.text: bhuṅkte paravaśo bhogaṃ tadbhāvātsaṃsaredataḥ /
children.translated_text: being subject to another's power (<s>paravaśa</s>). Due to the nature of that [<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>], he transmigrates. Therefore,

children.text: saṃsṛtipralayasyāsya kāraṇaṃ sampracakṣmahe // VSpk_3.18 //
children.translated_text: we shall declare the cause of the destruction of this <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.17–3.18)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* puryaṣṭakotthitaṃ bhogaṃ bhuṅkte || VSpkC_3.17-18:1
children.translated_text: He experiences the enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) arisen from the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body).

children.text: * yata eva pratyayeṣu sukhādipratyayodbhavaḥ ata evāsau pratyayodbhavāt paśuḥ paravaśaḥ śabdānuvedhakrameṇa pade pade brāhmyādidevībhir ākṣipyamāṇaḥ na tu suprabuddhavat svatantraḥ tasya puryaṣṭakasya bhāvādeva punaḥpunarudbodhitavicitravāsanaḥ saṃsaret tattadbhogocitabhogāyatanāni śarīrāṇyarjayitvā gṛhṇāti cotsṛjati ca || VSpkC_3.17-18:2
children.translated_text: Since in [various] cognitions there arises the experience of pleasure and the like, for that very reason this bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), being 'subject to another's power' — being seized at every step by the goddesses <s>Brāhmī</s> and the rest through the sequence of attachment to words — not being independent like the fully awakened one — transmigrates due to the very nature of that <s>puryaṣṭaka</s>, whose various latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) are repeatedly awakened; i.e., he acquires bodies as suitable receptacles of enjoyment for the respective types of experience, and he takes [them] on and discards [them].

children.text: * yataś caivam ato 'sya puryaṣṭakasaṃruddhasya yā saṃsṛtis tasyā yaḥ prakṛṣṭo layaḥ puryaṣṭakātmakamalocchedena vināśaḥ tasya kāraṇaṃ samyak sukhopāyaṃ pracakṣmahe samanantaram eva brūmaḥ tathā sampracakṣmahe prakaraṇe 'smin svayaṃ pratipāditavantaḥ || VSpkC_3.17-18:3
children.translated_text: And since this is so, therefore we 'declare' — i.e., we shall state immediately — the cause, i.e., the proper easy means, of the complete dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>) of the transmigration (<s>saṃsṛti</s>) of this one who is confined by the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> — [that is,] the destruction through the complete eradication of the impurity that constitutes the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s>. Similarly, 'we declare' [can mean] we ourselves have demonstrated [it] in this treatise.

children.text: * vartamānasāmīpye vartamānavad vā || VSpkC_3.17-18:4
children.translated_text: [The present tense is used] either because of proximity to the present, or as a present tense [used for] the future.

children.text: * iti vartamānaprayogaḥ || VSpkC_3.17-18:5
children.translated_text: Thus the use of the present tense [is explained].

children.text: * etat pratipādayan ādyasūtroktamarthaṃ nigamayati || VSpkC_3.17-18:6]
children.translated_text: By demonstrating this, he concludes the meaning stated in the first <s>sūtra</s>.
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: yadā tv ekatra saṃrūḍhas tadā tasya layodayau /
children.translated_text: But when one is firmly established in one [point], then, controlling the dissolution and arising of that [<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>],

children.text: niyacchan bhoktṛtām eti tataś cakreśvaro bhavet // VSpk_3.19 //
children.translated_text: one attains the status of experiencer (<s>bhoktṛtā</s>), and thereby becomes the lord of the circle [of powers] (<s>cakreśvara</s>). (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 3.19)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* yadā punarayamuktāḥ paratattvasamāveśopadeśayuktīḥ pariśīlayan ekatra pūrṇāhaṃtātmani spandatattve samyagavicalatvena rūḍhaḥ samāviṣṭas tanmayo bhavati tadā tasyeti pūrvasūtranirdiṣṭasya puryaṣṭakasya taddvāreṇaiva viśvasya nimīlanonmīlanasamāveśābhyāṃ layodayau niyacchan prathamasūtranirṇītadṛśā ekasmād eva śaṃkarātmanaḥ svabhāvāt saṃhāraṃ sargaṃ ca kurvan bhoktṛtām eti dharādiśivāntasamagrabhogyakavalanena paramapramātṛtāṃ satīm eva pratyabhijñānakrameṇāvalambeta || VSpkC_3.19:1
children.translated_text: But when this [<s>yogin</s>], practicing the instructions and reasonings of entry into the supreme reality (<s>paratattvasamāveśa</s>) as stated [above], is 'firmly established in one [point]' — i.e., properly and unwaveringly established, absorbed, and identified with the <s>spanda</s> reality, whose nature is complete 'I'-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhaṃtā</s>) — then, controlling the dissolution and arising of 'that,' i.e., the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> described in the preceding <s>sūtra</s> — and thereby of the entire universe through that very [<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>] — through the two types of absorption: <s>nimīlana</s> (inward-closing) and <s>unmīlana</s> (outward-opening) — performing dissolution and creation from one and the same essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) whose self is <s>Śaṃkara</s>, as ascertained in the first <s>sūtra</s> — 'one attains the status of experiencer' — i.e., one would take hold of, through the process of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>), the status of the supreme knowing subject (<s>paramapramātṛtā</s>), which already exists, through the devouring of the entirety of the enjoyable from <s>dharā</s> (earth) to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: * tataś ca prathamasūtranirṇītasya śakticakrasya svamarīcinicayasyeśvaro 'dhipatir bhavet || VSpkC_3.19:2
children.translated_text: And thereby one would become the lord (<s>īśvara</s>), the sovereign, of the circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>) — the assemblage of one's own rays (<s>svamarīcinicaya</s>) — as ascertained in the first <s>sūtra</s>.

children.text: * anenaiva ca dehena maheśvaratvam avāpnotyeveti yāvat || VSpkC_3.19:3
children.translated_text: And [the implication is that] one attains the state of <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord) with this very body.

children.text: * evaṃ copakramopasaṃhārayor mahārthasaṃpuṭīkāraṃ darśayan tatsāratayā samastaśāṃkaropaniṣanmūrdhanyatām asyāviṣkaroti śāstrasya śrīmān vasuguptācāryaḥ iti śivam || VSpkC_3.19:4]
children.translated_text: Thus, showing the enclosure of the great meaning (<s>mahārthasaṃpuṭīkāra</s>) between the opening and conclusion [of the work], the glorious master <s>Vasugupta</s> reveals the supremacy of this treatise among all the <s>Upaniṣads</s> of <s>Śaṃkara</s> (Śiva), as being their very essence. Thus, auspiciousness (<s>śivam</s>).
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: spandakārikā, caturtho niḥṣyandaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Spandakārikā</s>, Fourth Outflow (<s>Caturtho Niḥṣyandaḥ</s>)

children.text: agādhasaṃśayāmbhodhisamuttaraṇatāriṇīm /
children.translated_text: I revere that speech of the <s>Guru</s>, with its wonderful meanings and expressions,

children.text: vande vicitrārthapadāṃ citrāṃ tāṃ gurubhāratīm // VSpk_4.1 //
children.translated_text: which is the boat for crossing the fathomless ocean of doubt. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 4.1)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>
* tāmasāmānyāṃ bhagavatīṃ guruṃ śaivī mukham ihocyate iti sthityā śivadhāmaprāptihetutvād ācāryarūpām || VSpkC_4.1:1
children.translated_text: 'That' universal, blessed [speech]; 'of the <s>Guru</s>' — in the form of the preceptor (<s>ācārya</s>), because it is the cause of attaining the abode of <s>Śiva</s>, according to the established [teaching]: 'the face of <s>Śaivī</s> [power] is declared here.'

children.text: * atha ca guruṃ paśyantyādikroḍīkārāt mahatīṃ bhāratīṃ parāṃ vācam tathā guror ācāryasya sambandhinīm upadeṣṭrīṃ giraṃ citrāṃ lokottaracamatkārarūpāṃ vande sarvotkṛṣṭatvena samāviśāmi || VSpkC_4.1:2
children.translated_text: Moreover, 'the <s>Guru</s>' — i.e., great, because of embracing <s>Paśyantī</s> and the other [levels of speech] — 'speech' (<s>bhāratī</s>), i.e., the supreme word (<s>Parā Vāc</s>); also 'of the <s>Guru</s>' — i.e., the instructing voice belonging to the preceptor; 'wonderful' (<s>citrā</s>) — of the form of extraordinary wonder; 'I revere' — I enter into [it] as the most exalted of all.

children.text: * atha ca sarvāvasthāsu sphuradrūpatvād abhivadantīm udyantṛtāprayatnenābhivādaye svarūpavimarśaniṣṭhāṃ tāṃ samāveṣṭuṃ saṃmukhīkaromi || VSpkC_4.1:3
children.translated_text: Moreover, [this speech] which addresses [one] in all states because of its nature as that which pulsates; 'I salute' — I salute with the effort of the rising (<s>udyantṛtā-prayatna</s>); [that speech] which is established in the reflective awareness of one's own essential nature — 'that' — I make it face me, i.e., I [make it accessible] in order to be absorbed [in it].

children.text: * kīdṛśīm agādho duruttaro yaḥ saṃśayaḥ pūrṇāhaṃtāniścayābhāvātmā vicitraḥ śaṅkākalaṅkaḥ sa eva vitatatvenāmbhodhis tasya samyaguttaraṇe yā tāriṇī naur iva tām ityubhayatrāpi yojyam /
children.translated_text: Of what kind? 'Fathomless' (<s>agādha</s>) — difficult to cross — is the doubt, whose nature is the absence of certainty regarding complete 'I'-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhaṃtā</s>); that doubt itself is multifarious, a stain of suspicion; it is, in its extension, an ocean — of the complete crossing of that [ocean], she who is the boat (<s>tāriṇī</s>) — 'that' should be connected in both senses.

children.text: * tathā vicitrārthāni nānācamatkāraprayojanāni padāni viśrāntayo yasyāṃ parasyāṃ vāci tāṃ vicitrāṇi ramyaracanānupraviṣṭāni arthapadāni vācyavācakāni yasyāṃ guruvāci tām || VSpkC_4.1:4
children.translated_text: Similarly, 'with wonderful meanings' — whose resting places (<s>pada</s>) have various purposes, serving manifold wonders; 'of the <s>Guru</s>'s speech' — in the supreme word (<s>Parā Vāc</s>). [Or:] 'wonderful' — with beautiful compositions interwoven; 'meaning-words' (<s>arthapadāni</s>) — [pairs of] designated and designator — in the speech of the <s>Guru</s>.

children.text: * prasiddhaprabhāvasvanāmodīraṇāt sambhāvanāpratyayenārthinaḥ pravartayan gūhanīyatayā mahāphalatām asya śāstrasya nirūpayati śāstrakāraḥ || VSpkC_4.1:5]
children.translated_text: By emitting the sound of his well-known splendor, causing the aspirant to proceed through a cognition of esteem — [thereby] the author of the treatise establishes the great fruitfulness of this scripture through [its quality of] being worthy of concealment.
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]

children.text: labdhvāpyalabhyam etajjñānadhanaṃ hṛdguhāntakṛtanihiteḥ /
children.translated_text: Having obtained this wealth of knowledge, though unobtainable, by one who has deposited [it] within the cave of the heart,

children.text: vasuguptavacchivāya hi bhavati sadā sarvalokasya // VSpk_4.2 //
children.translated_text: it becomes, like [it did for] <s>Vasugupta</s>, always for the welfare (<s>śiva</s>) of the entire world. (<s>Spandakārikā</s> 4.2)

children.text: * [<Spandakārikānirṇaya>

* etacchāstroktam etajjñānam eva puruṣārthaprāptihetutvād dhanam alabhyam api duṣprāpam api labdhvā śaṃkarasvapnopadeśasāraṃ śilātalād avāpya prakāśavimarśātmakaṃ hṛdayam eva viśvāntaḥpraveśāvakāśapradatvād guhā tasyām antena niścayena kṛtā nihitiḥ sthāpanā yena arthāttasyaiva jñānadhanasya tasya svāminaḥ śrīvasuguptābhidhānasya guroryathaiva tacchivāya jātaṃ tadvadadhikāriniyamasaṃkocābhāvāt sarvalokasyāpi hṛdguhāntakṛtanihiter yatnād asāmayikāt gopayataḥ dṛḍhapratipattyā ca svātmīkurvataḥ sadā śivāya bhavati nityaśaṃkarātmakasvasvabhāvasamāveśalābhāya sampadyata iti śivam || VSpkC_4.2:1
children.translated_text: Having obtained 'this knowledge' — the knowledge taught in this scripture — which is 'wealth' because it is the cause of attaining the supreme goal of human life; 'unobtainable' — difficult to obtain — having obtained [it], i.e., having recovered the essence of <s>Śaṃkara</s>'s instruction in a dream, from the stone slab; [this knowledge] whose nature is light and reflective awareness (<s>prakāśa-vimarśa</s>); 'the heart' — because it provides scope for the entry of the entire universe within — is 'the cave'; 'within that' — with certainty — the 'depositing,' i.e., establishment, has been made; the meaning is: of this very wealth of knowledge. Just as it became for the welfare of <s>Śiva</s> for its owner, the <s>Guru</s> named <s>Vasugupta</s>, so too — since there is no restriction limiting [it] to qualified recipients — it becomes always for the welfare of the entire world as well, for one who deposits [it] within the cave of the heart, i.e., for one who guards [it] with assiduous effort, not merely by convention, and who firmly makes it one's own — [such a person attains] the welfare of <s>Śiva</s>, i.e., [it] conduces to the attainment of absorption in one's own essential nature as eternally <s>Śaṃkara</s>. Thus, auspiciousness (<s>śivam</s>).

children.text: * yadyapyasmin vivṛtigaṇanā vidyate naiva śāstre lokaścāyaṃ yadapi matimān bhūyasottānavṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Although in this scripture there is indeed no enumeration of commentaries, and although this world, however intelligent, mostly [prefers] surface-level commentary,

children.text: * jānantyete tadapi kuśalāste 'smadukter viśeṣaṃ kecit sāragrahaṇanipuṇāś cetanārājahaṃsāḥ || VSpkC_4.2:2
children.translated_text: nonetheless, those who are skilled will recognize the distinction of our exposition — certain ones who are adept at grasping the essence, [who are like] royal swans among conscious beings.

children.text: * anantāparaṭīkākṛnmadhye sthitim amṛṣyatā /
children.translated_text: Unable to tolerate remaining amidst the endless [mass] of other commentators,

children.text: * vivṛtaṃ spandaśāstraṃ no guruṇā no mayāsya tu || VSpkC_4.2:3
children.translated_text: the <s>Spanda</s> scripture was commented upon — not by our <s>Guru</s>, not by me, but —

children.text: * viśeṣaleśaḥ saṃdohe darśitaḥ pūrvamadya tu /
children.translated_text: a slight trace of its distinction was shown previously in the collection [of commentaries]; but now,

children.text: * rudraśaktisamāveśaśālinaḥ śivarūpiṇaḥ || VSpkC_4.2:4
children.translated_text: for [the student] <s>Śūranāman</s>, who is of the form of <s>Śiva</s>, possessed of absorption in the power of <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: * śūranāmnaḥ svaśiṣyasya prārthanātirasena tat /
children.translated_text: at the urging of his request,

children.text: * nirṇītaṃ kṣemarājena sphārānnijaguror guroḥ || VSpkC_4.2:5
children.translated_text: it has been ascertained (nirṇīta) by <s>Kṣemarāja</s>, through the expansion [of grace] from his own <s>Guru</s>'s <s>Guru</s>.

children.text: * yeṣāṃ no dhiṣaṇopadeśaviśadā saddaiśikairdarśitā śrīmacchāmbhavaśāsanopaniṣadā yeṣāṃ na bhagno bhramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those for whom the <s>Upaniṣad</s> of the glorious <s>Śāmbhava</s> teaching — made clear by the instruction and intellect of true preceptors — has not dispelled delusion,

children.text: * ye nāsvāditapūrviṇo mṛdudhiyaḥ śrīpratyabhijñāmṛtaṃ tenātrādhikṛtāḥ paraiḥ punar idaṃ pūrṇāśayaiś carvyatām || VSpkC_4.2:6
children.translated_text: who are of tender intellect and have not previously tasted the nectar of the glorious <s>Pratyabhijñā</s> — they are not qualified here. But let those of full understanding chew upon this.

children.text: * śivādikṣityanto vitatavitato yo 'dhvavibhavaḥ sphurannānāsargasthitilayadaśācitritatanuḥ /
children.translated_text: The magnificence of the cosmic path (<s>adhvan</s>), extending from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth, spread out far and wide, its body made wondrous by the manifold states of creation, maintenance, and dissolution —

children.text: * iyadviśvaṃ yasya prasarakaṇikāsau vijayate paraḥ saṃvitspando lasadasamasaukhyāyatanabhūḥ || VSpkC_4.2:7]
children.translated_text: this entire universe is [but] a particle of the expansion of that [reality]: victorious is the supreme <s>Saṃvit-Spanda</s> (vibration of consciousness), the ground that is the abode of radiant, incomparable bliss.
[From the <s>Spandakārikānirṇaya</s>:]
